check_stacking

Groups laid out against the stacking rule, both ways, and lines past the width, read a byte at a time by the Roc library's Groups and Stacking, with write=1 adding and taking trailing commas for roc fmt until a pass changes nothing.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.exists!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.mkdir!, Shale.print!, Shale.re_find!, Shale.read!, Shale.real!, Shale.remove_tree!, Shale.roc_tree!, Shale.run!, Shale.write!.
Roc: 1,203 lines in 5 files. Shale original: 610 lines, plus 681 lines in the 6 libraries it loads, which other recipes share.

Roc

It also imports Bytes, Finding, Groups, Headers, Stacking, Text, Tree from the shared Roc library.

cookbook/roc/check_stacking/check_stacking.roc, 157 lines

## check_stacking, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md): the
## groups in .roc files laid out against the stacking rule and the lines
## past the width, found and, with `write=1`, laid out by the rule. Its
## launcher, cookbook/roc/check_stacking.shale, is how it is run, and its
## header says the rule, the findings and the rewrite. check_goldens.shale,
## beside this, holds its output on the plants to its goldens, line for line.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/check_stacking.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/check_stacking.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc write=1
##   shale cookbook:roc/check_stacking.shale self_test=1
##
## The arguments: `glob` (`**/*.roc`), `skip` (files the glob finds to leave
## out, comma-separated), `width` (100), `tokens` (6), `dictated` (a table of
## functions whose arguments something outside the file dictates), `house`
## (`house=0` leaves out every finding, all of them house style), `write`
## (`write=1` rewrites the files) and `self_test` (`self_test=1` checks the
## plants and rewrites copies of them).
##
## This root reads the arguments, globs the files, rewrites them when asked
## (Rewrite) and prints the findings (Report, by Annotations) and the
## verdict; SelfTest is the self-test. Groups, Stacking, Headers, Finding
## and Text are the cookbook's Roc library, cookbook/roc/lib/.
## budget: steps=900000000 read_bytes=1000000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 programs=100 roc_cpu_ms=120000
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import lib.Finding
import lib.Stacking
import Report
import Rewrite
import SelfTest

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	self_test = Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1"
	pattern = if self_test {
		"${SelfTest.plants}/*.roc"
	} else {
		Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc")
	}
	skip = Shale.arg!("skip", "")
	dictated = if self_test {
		"${SelfTest.plants}/dictated.txt"
	} else {
		Shale.arg!("dictated", "")
	}
	width = integer_of!("width", Shale.arg!("width", "100"))
	write = Shale.arg!("write", "") == "1"
	tokens = integer_of!("tokens", Shale.arg!("tokens", Stacking.stack_tokens.to_str()))
	settings = { rule: { tokens, width }, dictated }
	if self_test {
		SelfTest.run!(chosen_files!(pattern, skip), settings)
	} else if write {
		refuse_house_rewrite!({})
		# Stop before any change if the tree's Roc is missing.
		roc = Rewrite.roc_bin!(Bool.False)
		paths = chosen_files!(pattern, skip)
		_first = Rewrite.trailing_commas!(paths, { rule: settings.rule, roc })
		judged = Report.findings_in!(paths, settings)
		left = judged.found.map(Finding.line_of)
		print_findings!("${left.len().to_str()} left, each a line the rewrite can't reach", left)
		SelfTest.fail_if_refused!(judged.refused)
	} else {
		paths = chosen_files!(pattern, skip)
		judged = Report.findings_in!(paths, settings)
		house_is_off = read_house_is_off!({})
		kept = if house_is_off {
			[]
		} else {
			judged.found
		}
		count_of = |check| kept.count_if(|finding| finding.check == check).to_str()
		counts = "${count_of("stack")} to stack, ${count_of("unstack")} to unstack, ${count_of("long")} long, ${count_of("wide string")} wide string"
		note = if house_is_off {
			"; left out as house style: stack, unstack, long, wide string"
		} else {
			""
		}
		summary = "${kept.len().to_str()} findings in ${paths.len().to_str()} files: ${counts}${note}"
		print_findings!(summary, kept.map(Finding.line_of))
		SelfTest.fail_if_refused!(judged.refused)
	}
}

## The whole number an argument gives; another value stops the run, as
## Shale's `arg` does for an integer default. (Each `Shale.arg!` names its
## argument as a literal, so the launcher's check of the values finds it.)
integer_of! : Str, Str => U64
integer_of! = |name, given|
	match I64.from_str(given) {
		Ok(value) if value >= 0 => value.to_u64_wrap()
		Ok(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("check_stacking: ${name}=${given} is below 0")
			0
		}
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("`arg`: ${name}=${given} is not an integer, and its default is one")
			0
		}
	}

## The files the glob finds, less the ones `skip` names. A name in `skip`
## that the glob doesn't find stops the run, so a renamed file can't go
## unchecked.
chosen_files! : Str, Str => List(Str)
chosen_files! = |pattern, skip| {
	found = Shale.glob!(pattern)
	if skip == "" {
		return found
	}
	skipped = skip.split_on(",")
	for name in skipped {
		if !(found.contains(name)) {
			Shale.fail!("check_stacking: skip names ${name}, which the glob doesn't find")
		}
	}
	found.drop_if(|path| skipped.contains(path))
}

## Whether `house=0` leaves the house style out (cookbook/roc/house.shale):
## here that is every finding.
read_house_is_off! : {} => Bool
read_house_is_off! = |{}| {
	house = Shale.arg!("house", "1")
	number = match I64.from_str(house) {
		Ok(value) => value
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("`arg`: house=${house} is not an integer, and its default is one")
			1
		}
	}
	if number != 0 and number != 1 {
		Shale.fail!("house must be 1 (the default) or 0, not ${number.to_str()}")
	}
	number == 0
}

## A rewrite applies our house style, so `house=0` refuses one.
refuse_house_rewrite! : {} => {}
refuse_house_rewrite! = |{}| {
	if read_house_is_off!({}) {
		Shale.fail!("check_stacking: write=1 applies our house style, so it refuses house=0")
	}
}

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale):
## the first copy survives a cut output, and a gate reads the last line.
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, finding_lines| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(finding_lines.is_empty()) {
		for line in finding_lines {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

cookbook/roc/check_stacking/Report.roc, 392 lines

## Every finding in a run's files, in the files' order and each file's line
## order, as the Shale original found them: a group on one line that should
## stack, a function type's bare arguments, a stacked group that should sit
## on one line, and a line wider than the width with nothing to stack, which
## is `wide string` when its strings' text is what makes it wide (by Roc's
## parser) and `long` otherwise. The names a file's header dictates, and
## those the `dictated` table names, are no finding for their arguments.
import pf.Shale
import lib.Bytes
import Annotations
import lib.Finding
import lib.Groups
import lib.Headers
import lib.Stacking
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

Report := [].{

	## What a run judges by: the stacking rule, and the path of the
	## `dictated` table (`""` for none).
	Settings : { rule : Stacking.Rule, dictated : Str }

	## A run's findings, and why each file roc-ast refused was refused.
	Judged : { found : List(Finding), refused : List(Str) }

	## Every finding in the files.
	findings_in! : List(Str), Report.Settings => Report.Judged
	findings_in! = |paths, settings| {
		var $texts = Dict.empty()
		for path in paths {
			$texts = $texts.insert(path, Report.read_text!(path))
		}
		texts = $texts
		strings = string_columns_in!(paths, { texts, width: settings.rule.width })
		headed = dictated_names_in!(paths, texts)
		dictated = with_dictated_table!(headed.names, { paths, table: settings.dictated })
		var $found = []
		for path in paths {
			source_lines = (texts.get(path) ?? "").split_on("\n")
			file = {
				path,
				source_lines,
				string_columns: strings.columns.get(path) ?? Dict.empty(),
				dictated: dictated.get(path) ?? [],
				rule: settings.rule,
			}
			match file_findings(file) {
				Ok(found) => {
					$found = $found.concat(found)
				}
				Err(NoComma(line)) => Shale.fail!("groups: line ${line.to_str()} does not end in its group's trailing comma")
			}
		}
		var $refused = []
		for refusal in strings.refused.concat(headed.refused) {
			if !($refused.contains(refusal)) {
				$refused = $refused.append(refusal)
			}
		}
		{ found: $found, refused: $refused }
	}

	## Why roc-ast refused a file, beginning with its path
	## (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale's `parse_roc_files`).
	refusal_of : Str, Str -> Str
	refusal_of = |path, err|
		if err.starts_with(path) {
			err
		} else {
			"${path}: ${err}"
		}

	## A file's text; a file gone since the glob stops the run.
	read_text! : Str => Str
	read_text! = |path|
		match Shale.read!(path) {
			Found(text) => text
			Missing => {
				Shale.fail!("check_stacking: no file ${path}")
				""
			}
		}
}

## A file to judge: its path, its lines, the columns its strings' text takes
## up by line number, the names whose arguments something else dictates, and
## the rule.
FileToJudge : {
	path : Str,
	source_lines : List(Str),
	string_columns : Dict(U64, U64),
	dictated : List(Str),
	rule : Stacking.Rule,
}

## What a file's scan knows so far: the function whose annotation ended on
## the line before and was a finding for its arguments (`""` for none),
## whose lambda's arguments are not reported again, and the last line of the
## annotation read last.
Annotated : { name : Str, end : U64 }

## The findings in one file, line by line, then the groups to unstack.
file_findings : FileToJudge -> Try(List(Finding), [NoComma(U64)])
file_findings = |file| {
	rule = file.rule
	reachable = Stacking.without_targets_section(file.source_lines)
	var $found = []
	var $annotated = { name: "", end: 0 }
	$number : U64
	var $number = 0
	for text in file.source_lines {
		$number = $number + 1
		number = $number
		on_line = line_findings(
			file,
			{
				number,
				text,
				reachable: reachable.get(number - 1) ?? "",
				annotated: $annotated,
			},
		)
		$annotated = on_line.annotated
		$found = $found.concat(on_line.found)
	}
	for unstacked in Stacking.groups_to_unstack(file.source_lines, rule)? {
		joined = Stacking.group_on_one_line(file.source_lines, unstacked.group) ?? ""
		$found = $found.append({
			path: file.path,
			line: unstacked.group.line,
			check: "unstack",
			what: "${unstacked.group.tokens.to_str()} tokens in ${Annotations.shortened(Text.trim(joined))}",
		})
	}
	Ok($found)
}

## A line to judge: its number, its text, its text with a `targets:` section
## blanked, and what the scan knew of the annotation before it.
LineToJudge : {
	number : U64,
	text : Str,
	reachable : Str,
	annotated : Annotated,
}

## The findings on one line, and what the scan knows after it.
line_findings : FileToJudge, LineToJudge -> { found : List(Finding), annotated : Annotated }
line_findings = |file, at| {
	rule = file.rule
	bytes = at.text.to_utf8()
	place = { path: file.path, line: at.number }
	before = at.annotated
	follows_annotation = before.name != "" and at.number == before.end + 1
	var $skip_lambda = follows_annotation and Text.trim(at.text).starts_with("${before.name} = |")
	var $annotated = if at.number > before.end {
		{ ..before, name: "" }
	} else {
		before
	}
	data_line = Stacking.is_data_line(at.reachable, rule.width)
	var $found = []
	for group in Groups.groups_on_line(at.reachable).sort_with(by_opening) {
		inner = Str.from_utf8_lossy(Bytes.span(bytes, group.open + 1, group.close - 1))
		whole = Str.from_utf8_lossy(Bytes.span(bytes, group.open, group.close))
		opening = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, group.open)
		if opening == '{' {
			for field in Annotations.record_field_functions(inner) {
				if field.items >= 3 and !(file.dictated.contains(field.name)) {
					arguments = {
						items: field.items,
						shown: Annotations.shortened(field.text),
						text: field.text,
					}
					$found = $found.append(Annotations.function_type_finding(place, arguments))
				}
			}
		}
		if group.items >= 3 and group.fn_type {
			text = Text.before_first(Text.before_first(inner, "->"), "=>")
			arguments = {
				items: group.items,
				shown: Annotations.shortened(whole),
				text,
			}
			$found = $found.append(Annotations.function_type_finding(place, arguments))
		} else if $skip_lambda and opening == '|' {
			$skip_lambda = Bool.False
		} else if !(data_line) {
			are_flags = group.items >= 3 and !(group.trailing) and Annotations.are_all_flags(inner)
			if are_flags or Stacking.should_stack({ line: at.text, group }, rule) {
				advice = if are_flags {
					Annotations.flag_advice
				} else {
					""
				}
				what = "${group.tokens.to_str()} tokens in ${Annotations.shortened(whole)}${advice}"
				$found = $found.append({
					path: file.path,
					line: at.number,
					check: "stack",
					what,
				})
			}
		}
	}
	# A line inside a wrapped annotation starts none.
	if at.number > $annotated.end {
		match Annotations.annotation_arguments(file.source_lines, at.number) {
			Ok(annotation) => {
				$annotated = { ..$annotated, end: annotation.last }
				if annotation.items >= 3 {
					$annotated = { ..$annotated, name: annotation.name }
					if !(file.dictated.contains(annotation.name)) {
						arguments = {
							items: annotation.items,
							shown: annotation.shown,
							text: annotation.text,
						}
						$found = $found.append(Annotations.function_type_finding(place, arguments))
					}
				}
			}
			Err(_) => {}
		}
	}
	if $found.is_empty() and Bytes.width_of(bytes) > rule.width {
		$found = $found.append(wide_line_finding(file, at))
	}
	{ found: $found, annotated: $annotated }
}

## The finding for a line wider than the width with nothing else found on it.
wide_line_finding : FileToJudge, LineToJudge -> Finding
wide_line_finding = |file, at| {
	rule = file.rule
	width = Bytes.line_width(at.text)
	strings = file.string_columns.get(at.number) ?? 0
	without_strings = width.to_i64_wrap() - strings.to_i64_wrap()
	if without_strings <= rule.width.to_i64_wrap() {
		what = "${width.to_str()} columns, ${without_strings.to_str()} without its strings"
		{
			path: file.path,
			line: at.number,
			check: "wide string",
			what,
		}
	} else {
		why = if Text.trim(at.text).starts_with("#") {
			"a comment"
		} else if Stacking.group_to_stack(at.reachable, rule).is_ok() {
			"a group to stack"
		} else {
			"nothing to stack"
		}
		{
			path: file.path,
			line: at.number,
			check: "long",
			what: "${width.to_str()} columns, ${why}",
		}
	}
}

## The columns that strings' text takes up in the files, by Roc's parser,
## by path and line number, and why each file roc-ast refused was refused.
## Only a file with a line wider than the width is parsed, so a tree of short
## lines never needs roc-ast.
string_columns_in! : List(Str),
{ texts : Dict(Str, Str), width : U64 } => {
	columns : Dict(Str, Dict(U64, U64)),
	refused : List(Str),
}
string_columns_in! = |paths, given| {
	wide_paths = paths.keep_if(
		|path| {
			text = given.texts.get(path) ?? ""
			Text.lines(text).any(|line| Bytes.line_width(line) > given.width)
		},
	)
	var $columns = Dict.empty()
	var $refused = []
	if !(wide_paths.is_empty()) {
		for file in Shale.roc_tree!(wide_paths) {
			if file.err == "" {
				source_lines = (given.texts.get(file.path) ?? "").split_on("\n")
				match Stacking.string_columns_on_lines(file.nodes, source_lines) {
					Ok(by_line) => {
						$columns = $columns.insert(file.path, by_line)
					}
					Err(CrossesLine(line)) => Shale.fail!("check_stacking: ${file.path}: line ${line.to_str()}: a run of string text crosses a line")
				}
			} else {
				$refused = $refused.append(Report.refusal_of(file.path, file.err))
			}
		}
	}
	{ columns: $columns, refused: $refused }
}

## The names the headers of the files dictate, by path, and why each file
## roc-ast refused was refused. Only an app's or a platform's file is parsed,
## so a tree of modules needs no roc-ast for this.
dictated_names_in! : List(Str),
Dict(Str, Str) => {
	names : Dict(Str, List(Str)),
	refused : List(Str),
}
dictated_names_in! = |paths, texts| {
	headed = paths.keep_if(
		|path| {
			word = Headers.header_word(texts.get(path) ?? "")
			word == "app" or word == "platform"
		},
	)
	var $names = Dict.empty()
	var $refused = []
	if !(headed.is_empty()) {
		for file in Shale.roc_tree!(headed) {
			if file.err == "" {
				nodes : List(Tree.Node)
				nodes = file.nodes
				$names = $names.insert(file.path, Headers.header_names(nodes).dictated)
			} else {
				$refused = $refused.append(Report.refusal_of(file.path, file.err))
			}
		}
	}
	{ names: $names, refused: $refused }
}

## The names the `dictated` table adds. Each line of the table is a file's
## path, a function's name, and after ` -- ` who dictates its arguments. The
## path names the file the glob finds with that path or ending `/` and that
## path, so the self-test's copies in scratch are found too. A line whose
## file the glob doesn't find, whose function has no annotation there, or
## that gives no reason stops the run, so the table can't go stale.
with_dictated_table! : Dict(Str, List(Str)),
{
	paths : List(Str),
	table : Str,
} => Dict(Str, List(Str))
with_dictated_table! = |names, given| {
	if given.table == "" {
		return names
	}
	var $names = names
	for line in Text.lines(Report.read_text!(given.table)) {
		trimmed = Text.trim(line)
		if trimmed != "" and !(trimmed.starts_with("#")) {
			groups = match Shale.re_find!(line, "^(\\S+) ([a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!?) -- \\S") {
				Found(found) => found.groups
				NoMatch => []
			}
			(wanted_path, name) = match groups {
				[path_given, name_given, ..] => (path_given, name_given)
				_ => {
					Shale.fail!("check_stacking: ${given.table} has a line that is not `path name -- reason`: ${line}")
					("", "")
				}
			}
			is_named = |path| path == wanted_path or path.ends_with("/${wanted_path}")
			found = given.paths.keep_if(is_named).last()
			match found {
				Err(_) => Shale.fail!("check_stacking: ${given.table} names ${wanted_path}, which the glob doesn't find")
				Ok(path) => {
					opening = "${name} :"
					path_lines = Text.lines(Report.read_text!(path))
					annotated = path_lines.any(|text| Text.trim(text).starts_with(opening))
					if !(annotated) {
						Shale.fail!("check_stacking: ${given.table} names ${name}, which has no annotation in ${path}")
					}
					here = $names.get(path) ?? []
					$names = $names.insert(path, here.append(name))
				}
			}
		}
	}
	$names
}

## Two groups of a line in the order of their opening brackets.
by_opening : Groups.Group, Groups.Group -> [Before, Same, After]
by_opening = |first, second|
	if first.open < second.open {
		Before
	} else if first.open > second.open {
		After
	} else {
		Same
	}

cookbook/roc/check_stacking/Rewrite.roc, 157 lines

## `write=1`: the files rewritten pass after pass until a pass changes
## nothing. A pass takes the trailing comma from each group that should
## unstack and gives one to each line's group that should stack, and `roc
## fmt` lays out the result: it stacks a group with a trailing comma and
## joins a group without one. The Roc is the tree's own
## (cookbook/roc/pinned.shale), run by its OS path.
import pf.Shale
import Report
import lib.Stacking
import lib.Text

Rewrite := [].{

	## Rewrites the files until a pass changes nothing, printing each pass,
	## and answers how many groups the first pass changed. Twelve passes
	## that still change something stop the run.
	trailing_commas! : List(Str), { rule : Stacking.Rule, roc : Str } => U64
	trailing_commas! = |paths, given| {
		$first_pass_count : U64
		var $first_pass_count = 0
		$pass : U64
		var $pass = 1
		$changed : U64
		var $changed = 1
		var $touched = []
		while $changed > 0 and $pass <= max_passes {
			$changed = 0
			$touched = []
			for path in paths {
				n = rewrite_file!(path, given.rule)
				if n > 0 {
					$touched = $touched.append(path)
					$changed = $changed + n
				}
			}
			Shale.print!("pass ${$pass.to_str()}: ${$changed.to_str()} groups rewritten, in ${$touched.len().to_str()} files")
			if $pass == 1 {
				$first_pass_count = $changed
			}
			if !($touched.is_empty()) {
				result = Rewrite.format!($touched, given.roc)
				if result.code != 0 {
					Shale.print!(result.out)
					Shale.fail!("roc fmt failed")
				}
			}
			$pass = $pass + 1
		}
		if $changed > 0 {
			Shale.fail!(
				"check_stacking: still changing after ${max_passes.to_str()} passes: ${Str.join_with($touched, ", ")}",
			)
		}
		$first_pass_count
	}

	## `roc fmt` run on the files; its code is not 0 when a file does not
	## parse.
	format! : List(Str), Str => { code : I64, out : Str }
	format! = |paths, roc| {
		var $argv = [roc, "fmt"]
		for path in paths {
			$argv = $argv.append(Shale.real!(path))
		}
		Shale.run!({
			argv: $argv,
			keep: Tail(20),
			timeout_ms: 120000,
			want: "",
		})
	}

	## The OS path of the Roc to rewrite with: in a self-test the pin every
	## recipe's self-test runs (pinned.shale's `SELF_TEST_PIN`, read there),
	## else the one the `roc-version` where the run starts names.
	roc_bin! : Bool => Str
	roc_bin! = |self_test| {
		pin = if self_test {
			self_test_pin!({})
		} else {
			if !(Shale.exists!("roc-version")) {
				Shale.fail!("check_stacking: no roc-version where the run starts: run it from the repository's root, whose roc-version pins its Roc")
			}
			Text.trim(Report.read_text!("roc-version"))
		}
		roc = "tools:roc-${pin}/roc"
		if !(Shale.exists!(roc)) {
			Shale.fail!("check_stacking: no ${roc}: install Roc ${pin} into ~/tools/roc-${pin}/ (roc-apps's toolchain release carries it)")
		}
		Shale.real!(roc)
	}
}

## The most passes a rewrite makes.
max_passes : U64
max_passes = 12

## One pass over one file: the groups that should unstack lose their trailing
## commas, then each line's group that should stack gets one; the file is
## written when any changed, and the answer is how many did.
rewrite_file! : Str, Stacking.Rule => U64
rewrite_file! = |path, rule| {
	source_lines = Report.read_text!(path).split_on("\n")
	unstacked = match Stacking.groups_to_unstack(source_lines, rule) {
		Ok(found) => found
		Err(NoComma(line)) => {
			Shale.fail!("groups: line ${line.to_str()} does not end in its group's trailing comma")
			[]
		}
	}
	unstacked_lines = Stacking.without_trailing_commas(source_lines, unstacked)
	reachable = Stacking.without_targets_section(unstacked_lines)
	var $lines = unstacked_lines
	$n : U64
	var $n = unstacked.len()
	$index : U64
	var $index = 0
	for text in unstacked_lines {
		if !(Text.trim(text).starts_with("#")) {
			match Stacking.group_to_stack(reachable.get($index) ?? "", rule) {
				Ok(group) => {
					$lines = $lines.set(
						$index,
						Stacking.with_trailing_comma({ line: text, group }),
					) ?? crash "check_stacking: a line past the file's end"
					$n = $n + 1
				}
				Err(_) => {}
			}
		}
		$index = $index + 1
	}
	if $n > 0 {
		Shale.write!(path, Str.join_with($lines, "\n"))
	}
	$n
}

## pinned.shale's `SELF_TEST_PIN`, the one home of the self-tests' Roc.
self_test_pin! : {} => Str
self_test_pin! = |{}| {
	pinned = "cookbook:roc/pinned.shale"
	groups = match Shale.re_find!(
		Report.read_text!(pinned),
		"\nconst SELF_TEST_PIN = \"([^\"]+)\"",
	) {
		Found(found) => found.groups
		NoMatch => []
	}
	match groups {
		[pin, ..] => pin
		[] => {
			Shale.fail!("check_stacking: no SELF_TEST_PIN in ${pinned}")
			""
		}
	}
}

cookbook/roc/check_stacking/SelfTest.roc, 193 lines

## The recipe's self-test, the Shale original's: each plant in
## cookbook/roc/plants/check_stacking/ must give a finding of the kind its
## name starts with (`long`, `wide`, `unstack`, or else `stack`), a `long`
## plant no `wide string` and a `wide` plant no `long`, and a `clean*.roc`
## plant none. A plant line ending `# findings N` must give exactly N
## findings, and with `advice W` after it each of them must contain the word
## W. Then the plants are copied to `scratch:stack/` and rewritten there with
## the self-tests' Roc: the rewrite must end, a second rewrite must change
## nothing, every file must still parse, and a plant with a `.want` file must
## come out as it.
import pf.Shale
import Report
import Rewrite
import lib.Text

SelfTest := [].{

	## The plants, whose `*.roc` a self-test checks.
	plants : Str
	plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_stacking"

	## The self-test of the plants, judged by `settings`.
	run! : List(Str), Report.Settings => {}
	run! = |paths, settings| {
		judged = Report.findings_in!(paths, settings)
		fail_if_refused!(judged.refused)
		marks_wrong = check_marks!(paths, judged)
		kinds_wrong = check_kinds!(paths, judged)
		wrong = marks_wrong + kinds_wrong
		if wrong > 0 {
			Shale.fail!("${wrong.to_str()} plants wrong")
		}
		if Shale.exists!(scratch) {
			Shale.remove_tree!(scratch)
		}
		Shale.mkdir!(scratch)
		copies = paths.map(copy_of)
		for path in paths {
			Shale.write!(copy_of(path), Report.read_text!(path))
		}
		roc = Rewrite.roc_bin!(Bool.True)
		given = { rule: settings.rule, roc }
		_first = Rewrite.trailing_commas!(copies, given)
		again = Rewrite.trailing_commas!(copies, given)
		if again > 0 {
			Shale.fail!("check_stacking: a second rewrite changed ${again.to_str()} more groups")
		}
		formatted = Rewrite.format!(copies, roc)
		if formatted.code != 0 {
			Shale.print!(formatted.out)
			Shale.fail!("check_stacking: a rewritten plant no longer parses")
		}
		$came_out_wrong : U64
		var $came_out_wrong = 0
		for want in Shale.glob!("${plants}/*.want") {
			name = Text.basename(want).drop_suffix(".want")
			ok = Report.read_text!("${scratch}/${name}.roc") == Report.read_text!(want)
			Shale.print!("${verdict(ok)}${name}.roc: comes out as its .want")
			if !(ok) {
				$came_out_wrong = $came_out_wrong + 1
			}
		}
		if $came_out_wrong > 0 {
			Shale.fail!("${$came_out_wrong.to_str()} plants came out wrong")
		}
		Shale.print!("PASS: every plant gives its finding, the clean ones none; the rewrite ends, a second changes nothing, every plant parses and comes out as its .want")
	}

	## The files Roc's parser refused, named, then a stop
	## (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale's `fail_if_refused`); nothing when it
	## refused none.
	fail_if_refused! : List(Str) => {}
	fail_if_refused! = |refused| {
		if !(refused.is_empty()) {
			for refusal in refused {
				Shale.print!("refused: ${refusal}")
			}
			refusals = "roc-ast refused ${refused.len().to_str()} files (named above)"
			why = "which have no tree to judge; every other file was judged"
			Shale.fail!("check_stacking: ${refusals}, ${why}")
		}
	}
}

## Where the self-test rewrites its copies of the plants.
scratch : Str
scratch = "scratch:stack"

## A plant's name, its path after the plants' folder.
name_of : Str -> Str
name_of = |path| path.drop_prefix("${SelfTest.plants}/")

## A plant's copy in `scratch`.
copy_of : Str -> Str
copy_of = |path| "${scratch}/${name_of(path)}"

## The start of a verdict's line.
verdict : Bool -> Str
verdict = |ok|
	if ok {
		"ok   "
	} else {
		"FAIL "
	}

## Each line marked `# findings N` (with `advice W`) held to the findings on
## it, a line printed for each: the answer is how many were wrong.
check_marks! : List(Str), Report.Judged => U64
check_marks! = |paths, judged| {
	$bad : U64
	var $bad = 0
	for path in paths {
		$number : U64
		var $number = 0
		for line in Text.lines(Report.read_text!(path)) {
			$number = $number + 1
			number = $number
			match Shale.re_find!(line, "# findings ([0-9]+)(?: advice ([a-z]+))?$") {
				Found(mark) => {
					(count_text, word) = match mark.groups {
						[count_given, word_given, ..] => (count_given, word_given)
						[count_given] => (count_given, "")
						[] => ("", "")
					}
					is_here = |finding| finding.path == path and finding.line == number
					here = judged.found.keep_if(is_here)
					got = here.len()
					var $ok = Ok(got.to_i64_wrap()) == I64.from_str(count_text)
					if word != "" {
						for finding in here {
							if !(finding.what.contains(word)) {
								$ok = Bool.False
							}
						}
					}
					place = "${name_of(path)}:${number.to_str()}"
					Shale.print!("${verdict($ok)}${place}: ${got.to_str()} findings, want ${count_text}")
					if !($ok) {
						$bad = $bad + 1
					}
				}
				NoMatch => {}
			}
		}
	}
	$bad
}

## Each plant held to the kinds of its findings by its name, a line printed
## for each: the answer is how many were wrong.
check_kinds! : List(Str), Report.Judged => U64
check_kinds! = |paths, judged| {
	$bad : U64
	var $bad = 0
	for path in paths {
		name = name_of(path)
		kinds = judged.found.keep_if(|finding| finding.path == path).map(|finding| finding.check)
		got = if kinds.is_empty() {
			""
		} else {
			" ${Str.join_with(kinds, " ")} "
		}
		is_long = name.starts_with("long")
		is_wide = name.starts_with("wide")
		want = if is_long {
			"long"
		} else if is_wide {
			"wide string"
		} else if name.starts_with("unstack") {
			"unstack"
		} else {
			"stack"
		}
		clean = name.starts_with("clean")
		var $ok = (clean and got == "") or (!(clean) and got.contains(" ${want} "))
		if is_long and got.contains("wide string") {
			$ok = Bool.False
		}
		if is_wide and got.contains("long") {
			$ok = Bool.False
		}
		shown = if got == "" {
			"no finding"
		} else {
			got
		}
		Shale.print!("${verdict($ok)}${name}: ${shown}")
		if !($ok) {
			$bad = $bad + 1
		}
	}
	$bad
}

cookbook/roc/check_stacking/Annotations.roc, 304 lines

## A function type's bare arguments, which no trailing comma can stack, read
## as the Shale original read them: an annotation (`name : A, B, C -> R`) or a
## type alias of a function (`Pick(a) : a, a, a -> a`) to its first arrow,
## over the lines `roc fmt` wraps it onto, and a record type's field whose
## type is a function (`{ on_pick : U8, U8, U8 -> U8 }`). The finding says
## what to do instead: a record for values that travel together, or a tag
## for a run of flags.
import lib.Bytes
import lib.Finding
import lib.Groups
import lib.Text

Annotations := [].{

	## An annotation's arguments: how many, its type's text up to the arrow
	## and that text shortened, the annotated name, and the annotation's last
	## line read.
	Annotation : {
		items : U64,
		shown : Str,
		text : Str,
		name : Str,
		last : U64,
	}

	## A record type's field whose type is a function: its name, how many
	## arguments, and the type's text up to the arrow.
	FieldFunction : {
		name : Str,
		items : U64,
		text : Str,
	}

	## Text cut to 60 bytes for a finding line, its end `...`.
	shortened : Str -> Str
	shortened = |text| {
		bytes = text.to_utf8()
		if bytes.len() > 60 {
			Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.take_first(57).concat(['.', '.', '.']))
		} else {
			text
		}
	}

	## The annotation line `number` of the lines starts, when it annotates a
	## function: its arguments before the first arrow outside any bracket,
	## counted by the commas outside any bracket. It goes on to the next line
	## while its text so far is empty, a bracket is open or its text ends in a
	## comma, passing over a comment on a line of its own; a blank line, or a
	## next line that starts another annotation, ends it.
	annotation_arguments : List(Str), U64 -> Try(Annotations.Annotation, [NoFunction])
	annotation_arguments = |source_lines, number| {
		first_line = Bytes.line_of(source_lines, number)
		var $piece = match start_text(type_line(first_line)) {
			Ok(piece) => piece
			Err(NoStart) => return Err(NoFunction)
		}
		name = Bytes.trimmed(before_colon(Bytes.trimmed(first_line)))
		var $type_text = []
		$depth : I64
		var $depth = 0
		$commas : U64
		var $commas = 0
		var $n = number
		while $n <= source_lines.len() {
			start = $type_text.len()
			$type_text = if start == 0 or $piece.is_empty() {
				$type_text.concat($piece)
			} else {
				$type_text.append(' ').concat($piece)
			}
			var $at = start + 1
			while $at <= $type_text.len() {
				c = Bytes.byte_at($type_text, $at)
				if Groups.closer_of(c) != 0 {
					$depth = $depth + 1
				}
				if Groups.is_closer(c) {
					$depth = $depth - 1
				}
				if $depth < 0 {
					return Err(NoFunction)
				}
				if $depth == 0 and c == ',' {
					$commas = $commas + 1
				}
				if $depth == 0 and is_arrow_at($type_text, $at) {
					text = Str.from_utf8_lossy(Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.span($type_text, 1, $at - 1)))
					return Ok({
						items: $commas + 1,
						shown: Annotations.shortened(text),
						text,
						name: Str.from_utf8_lossy(name),
						last: $n,
					})
				}
				$at = $at + 1
			}
			goes_on = $type_text.is_empty() or $depth > 0 or $type_text.last() == Ok(',')
			if !(goes_on) {
				return Err(NoFunction)
			}
			# The next line of code, past any comment on a line of its own.
			$n = $n + 1
			while $n <= source_lines.len() and !(
				Bytes.trimmed(
					Bytes.line_of(source_lines, $n),
				).is_empty()
			) and type_line(Bytes.line_of(source_lines, $n)).is_empty() {
				$n = $n + 1
			}
			if $n > source_lines.len() or Bytes.trimmed(
				Bytes.line_of(source_lines, $n),
			).is_empty() {
				return Err(NoFunction)
			}
			next_line = type_line(Bytes.line_of(source_lines, $n))
			if $depth == 0 and start_text(next_line) != Err(NoStart) {
				return Err(NoFunction)
			}
			$piece = next_line
		}
		Err(NoFunction)
	}

	## The function types among the fields of a record type whose inside,
	## between its braces, is `inner`: a field whose type has an arrow outside
	## any bracket, its arguments counted by the commas before it. A comma
	## starts the next field only when `name : ` follows it, so the commas of a
	## field's function type stay its own.
	record_field_functions : Str -> List(Annotations.FieldFunction)
	record_field_functions = |text| {
		inner = text.to_utf8()
		if !(starts_field(inner)) {
			return []
		}
		var $out = []
		$depth : I64
		var $depth = 0
		$commas : U64
		var $commas = 0
		var $type_start = 0
		var $field_start = 1
		var $name = []
		var $done = Bool.False
		var $at = 1
		while $at <= inner.len() {
			c = Bytes.byte_at(inner, $at)
			if Groups.closer_of(c) != 0 {
				$depth = $depth + 1
			}
			if Groups.is_closer(c) {
				$depth = $depth - 1
			}
			if $depth == 0 {
				if $type_start == 0 and Bytes.span(inner, $at, $at + 2) == [' ', ':', ' '] {
					$type_start = $at + 3
					$name = Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.span(inner, $field_start, $at - 1))
					$at = $at + 2
				} else if c == ',' and starts_field(Bytes.rest_from(inner, $at + 1)) {
					$commas = 0
					$type_start = 0
					$field_start = $at + 1
					$done = Bool.False
				} else if c == ',' {
					$commas = $commas + 1
				} else if !($done) and $type_start > 0 and Bytes.byte_at(
					inner,
					$at - 1,
				) == ' ' and is_arrow_at(inner, $at) {
					type_text = Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.span(inner, $type_start, $at - 1))
					$out = $out.append({
						name: Str.from_utf8_lossy($name),
						items: $commas + 1,
						text: Str.from_utf8_lossy(type_text),
					})
					$done = Bool.True
				}
			}
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		$out
	}

	## Whether every comma-separated item of a text is `Bool` or a Bool
	## literal, like `Bool, Bool, Bool` or `Bool.true, Bool.false, Bool.true`.
	are_all_flags : Str -> Bool
	are_all_flags = |text|
		text.split_on(",").all(
			|item| {
				flag = Text.trim(item)
				flag == "Bool" or flag == "Bool.true" or flag == "Bool.false" or flag == "Bool.True" or flag == "Bool.False"
			},
		)

	## What a flag's finding adds.
	flag_advice : Str
	flag_advice = ": a flag a caller passes is a tag, not a Bool (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md)"

	## The finding for a function type's bare arguments at a file's line.
	function_type_finding : { path : Str, line : U64 },
	{
		items : U64,
		shown : Str,
		text : Str,
	} -> Finding
	function_type_finding = |place, arguments| {
		advice = if Annotations.are_all_flags(arguments.text) {
			Annotations.flag_advice
		} else {
			": take a record (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md, Name what travels together)"
		}
		{
			path: place.path,
			line: place.line,
			check: "stack",
			what: "${arguments.items.to_str()} bare arguments in ${arguments.shown}, which no comma stacks${advice}",
		}
	}
}

## A line without a `#` comment, trimmed. A type has no string, so the first
## `#` starts the comment.
type_line : List(U8) -> List(U8)
type_line = |bytes|
	match bytes.find_first_index(|byte| byte == '#') {
		Ok(at) => Bytes.trimmed(bytes.take_first(at))
		Err(_) => Bytes.trimmed(bytes)
	}

## The text of a trimmed line before its first ` :`, or all of it.
before_colon : List(U8) -> List(U8)
before_colon = |bytes| {
	var $at = 1
	while $at < bytes.len() {
		if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $at) == ' ' and Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $at + 1) == ':' {
			return Bytes.span(bytes, 1, $at - 1)
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	bytes
}

## Whether `->` or `=>` stands at `place`.
is_arrow_at : List(U8), U64 -> Bool
is_arrow_at = |bytes, place| {
	byte = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, place)
	(byte == '-' or byte == '=') and Bytes.byte_at(bytes, place + 1) == '>'
}

## The type text after the start of a function's annotation (`name :`) or of
## a type alias (`Handler :`, `Pick(a) :`) on a comment-free line, which is
## empty when the type starts on the next line:
## `^[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!? :(?: (.*))?$` or
## `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\([^()]*\))? :(?: (.*))?$`.
start_text : List(U8) -> Try(List(U8), [NoStart])
start_text = |bytes| {
	first = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, 1)
	name_end =
		if (first >= 'a' and first <= 'z') or first == '_' {
			end = Bytes.word_end(bytes, 2)
			if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, end) == '!' {
				end + 1
			} else {
				end
			}
		} else if first >= 'A' and first <= 'Z' {
			end = Bytes.word_end(bytes, 2)
			if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, end) == '(' {
				match bytes.drop_first(end).find_first_index(|byte| byte == '(' or byte == ')') {
					Ok(offset) if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, end + offset + 1) == ')' => end + offset + 2
					_ => end
				}
			} else {
				end
			}
		} else {
			return Err(NoStart)
		}
	rest = Bytes.rest_from(bytes, name_end)
	if rest == [' ', ':'] {
		Ok([])
	} else if rest.starts_with([' ', ':', ' ']) {
		Ok(rest.drop_first(3))
	} else {
		Err(NoStart)
	}
}

## Whether the bytes start a record type's field: `^ *[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* : `.
starts_field : List(U8) -> Bool
starts_field = |bytes| {
	var $at = 1
	while Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $at) == ' ' {
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	first = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $at)
	if (first >= 'a' and first <= 'z') or first == '_' {
		end = Bytes.word_end(bytes, $at + 1)
		Bytes.span(bytes, end, end + 2) == [' ', ':', ' ']
	} else {
		Bool.False
	}
}

-- This recipe finds groups in .roc files laid out against the stacking rule,
-- and with `write=1` lays them out by it. A group is a list, record, tuple,
-- call's arguments, tag payload or lambda's arguments. A group of three or
-- more items and six or more tokens stacks, one item a line. Any other group
-- sits on one line while that line fits `width`. The rule and what counts as
-- a token are in cookbook/roc/groups.shale.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_stacking.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_stacking.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc write=1
--   shale cookbook:roc/check_stacking.shale self_test=1
--
-- The arguments:
--   glob   the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default;
--   skip   files the glob finds to leave out, by path, comma-separated, for
--          tables of data that read better side by side;
--   width  the widest a line may be, 100 by default, a tab counting four;
--   tokens the tokens from which a group stacks, 6 by default;
--   dictated a table of functions whose arguments something outside the file
--          dictates, one `path name -- reason` a line, judged as a header's
--          names are (below);
--   house  with `house=0`, leave out every finding here, as the stacking rule
--          is our house style (cookbook/roc/house.shale);
--   write  with `write=1`, rewrite the files (see below).
--
-- A group on one line that should stack is a finding, `path:line: stack: ...`,
-- left to right. A stacked group that should sit on one line is a finding,
-- `path:line: unstack: ...`, at the line it opens on. A line wider than `width`
-- with nothing to stack by the rule is a finding too, of one of two kinds. It
-- is `wide string` when
-- it would fit `width` if the text of each string literal on it counted as
-- empty, because Roc has no short way to split a string. Otherwise it is
-- `long`. Roc's own parser says which columns are a string's text, so the
-- code in an interpolation (`"${...}"`) counts, a comment counts, and so does
-- a string in an `import` or the file's header, which has no such node. The
-- output is the counts, the findings, and the counts again
-- (cookbook/findings.shale). A file with a line wider than `width` that
-- roc-ast refuses keeps that line as `long`, and the run fails, naming it, as
-- it does for an app's or platform's file that roc-ast refuses.
--
-- A stacked group stays stacked, with no finding, when its joined line would
-- be wider than `width`, or when it holds a comment, a `\\` string, a blank
-- line, a block's statements, or a group that stays stacked.
--
-- Some groups are not findings, or get special advice:
--   - A list or tuple whose items are all literals (numbers, plain strings,
--     characters, bare tags) is a table's row, like `[0, 0, 0]` or
--     `(0.0, 0.0, 1.5)`, and is read at a glance. It is no finding while
--     its line fits `width`. A call's arguments are never a row.
--   - A group of three or more `Bool`s or Bool literals is told that a flag
--     a caller passes should be a tag, as roc-style.md says, whatever its
--     tokens.
--   - A function's annotation (`name : A, B, C -> R`), or a type alias of a
--     function (`Pick(a) : a, a, a -> a`), is read to its first arrow, over
--     the lines `roc fmt` wraps it onto, from a type that starts on the line
--     after the colon, past a comment on a line of its own, to a blank line.
--     When it is a finding for its arguments, at its first line, the
--     function's lambda arguments on the line after it are not reported
--     again.
--   - A field of a record type on one line whose type is a function
--     (`{ on_pick : U8, U8, U8 -> U8 }`) is read the same way, its arguments
--     counted up to its arrow, unless its file's header dictates it (a
--     platform's `requires { step : U8, U8, U8 -> U8 }`).
--   - The annotation of a name its file's header dictates is no finding for
--     its arguments, as the platform chose them: what an app's header
--     provides, and what a platform's header requires and provides
--     (cookbook/roc/headers.shale). Nor are that name's lambda arguments.
--   - The items of a `where` clause are its method constraints, so
--     `k.is_eq : k, k -> Bool` is one item, and a record or list pattern's
--     rest (`..`) is no item.
--   - The groups of a platform header's `targets:` section are no findings, and
--     the rewrite leaves them alone, as `roc fmt` lays that section out by
--     itself. A line there wider than `width` is still `long`.
-- Strings, characters, `\\` multiline strings and `#` comments are skipped,
-- so a comma or bracket inside one is no item.
--
-- With `write=1`, the recipe gives each group that should stack a trailing
-- comma after its last item, outermost first, takes the trailing comma from
-- each group that should unstack, and runs `roc fmt` on the files it changed,
-- which stacks a group with a trailing comma and joins a group without one. On
-- a long line with no group to stack by the rule, the widest group of two or
-- more items gets the comma, as wrap_long_lines.shale does. This repeats until a
-- pass changes nothing, so a second run changes nothing either. The recipe then
-- prints the findings left, which the rewrite can't reach: long lines, and
-- the arguments of a function type, bare (`three : U8, U8, U8 -> U8`) or in
-- parentheses (`(U8, U8, U8 -> U8)`), because Roc refuses a trailing comma
-- there.
--
-- `roc fmt`'s layout changes between Roc nightlies, so `write=1` runs the
-- Roc the tree is built with: `tools:roc-<pin>/roc`, the pin read from the
-- `roc-version` file in the directory the run starts in, normally the
-- repository's root. Without that file it stops before changing anything
-- (cookbook/roc/pinned.shale).
--
-- `self_test=1` checks the plants in `cookbook/roc/plants/check_stacking/`. Each
-- plant must give a finding of the kind its name starts with (`long`,
-- `wide`, `unstack`, or else `stack`), a `long` plant no `wide string` and a
-- `wide` plant no `long`, and a `clean*.roc` plant none. A plant line ending
-- `# findings N` must give exactly N findings, and with `advice W` after
-- it each of them must contain the word W. Then the test copies the plants
-- to `scratch:stack/` and rewrites them there with the self-test's Roc:
-- the rewrite must end, a second rewrite must change nothing, every file must
-- still parse, and a plant with a `.want` file must come out as it.
--
-- budget: steps=900000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000

const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_stacking"
const SCRATCH = "scratch:stack"
const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "/*.roc") or arg("glob", "**/*.roc")
const SKIP = arg("skip", "")
const DICTATED = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "/dictated.txt") or arg("dictated", "")
const WIDTH = arg("width", 100)
const WRITE = arg("write", "") == "1"

-- The files the glob finds, less the ones `skip` names. A name in `skip` that
-- the glob doesn't find stops the run, so a renamed file can't go unchecked.
function chosen_files()
  local found = glob(GLOB)
  if SKIP == "" then return found end
  local skipped = {}
  for name in split(SKIP, ",") do skipped[name] = false end
  local kept = {}
  for f in found do
    if has_key(skipped, f) then skipped[f] = true else push(kept, f) end
  end
  for name in keys(skipped) do
    if not skipped[name] then fail("check_stacking: skip names " .. name .. ", which the glob doesn't find") end
  end
  return kept
end
use("./pinned.shale")
use("cookbook:findings.shale")
use("./groups.shale")
use("./parsed.shale")
use("./headers.shale")
use("./house.shale")
const TOKENS = arg("tokens", STACK_TOKENS)
const MAX_PASSES = 12

-- Text cut to 60 characters for a finding line.
function shortened(s)
  if #s > 60 then return sub(s, 1, 57) .. "..." end
  return s
end

-- The start of a function's annotation (`name :`) or of a type alias
-- (`Handler :`, `Pick(a) :`), the type's text after it, which may be empty
-- when the type starts on the next line.
const ANNOTATION_START = "^[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!? :(?: (.*))?$"
const ALIAS_START = "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\\([^()]*\\))? :(?: (.*))?$"

-- The start of an annotation or alias on the line `l`, read with type_line,
-- or nil.
function annotation_start(l)
  local m = re_find(l, ANNOTATION_START)
  if m ~= nil then return m end
  return re_find(l, ALIAS_START)
end

-- The type text an annotation's start gives on its own line.
function start_text(m)
  local text = get(m.groups, 1, "")
  if text == nil then return "" end
  return text
end

-- Line `l` without a `#` comment, trimmed. A type has no string, so the
-- first `#` starts the comment.
function type_line(l)
  local at = find(l, "#")
  if at == nil then return trim(l) end
  return trim(sub(l, 1, at - 1))
end

-- If line `i` of `ls` starts a function's annotation (`name : A, B, C -> R`),
-- its arguments before the first arrow, counted by the commas outside any
-- brackets: `{items, shown, text, name, last}`, where `shown` is `text`
-- shortened and `last` the annotation's last line read. A type alias of a
-- function (`Handler : U8, U8, U8 -> U8`) counts the same way. `roc fmt` wraps
-- a long signature, so the annotation goes on to the next line while its text
-- so far is empty (the type starts after the colon's line), a bracket is open
-- or its text ends in a comma outside any bracket, until the first arrow
-- outside any bracket. A comment on a line of its own is passed over; a blank
-- line, or a next line that starts another annotation or field, ends it. nil
-- when line `i` annotates no function.
function annotation_arguments(ls, i)
  local m = annotation_start(type_line(ls[i]))
  if m == nil then return nil end
  local name = trim(split(trim(ls[i]), " :")[1])
  local type_text = ""
  local depth = 0
  local commas = 0
  local n = i
  local piece = start_text(m)
  while true do
    local start = #type_text
    type_text = type_text .. ((start == 0 or piece == "") and "" or " ") .. piece
    for at = start + 1, #type_text do
      local c = sub(type_text, at, at)
      if has_key(OPENERS, c) then depth = depth + 1 end
      if has_key(CLOSERS, c) then depth = depth - 1 end
      if depth < 0 then return nil end
      if depth == 0 and c == "," then commas = commas + 1 end
      if depth == 0 and (sub(type_text, at, at + 1) == "->" or sub(type_text, at, at + 1) == "=>") then
        local text = trim(sub(type_text, 1, at - 1))
        return {items = commas + 1, shown = shortened(text), text = text, name = name, last = n}
      end
    end
    local goes_on = type_text == "" or depth > 0 or ends_with(type_text, ",")
    if not goes_on then return nil end
    -- The next line of code, past any comment on a line of its own.
    n = n + 1
    while n <= #ls and trim(ls[n]) ~= "" and type_line(ls[n]) == "" do n = n + 1 end
    if n > #ls or trim(ls[n]) == "" then return nil end
    local next_line = type_line(ls[n])
    if depth == 0 and annotation_start(next_line) ~= nil then return nil end
    piece = next_line
  end
end

-- Whether every comma-separated item of `text` is `Bool` or a Bool
-- literal, like `Bool, Bool, Bool` or `Bool.true, Bool.false, Bool.true`.
const FLAGS = {Bool = true, ["Bool.true"] = true, ["Bool.false"] = true, ["Bool.True"] = true, ["Bool.False"] = true}
function are_all_flags(text)
  for item in split(text, ",") do
    if not has_key(FLAGS, trim(item)) then return false end
  end
  return true
end

const FLAG_ADVICE = ": a flag a caller passes is a tag, not a Bool (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md)"

-- The finding for a function type's arguments, which can't take a
-- trailing comma. The advice is a record for values that travel together,
-- or a tag for a run of flags.
function function_type_finding(path, line, items, shown, text)
  local advice = are_all_flags(text) and FLAG_ADVICE or ": take a record (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md, Name what travels together)"
  return {path = path, line = line, kind = "stack", what = items .. " bare arguments in " .. shown .. ", which no comma stacks" .. advice}
end

-- The start of a record type's field, `name : `.
const FIELD_START = "^ *[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* : "

-- The function types among the fields of a record type whose inside, between
-- its braces, is `inner`, each `{name, items, text}`: a field whose type has an
-- arrow outside any bracket, its arguments counted by the commas before it. A
-- comma starts the next field only when `name : ` follows it, so the commas
-- of a field's function type stay its own.
function record_field_functions(inner)
  local out = {}
  if re_find(inner, FIELD_START) == nil then return out end
  local depth = 0
  local commas = 0
  local type_start = 0
  local field_start = 1
  local name = ""
  local done = false
  local at = 1
  while at <= #inner do
    local c = sub(inner, at, at)
    if has_key(OPENERS, c) then depth = depth + 1 end
    if has_key(CLOSERS, c) then depth = depth - 1 end
    if depth == 0 then
      if type_start == 0 and sub(inner, at, at + 2) == " : " then
        type_start = at + 3
        name = trim(sub(inner, field_start, at - 1))
        at = at + 2
      elseif c == "," and re_find(sub(inner, at + 1), FIELD_START) ~= nil then
        commas = 0
        type_start = 0
        field_start = at + 1
        done = false
      elseif c == "," then
        commas = commas + 1
      elseif not done and type_start > 0 and sub(inner, at - 1, at - 1) == " " and (sub(inner, at, at + 1) == "->" or sub(inner, at, at + 1) == "=>") then
        push(out, {name = name, items = commas + 1, text = trim(sub(inner, type_start, at - 1))})
        done = true
      end
    end
    at = at + 1
  end
  return out
end

-- Whether any line of the file at `p` is wider than WIDTH.
function has_wide_line(p)
  for l in lines(read(p)) do
    if line_width(l) > WIDTH then return true end
  end
  return false
end

-- The columns that strings' text takes up in `files`, by Roc's parser, as
-- `{columns, refused}`. `columns[path]` maps a line's number, as text, to
-- those columns. Only a file with a wide line is parsed, so a tree of short
-- lines never needs roc-ast. `refused` is parse_roc_files' list.
function string_columns_in(files)
  local wide_files = {}
  for p in files do
    if has_wide_line(p) then push(wide_files, p) end
  end
  local columns = {}
  if #wide_files == 0 then return {columns = columns, refused = {}} end
  local parsed = parse_roc_files(wide_files)
  for f in parsed.files do
    columns[f.path] = string_columns_on_lines(f.nodes, split(read(f.path), "\n"), "check_stacking: " .. f.path)
  end
  return {columns = columns, refused = parsed.refused}
end

-- The finding for line `i` of `p`, wider than WIDTH with nothing else found
-- on it. `string_columns` is the columns of strings' text on that file's
-- lines, by line number.
function wide_line_finding(p, i, l, reachable_line, string_columns)
  local width = line_width(l)
  local without_strings = width - get(string_columns, "" .. i, 0)
  if without_strings <= WIDTH then
    return {path = p, line = i, kind = "wide string", what = width .. " columns, " .. without_strings .. " without its strings"}
  end
  local why = starts_with(trim(l), "#") and "a comment" or (group_to_stack(reachable_line, TOKENS, WIDTH) ~= nil and "a group to stack" or "nothing to stack")
  return {path = p, line = i, kind = "long", what = width .. " columns, " .. why}
end

function concat_lists(a, b)
  local out = {}
  for x in a do push(out, x) end
  for x in b do push(out, x) end
  return out
end

-- The names the headers of `files` dictate, by path, as `{names, refused}`.
-- Only an app's or a platform's file is parsed, so a tree of modules needs no
-- roc-ast for this.
function dictated_names_in(files)
  local headed = {}
  for p in files do
    local word = header_word(read(p))
    if word == "app" or word == "platform" then push(headed, p) end
  end
  local names = {}
  if #headed == 0 then return {names = names, refused = {}} end
  local parsed = parse_roc_files(headed)
  for f in parsed.files do names[f.path] = header_names(f.nodes).dictated end
  return {names = names, refused = parsed.refused}
end

-- The names the `dictated` table adds to `names`, the result of
-- dictated_names_in. Each line of the table is a file's path, a function's
-- name, and after ` -- ` who dictates its arguments, such as an API the file
-- copies or an edge with no records. The path names the file the glob finds
-- with that path or ending `/` and that path, so the self-test's copies in
-- scratch are found too. A line whose file the glob doesn't find, whose
-- function has no annotation there, or that gives no reason stops the run, so
-- the table can't go stale.
function with_dictated_table(names, files)
  if DICTATED == "" then return names end
  for l in lines(read(DICTATED)) do
    if trim(l) ~= "" and not starts_with(trim(l), "#") then
      local m = re_find(l, "^(\\S+) ([a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!?) -- \\S")
      if m == nil then fail("check_stacking: " .. DICTATED .. " has a line that is not `path name -- reason`: " .. l) end
      local name = m.groups[2]
      local path = nil
      for p in files do
        if p == m.groups[1] or ends_with(p, "/" .. m.groups[1]) then path = p end
      end
      if path == nil then fail("check_stacking: " .. DICTATED .. " names " .. m.groups[1] .. ", which the glob doesn't find") end
      local annotated = false
      for line in lines(read(path)) do
        if starts_with(trim(line), name .. " :") then annotated = true end
      end
      if not annotated then
        fail("check_stacking: " .. DICTATED .. " names " .. name .. ", which has no annotation in " .. path)
      end
      local here = get(names, path, {})
      here[name] = true
      names[path] = here
    end
  end
  return names
end

-- Every finding in `files`, as `{found, refused}`: `found` holds each as
-- `{path, line, kind, what}`, and `refused` the files roc-ast refused.
function findings_in(files)
  local out = {}
  local strings = string_columns_in(files)
  local dictated = dictated_names_in(files)
  dictated.names = with_dictated_table(dictated.names, files)
  for p in files do
    local ls = split(read(p), "\n")
    local reachable = without_targets_section(ls)
    local string_columns = get(strings.columns, p, {})
    local dictated_here = get(dictated.names, p, {})
    -- The function whose annotation ended on the line before and was a
    -- finding for its arguments, or "". Its lambda's arguments are not
    -- reported again.
    local annotated_fn = ""
    local annotation_end = 0
    for i = 1, #ls do
      local found_on_line = 0
      local skip_lambda = annotated_fn ~= "" and i == annotation_end + 1 and starts_with(trim(ls[i]), annotated_fn .. " = |")
      if i > annotation_end then annotated_fn = "" end
      local data_line = is_data_line(reachable[i], WIDTH)
      for g in sort(groups_on_line(reachable[i]), "open") do
        local inner = sub(ls[i], g.open + 1, g.close - 1)
        if sub(ls[i], g.open, g.open) == "{" then
          for field in record_field_functions(inner) do
            if field.items >= 3 and not has_key(dictated_here, field.name) then
              push(out, function_type_finding(p, i, field.items, shortened(field.text), field.text))
              found_on_line = found_on_line + 1
            end
          end
        end
        if g.items >= 3 and g.fn_type then
          local arguments = split(split(inner, "->")[1], "=>")[1]
          push(out, function_type_finding(p, i, g.items, shortened(sub(ls[i], g.open, g.close)), arguments))
          found_on_line = found_on_line + 1
        elseif skip_lambda and sub(ls[i], g.open, g.open) == "|" then
          skip_lambda = false
        elseif not data_line then
          local are_flags = g.items >= 3 and not g.trailing and are_all_flags(inner)
          if are_flags or should_stack(ls[i], g, TOKENS, WIDTH) then
            local advice = are_flags and FLAG_ADVICE or ""
            push(out, {path = p, line = i, kind = "stack", what = g.tokens .. " tokens in " .. shortened(sub(ls[i], g.open, g.close)) .. advice})
            found_on_line = found_on_line + 1
          end
        end
      end
      -- A line inside a wrapped annotation starts none.
      local annotation = i > annotation_end and annotation_arguments(ls, i) or nil
      if annotation ~= nil then annotation_end = annotation.last end
      if annotation ~= nil and annotation.items >= 3 then
        annotated_fn = annotation.name
        if not has_key(dictated_here, annotation.name) then
          push(out, function_type_finding(p, i, annotation.items, annotation.shown, annotation.text))
          found_on_line = found_on_line + 1
        end
      end
      if found_on_line == 0 and line_width(ls[i]) > WIDTH then
        push(out, wide_line_finding(p, i, ls[i], reachable[i], string_columns))
      end
    end
    for g in groups_to_unstack(ls, TOKENS, WIDTH) do
      push(out, {path = p, line = g.line, kind = "unstack", what = g.tokens .. " tokens in " .. shortened(trim(group_on_one_line(ls, g)))})
    end
  end
  return {found = out, refused = unique(concat_lists(strings.refused, dictated.refused))}
end

-- Runs `roc fmt` on `files`. The result's code is not 0 when a file does
-- not parse.
function roc_fmt(files)
  local argv = {roc_bin("check_stacking", SELF_TEST), "fmt"}
  for p in files do push(argv, real(p)) end
  return run(argv, {timeout_ms = 120000, tail = 20})
end

-- Rewrites `files` pass after pass until a pass changes nothing, and
-- returns how many groups the first pass changed. A pass takes the trailing
-- comma from each group that should unstack and gives one to each line's group
-- that should stack, and `roc fmt` lays out the result.
function rewrite_trailing_commas(files)
  local first_pass_count = 0
  local pass = 1
  local changed = 1
  local touched = {}
  while changed > 0 and pass <= MAX_PASSES do
    changed = 0
    touched = {}
    for p in files do
      local ls = split(read(p), "\n")
      local unstacked = groups_to_unstack(ls, TOKENS, WIDTH)
      ls = without_trailing_commas(ls, unstacked)
      local reachable = without_targets_section(ls)
      local n = #unstacked
      for i = 1, #ls do
        if not starts_with(trim(ls[i]), "#") then
          local g = group_to_stack(reachable[i], TOKENS, WIDTH)
          if g ~= nil then
            ls[i] = with_trailing_comma(ls[i], g)
            n = n + 1
          end
        end
      end
      if n > 0 then
        replace(p, join(ls, "\n"))
        push(touched, p)
        changed = changed + n
      end
    end
    print("pass " .. pass .. ": " .. changed .. " groups rewritten, in " .. #touched .. " files")
    if pass == 1 then first_pass_count = changed end
    if #touched > 0 then
      local r = roc_fmt(touched)
      if r.code ~= 0 then
        print(r.out)
        fail("roc fmt failed")
      end
    end
    pass = pass + 1
  end
  if changed > 0 then fail("check_stacking: still changing after " .. MAX_PASSES .. " passes: " .. join(touched, ", ")) end
  return first_pass_count
end

function self_test()
  local files = chosen_files()
  local kinds_by_plant = {}
  local count_by_line = {}
  local whats_by_line = {}
  local judged = findings_in(files)
  fail_if_refused("check_stacking", judged.refused)
  for f in judged.found do
    local name = sub(f.path, #PLANTS + 2)
    kinds_by_plant[name] = get(kinds_by_plant, name, " ") .. f.kind .. " "
    incr(count_by_line, f.path .. ":" .. f.line)
    push_at(whats_by_line, f.path .. ":" .. f.line, f.what)
  end
  local bad = 0
  for p in files do
    local n = 0
    for l in lines(read(p)) do
      n = n + 1
      local mark = re_find(l, "# findings ([0-9]+)(?: advice ([a-z]+))?$")
      if mark ~= nil then
        local got = get(count_by_line, p .. ":" .. n, 0)
        local ok = got == tonumber(mark.groups[1])
        local word = get(mark.groups, 2, "")
        if word ~= nil and word ~= "" then
          for what in get(whats_by_line, p .. ":" .. n, {}) do
            if not contains(what, word) then ok = false end
          end
        end
        print((ok and "ok   " or "FAIL ") .. sub(p, #PLANTS + 2) .. ":" .. n .. ": " .. got .. " findings, want " .. mark.groups[1])
        if not ok then bad = bad + 1 end
      end
    end
  end
  for p in files do
    local name = sub(p, #PLANTS + 2)
    local is_long = starts_with(name, "long")
    local is_wide = starts_with(name, "wide")
    local want = is_long and "long" or (is_wide and "wide string" or (starts_with(name, "unstack") and "unstack" or "stack"))
    local got = get(kinds_by_plant, name, "")
    local clean = starts_with(name, "clean")
    local ok = (clean and got == "") or (not clean and contains(got, " " .. want .. " "))
    if is_long and contains(got, "wide string") then ok = false end
    if is_wide and contains(got, "long") then ok = false end
    print((ok and "ok   " or "FAIL ") .. name .. ": " .. (got == "" and "no finding" or got))
    if not ok then bad = bad + 1 end
  end
  if bad > 0 then fail(bad .. " plants wrong") end
  if is_dir(SCRATCH) then remove_tree(SCRATCH) end
  mkdir(SCRATCH)
  local copies = {}
  for p in files do
    local to = SCRATCH .. "/" .. sub(p, #PLANTS + 2)
    replace(to, read(p))
    push(copies, to)
  end
  rewrite_trailing_commas(copies)
  local again = rewrite_trailing_commas(copies)
  if again > 0 then fail("check_stacking: a second rewrite changed " .. again .. " more groups") end
  local r = roc_fmt(copies)
  if r.code ~= 0 then
    print(r.out)
    fail("check_stacking: a rewritten plant no longer parses")
  end
  for want in glob(PLANTS .. "/*.want") do
    local name = sub(basename(want), 1, #basename(want) - 5)
    local ok = read(SCRATCH .. "/" .. name .. ".roc") == read(want)
    print((ok and "ok   " or "FAIL ") .. name .. ".roc: comes out as its .want")
    if not ok then bad = bad + 1 end
  end
  if bad > 0 then fail(bad .. " plants came out wrong") end
  print("PASS: every plant gives its finding, the clean ones none; the rewrite ends, a second changes nothing, every plant parses and comes out as its .want")
end

function finding_line(f)
  return f.path .. ":" .. f.line .. ": " .. f.kind .. ": " .. f.what
end

if SELF_TEST then
  self_test()
elseif WRITE then
  refuse_house_rewrite("check_stacking")
  -- Stop before any change if the tree's Roc is missing.
  roc_bin("check_stacking", SELF_TEST)
  local files = chosen_files()
  rewrite_trailing_commas(files)
  local left = {}
  local judged = findings_in(files)
  for f in judged.found do push(left, finding_line(f)) end
  print_findings(#left .. " left, each a line the rewrite can't reach", left)
  fail_if_refused("check_stacking", judged.refused)
else
  local files = chosen_files()
  local all = {}
  local count_by_kind = {}
  local judged = findings_in(files)
  for f in judged.found do
    if not house_leaves_out("check_stacking", f.kind) then
      push(all, finding_line(f))
      incr(count_by_kind, f.kind)
    end
  end
  local counts = get(count_by_kind, "stack", 0) .. " to stack, " .. get(count_by_kind, "unstack", 0) .. " to unstack, " .. get(count_by_kind, "long", 0) .. " long, " .. get(count_by_kind, "wide string", 0) .. " wide string" .. house_note("check_stacking")
  print_findings(#all .. " findings in " .. #files .. " files: " .. counts, all)
  fail_if_refused("check_stacking", judged.refused)
end

hunt_names

Awkward names hunted across a whole tree from Roc's own parse trees and, when asked, its type checker: an effect named like a state, a question that gives no Bool, tense in tags, container words, a one-word where method, a pure function named to act outside, and docs naming what is gone.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.exists!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.print!, Shale.re_find!, Shale.re_find_all!, Shale.re_match!, Shale.read!, Shale.real!, Shale.roc_tree!, Shale.run!.
Roc: 3,243 lines in 13 files. Shale original: 718 lines, plus 1,999 lines in the 10 libraries it loads, which other recipes share.

Roc

It also imports Finding, Headers, RocTypes, Text, Tree from the shared Roc library.

cookbook/roc/hunt_names/hunt_names.roc, 311 lines

## hunt_names, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md): awkward
## names in every .roc file of a tree, from Roc's own parser's trees. Its
## launcher, cookbook/roc/hunt_names.shale, is how it is run, and its header
## says the checks, from `state_effect` to `stale_doc_name`.
## check_goldens.shale, beside this, holds its output on the plants to its
## goldens, line for line.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/hunt_names.shale glob=app/**/*.roc
##   shale cookbook:roc/hunt_names.shale self_test=1
##
## The arguments: `glob` (`**/*.roc`), `words` (`words=1` prints the census
## of effects' first words instead), `house` (`house=0` leaves out the house
## style), `types` (`1` asks Roc's type checker), `root` (the app or apps the
## types are read from), `terms` (a project's terms) and `self_test`
## (`self_test=1` checks the plants, the typed ones with the types).
##
## This root reads the word lists (Words), globs the files, gathers the
## types (Types), has Roc's parser read the files, reads each file's
## definitions (Reading), judges them (Judge, with ListNames and Makers),
## then the bindings (ShortNames), the docs (DocNames) and what is judged
## over every file (Passes), and prints the verdict; SelfTest judges the
## plants. Tree, Text, Finding and RocTypes are the cookbook's Roc library,
## cookbook/roc/lib/.
## budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 output_bytes=4000000 roc_cpu_ms=600000 programs=100
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import lib.Finding
import lib.RocTypes
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree
import DocNames
import Facts
import Judge
import ListNames
import Passes
import Reading
import SelfTest
import ShortNames
import Types
import Words

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	self_test = Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1"
	plants = SelfTest.plants
	glob = if self_test {
		"${plants}*.roc"
	} else {
		Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc")
	}
	types_asked = Shale.arg!("types", "0")
	if types_asked != "0" and types_asked != "1" {
		Shale.fail!("hunt_names: types=${types_asked}: 0 (the default) or 1")
	}
	# The self-test checks its typed plants with the types, and the rest
	# without.
	use_types = self_test or types_asked == "1"
	root = if self_test {
		"${plants}typed/QuietApp.roc"
	} else {
		Shale.arg!("root", "")
	}
	is_census = Shale.arg!("words", "") == "1"
	terms_file = if self_test {
		"${plants}terms.txt"
	} else {
		Shale.arg!("terms", "")
	}
	lists = Words.read!(terms_file)
	house_style = Words.house_style!({})
	paths = if self_test {
		Shale.glob!(glob).concat(Shale.glob!("${plants}typed/*.roc"))
	} else {
		Shale.glob!(glob)
	}
	types = if use_types {
		roc = Types.roc_bin!("hunt_names", self_test)
		# The self-test's untyped plants are imported by no root.
		exempt = if self_test {
			Set.from_list(Shale.glob!("${plants}*.roc"))
		} else {
			Set.empty()
		}
		Types.gather!({ who: "hunt_names", kind: Patterns, root, roc, paths, exempt })
	} else {
		{ typing: RocTypes.no_types, unreached: [] }
	}
	parsed = parse!(paths)
	read = definitions_of(parsed.files, types.typing)
	found = judged!({ files: parsed.files, read, lists, self_test })
	house = if !(found.is_empty()) or !(is_census) {
		read_house!({})
	} else {
		Kept
	}
	is_kept = |finding|
		match house {
			Kept => Bool.True
			LeftOut => !(house_style.contains(finding.check))
		}
	reported = found.keep_if(is_kept)
	finding_lines = if is_census {
		[]
	} else {
		reported.map(Finding.line_of)
	}
	file_count = paths.len().to_str()
	if is_census {
		census = Passes.census_lines(Passes.census(read.definitions, lists))
		print_findings!("hunt_names (Roc) census: ${file_count} files; ${census.summary}", census.lines)
	} else {
		house_note = match house {
			Kept => ""
			LeftOut => "; left out as house style: ${Str.join_with(house_style, ", ")}"
		}
		print_findings!("hunt_names (Roc): ${file_count} files; ${Finding.counts_of(reported, checks)}${house_note}", finding_lines)
	}
	fail_if_refused!(parsed.refused, types.unreached)
	if self_test {
		census = Passes.census(read.definitions, lists)
		SelfTest.run!({ paths, findings: reported, census, finding_lines }, checks)
	}
}

## The checks, in the order the summary counts them.
checks : List(Str)
checks = ["state_effect", "question", "vague", "name_type", "negative", "noun_effect", "command_tense", "mixed_tense", "container", "preposition_split", "short_name", "worker_name", "stacked_preposition", "taken_word", "bare_participle", "phrase_name", "singular_list", "world_verb", "where_name", "stale_doc_name"]

## The files Roc's parser read, each with its text cut at each newline, and
## a `path: why` line for each it refused.
parse! : List(Str) => { files : List(Reading.FileRead), refused : List(Str) }
parse! = |paths| {
	var $files = []
	var $refused = []
	for file in Shale.roc_tree!(paths) {
		if file.err == "" {
			source = match Shale.read!(file.path) {
				Found(text) => text
				Missing => ""
			}
			$files = $files.append({ path: file.path, nodes: file.nodes, source_lines: source.split_on("\n") })
		} else if file.err.starts_with(file.path) {
			$refused = $refused.append(file.err)
		} else {
			$refused = $refused.append("${file.path}: ${file.err}")
		}
	}
	{ files: $files, refused: $refused }
}

## What the run asks of the files read: the files, their definitions and
## the facts their reading gathered, the word lists, and whether it is the
## self-test.
Asked : {
	files : List(Reading.FileRead),
	read : { definitions : List(Reading.Definition), facts : Facts.Gathered },
	lists : Words.Lists,
	self_test : Bool,
}

## Every file's definitions, in file order, and the facts their reading
## gathers.
definitions_of : List(Reading.FileRead), RocTypes.Typing -> { definitions : List(Reading.Definition), facts : Facts.Gathered }
definitions_of = |files, typing|
	files.fold(
		{ definitions: [], facts: Facts.none },
		|so_far, file| {
			pattern_types = pattern_types_of(typing, file.path, file.nodes)
			read = Reading.file_definitions(file, pattern_types)
			{ definitions: so_far.definitions.concat(read.definitions), facts: Facts.joined(so_far.facts, read.facts) }
		},
	)

## The checker's type of each plain-name pattern of the file at `path`, by
## its node's place: none when no root reached the file.
pattern_types_of : RocTypes.Typing, Str, List(Tree.Node) -> Dict(U64, Str)
pattern_types_of = |typing, path, nodes| {
	if !(typing.real.contains(path)) {
		return Dict.empty()
	}
	var $typed = Dict.empty()
	$place : U64
	var $place = 0
	for node in nodes {
		$place = $place + 1
		if node.kind == "p-ident" {
			match RocTypes.type_at(typing, path, node) {
				Ok(written) => {
					$typed = $typed.insert($place, written)
				}
				Err(NoType) => {}
			}
		}
	}
	$typed
}

## Every finding, in the Shale original's order: each definition's, each
## file's `where` clauses and bindings, each file's docs, the type and
## field names, and the preposition splits.
judged! : Asked => List(Finding)
judged! = |asked| {
	lists = asked.lists
	read = asked.read
	facts = read.facts
	by_definition = read.definitions.map(|definition| Judge.findings(definition, lists, facts)).join()
	by_file = asked.files
		.map(|file| Passes.where_name_findings(file.path, file.nodes, lists.fixed_names).concat(ShortNames.findings(file.path, file.nodes)))
		.join()
	sources = Words.word_set!("cookbook:words/cited_sources.txt")
	# Each plant opens by naming its check, so in the self-test the check
	# names, and this recipe's, count as names.
	known = if asked.self_test {
		Set.from_list(checks).insert("hunt_names")
	} else {
		Set.empty()
	}
	doc_files = asked.files.map(|file| { path: file.path, nodes: file.nodes, source_lines: file.source_lines })
	by_doc = DocNames.findings!(doc_files, DocNames.seen_of(doc_files, known, sources))
	by_name = facts.names
		.map(
			|named| {
				subject = { path: named.path, line: named.line, name: named.name, kind: "field", is_function: named.is_function, first: named.first, gives: named.gives }
				listed = if named.is_field {
					ListNames.findings(subject, lists)
				} else {
					[]
				}
				Passes.container_findings(named, lists).concat(listed)
			},
		)
		.join()
	splits = Passes.preposition_splits(read.definitions, lists, facts.keywords)
	by_definition.concat(by_file).concat(by_doc).concat(by_name).concat(splits)
}

## Whether `house=0` leaves the house style out (cookbook/roc/house.shale):
## `house` is read as an integer, 1 unless given.
read_house! : {} => [Kept, LeftOut]
read_house! = |{}| {
	given = Shale.arg!("house", "1")
	match integer_of(given) {
		Ok(0) => LeftOut
		Ok(1) => Kept
		Ok(other) => {
			Shale.fail!("house must be 1 (the default) or 0, not ${other.to_str()}")
			Kept
		}
		Err(NotAnInteger) => {
			Shale.fail!("`arg`: house=${given} is not an integer, and its default is one")
			Kept
		}
	}
}

## A launch value read as an integer, as Shale's `arg` reads one whose
## default is: digits, a `-` before them or not.
integer_of : Str -> Try(I64, [NotAnInteger])
integer_of = |text| {
	bytes = text.to_utf8()
	digits = match bytes {
		['-', .. as rest] => rest
		_ => bytes
	}
	if digits.is_empty() or !(digits.all(Text.is_digit)) {
		return Err(NotAnInteger)
	}
	value = digits.fold(0, |sum, digit| sum * 10 + (digit - '0').to_i64())
	if bytes.first() == Ok('-') {
		Ok(-value)
	} else {
		Ok(value)
	}
}

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale):
## the first copy survives a cut output, and a gate reads the last line.
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, finding_lines| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(finding_lines.is_empty()) {
		for line in finding_lines {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

## After the findings: the files that didn't parse, and those no root of the
## types reaches (judged without them), named, then a stop
## (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale's `fail_if_refused`).
fail_if_refused! : List(Str), List(Str) => {}
fail_if_refused! = |refused, unreached| {
	if !(refused.is_empty()) or !(unreached.is_empty()) {
		for refusal in refused {
			Shale.print!("refused: ${refusal}")
		}
		for missed in unreached {
			Shale.print!(missed)
		}
		var $why = []
		if !(refused.is_empty()) {
			$why = $why.append("roc-ast refused ${refused.len().to_str()} files (named above), which have no tree to judge")
		}
		if !(unreached.is_empty()) {
			$why = $why.append("${unreached.len().to_str()} files (named above) are reached by no root of the types, so were judged without them")
		}
		Shale.fail!("hunt_names: ${Str.join_with($why, "; ")}; every other file was judged")
	}
}

cookbook/roc/hunt_names/DocNames.roc, 399 lines

## What hunt_names' `stale_doc_name` reads (the Shale original's
## doc_names.shale): the names a file's comment lines put in backticks, and whether each still
## names something in the file, the modules it imports, or the module a
## `Module.name` names. Only a name a reader can't take for a prose word is
## judged: one of two words or more (`two_opt`), or a module's member
## (`Route.two_opt`). A name cited from another language or library, or
## with a possessive before it, is another's. Reading a module beside the
## file that the run didn't parse is an effect, so this module has them.
import pf.Shale
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

DocNames := [].{

	## What the run has read of names: the self-test's own (`known`), each
	## module's by its name, each file's by its path (`Unread` for one that
	## couldn't be), and the sources a citation names.
	Seen : {
		known : Set(Str),
		by_module : Dict(Str, Set(Str)),
		by_path : Dict(Str, [Read(Set(Str)), Unread]),
		sources : Set(Str),
	}

	## A parsed file, its lines and its tree.
	FileRead : { path : Str, nodes : List(Tree.Node), source_lines : List(Str) }

	## The names the parsed files hold, by module and by path.
	seen_of : List(DocNames.FileRead), Set(Str), Set(Str) -> DocNames.Seen
	seen_of = |files, known, sources| {
		var $by_module = Dict.empty()
		var $by_path = Dict.empty()
		for file in files {
			module_named = Tree.module_name(file.path)
			own = names_in_tree(file.nodes)
			$by_module = $by_module.insert(module_named, ($by_module.get(module_named) ?? Set.empty()).union(own))
			$by_path = $by_path.insert(file.path, Read(own))
		}
		{ known, by_module: $by_module, by_path: $by_path, sources }
	}

	## Each backticked name in a comment of each file that names nothing
	## there, once a line, file by file.
	findings! : List(DocNames.FileRead), DocNames.Seen => List(Finding)
	findings! = |files, seen_before| {
		var $seen = seen_before
		var $found = []
		for file in files {
			judged = file_findings!(file, $seen)
			$seen = judged.seen
			$found = $found.concat(judged.found)
		}
		$found
	}
}

## A backticked name: its line, its module (`""` for a bare name), the name,
## and whether a possessive or a cited source says it is another's.
