check_boundaries

Whether each function's boundary earns its keep and each parameter is really one, from Roc's own parse trees across a tree: a one-caller wrapper, a parameter every call fills with the same literal, a constant written as a function, dead code, alike branches and, with the types, a Bool flag passed as a literal.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.exists!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.print!, Shale.read!, Shale.real!, Shale.roc_tree!, Shale.run!.
Roc: 1,587 lines in 7 files. Shale original: 830 lines, plus 497 lines in the 5 libraries it loads, which other recipes share.

Roc

It also imports Bytes, Finding, Forest, Headers, RocTypes, Text, Tree from the shared Roc library.

cookbook/roc/check_boundaries/check_boundaries.roc, 283 lines

## check_boundaries, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md):
## whether each function's boundary earns its keep, and whether each of its
## parameters is really a parameter. Its launcher,
## cookbook/roc/check_boundaries.shale, is how it is run, and its header says
## the checks (`single`, `fixed`, `entry`, `constant`, `dead`, `unused_api`,
## `same_branches`, and `bool_param` under the types) and the arguments.
## check_goldens.shale, beside this, holds its output to its goldens, line
## for line.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/check_boundaries.shale glob='app/**/*.roc'
##   shale cookbook:roc/check_boundaries.shale self_test=1
##
## This root reads the arguments (`Shale.arg!`), globs the files
## (`Shale.glob!`), gathers the types (Types, through `Shale.run!`), has Roc's
## parser read the files (`Shale.roc_tree!`) and each package's main.roc
## (`Shale.read!`), and prints the verdict (`Shale.print!`, `Shale.fail!`).
## Its modules are beside it: the functions (Functions), what reaches them
## (References), the source texts compared (Source), the checks (Checks),
## Types and SelfTest; Forest, Tree, Text, Headers, Bytes, Finding and RocTypes
## are the cookbook's Roc library, cookbook/roc/lib/.
## budget: steps=400000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 output_bytes=8000000 programs=100 roc_cpu_ms=60000
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import Checks
import lib.Finding
import lib.Forest
import Functions
import lib.Headers
import References
import lib.RocTypes
import SelfTest
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree
import Types

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	asked = read_asked!({})
	client_files = globbed!(asked.clients)
	client_set = Set.from_list(globbed!(asked.clients))
	checked_files = globbed!(asked.glob).drop_if(|path| client_set.contains(path))
	checked = Set.from_list(checked_files)
	test_paths = Set.from_list(globbed!(asked.tests))
	types = if asked.use_types {
		roc = Types.roc_bin!("check_boundaries", asked.self_test)
		exempt = if asked.self_test {
			Set.from_list(checked_files.drop_if(|path| path.starts_with(SelfTest.typed_plants)))
		} else {
			Set.empty()
		}
		Types.gather!({ who: "check_boundaries", kind: Patterns, root: asked.root, roc, paths: checked_files, exempt })
	} else {
		{ typing: RocTypes.no_types, unreached: [] }
	}
	read = read_files!(checked_files.concat(client_files))
	forest = Forest.join(read.parsed)
	ancestry = Functions.ancestry(forest)
	limits = { ways: asked.ways, nodes: asked.nodes }
	defined = Functions.read(forest, ancestry, { checked, lines_of: read.lines_of, limits })
	tallies = References.tally(forest, ancestry, defined, test_paths)
	clients_read = if client_files.is_empty() {
		""
	} else {
		" and ${client_files.len().to_str()} clients"
	}
	judging = {
		forest,
		lines_of: read.lines_of,
		defined,
		tallies,
		checked,
		headers: read.headers,
		exposed_modules: exposed_modules!(checked_files),
		typing: types.typing,
		files_read: " in the ${checked_files.len().to_str()} files read${clients_read}",
		is_dead_by_production: asked.is_dead_by_production,
	}
	is_house_off = read_house_is_off!({})
	is_reported = |finding| {
		is_house = is_house_off and finding.check == "single"
		is_unjudged_plant = asked.self_test and (finding.check == "dead" or finding.check == "unused_api") and !(finding.path.starts_with(SelfTest.dead_plants))
		!(is_house) and !(is_unjudged_plant)
	}
	findings = Checks.judge(judging).keep_if(is_reported)
	for finding in findings {
		Shale.print!(Finding.line_of(finding))
	}
	house_note = if is_house_off {
		"; left out as house style: single"
	} else {
		""
	}
	files_said = "${checked_files.len().to_str()} files${clients_read}, ${defined.by_key.len().to_str()} functions"
	Shale.print!("check_boundaries (Roc): ${files_said}; ${Finding.counts_of(findings, checks)}${house_note}")
	fail_if_refused!(read.refused, types.unreached)
	if asked.self_test {
		SelfTest.run!({ paths: checked_files, clients: client_files, test_count: test_paths.len(), findings }, checks)
	}
}

## The checks, in the order the summary counts them.
checks : List(Str)
checks = ["single", "fixed", "entry", "constant", "bool_param", "dead", "unused_api", "same_branches"]

## The arguments, read and refused in the Shale original's order. The
## self-test reads every plant, those under `dead/clients/` as clients and
## those under `dead/gates/` as tests, with the types under
## `typed/QuietApp.roc` and `test_reach=dead`.
read_asked! : {} => {
	self_test : Bool,
	glob : Str,
	ways : I64,
	nodes : I64,
	use_types : Bool,
	root : Str,
	clients : Str,
	tests : Str,
	is_dead_by_production : Bool,
}
read_asked! = |{}| {
	self_test = Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1"
	plants = SelfTest.plants
	glob_asked = Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc")
	ways = integer_of!("ways", Shale.arg!("ways", "2"))
	nodes = integer_of!("nodes", Shale.arg!("nodes", "24"))
	types_asked = Shale.arg!("types", "0")
	if types_asked != "0" and types_asked != "1" {
		Shale.fail!("check_boundaries: types must be 0 (the default) or 1, not ${types_asked}")
	}
	root_asked = Shale.arg!("root", "")
	clients_asked = Shale.arg!("clients", "")
	tests_asked = Shale.arg!("tests", "")
	reach = Shale.arg!("test_reach", "keeps")
	if reach != "keeps" and reach != "dead" {
		Shale.fail!("check_boundaries: test_reach must be keeps (the default) or dead, not ${reach}")
	}
	if self_test {
		{
			self_test,
			glob: "${plants}**/*.roc",
			ways,
			nodes,
			use_types: Bool.True,
			root: "${SelfTest.typed_plants}QuietApp.roc",
			clients: "${SelfTest.dead_plants}clients/*.roc",
			tests: "${SelfTest.dead_plants}gates/*.roc",
			is_dead_by_production: Bool.True,
		}
	} else {
		{
			self_test,
			glob: glob_asked,
			ways,
			nodes,
			use_types: types_asked == "1",
			root: root_asked,
			clients: clients_asked,
			tests: tests_asked,
			is_dead_by_production: reach == "dead",
		}
	}
}

## The argument `name`, given as `given`, read as an integer, as Shale's
## `arg` reads one whose default is an integer. Each is read by its own
## `Shale.arg!`, which the launcher finds by name.
integer_of! : Str, Str => I64
integer_of! = |name, given|
	match I64.from_str(given) {
		Ok(number) => number
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("`arg`: ${name}=${given} is not an integer, and its default is one")
			0
		}
	}

## Whether `house=0` leaves the house style, `single`, out
## (cookbook/roc/house.shale).
read_house_is_off! : {} => Bool
read_house_is_off! = |{}| {
	house = integer_of!("house", Shale.arg!("house", "1"))
	if house != 0 and house != 1 {
		Shale.fail!("house must be 1 (the default) or 0, not ${house.to_str()}")
	}
	house == 0
}

## The files the globs match, a list separated by commas, each file as
## often as a glob matches it.
globbed! : Str => List(Str)
globbed! = |globs| {
	var $paths = []
	for named in globs.split_on(",") {
		pattern = Text.trim(named)
		if pattern != "" {
			$paths = $paths.concat(Shale.glob!(pattern))
		}
	}
	$paths
}

## The files Roc's parser reads, with each file's lines and header names,
## and a `path: reason` line for each it refuses.
read_files! : List(Str) => {
	parsed : List({ path : Str, nodes : List(Tree.Node) }),
	lines_of : Dict(Str, List(Str)),
	headers : Dict(Str, { dictated : Set(Str), exposed : Set(Str) }),
	refused : List(Str),
}
read_files! = |paths| {
	var $parsed = []
	var $lines_of = Dict.empty()
	var $headers = Dict.empty()
	var $refused = []
	for file in Shale.roc_tree!(paths) {
		if file.err == "" {
			text = match Shale.read!(file.path) {
				Found(found) => found
				Missing => {
					Shale.fail!("check_boundaries: ${file.path} went missing while it was read")
					""
				}
			}
			names = Headers.header_names(file.nodes)
			$parsed = $parsed.append({ path: file.path, nodes: file.nodes })
			$lines_of = $lines_of.insert(file.path, text.split_on("\n"))
			$headers = $headers.insert(file.path, { dictated: Set.from_list(names.dictated), exposed: Set.from_list(names.exposed) })
		} else if file.err.starts_with(file.path) {
			$refused = $refused.append(file.err)
		} else {
			$refused = $refused.append("${file.path}: ${file.err}")
		}
	}
	{ parsed: $parsed, lines_of: $lines_of, headers: $headers, refused: $refused }
}

## The modules each checked file's folder's main.roc exposes, when it is a
## package's or a platform's (cookbook/roc/lib/'s `Headers.exposed_by`), by
## folder.
exposed_modules! : List(Str) => Dict(Str, List(Str))
exposed_modules! = |paths| {
	var $by_folder = Dict.empty()
	for path in paths {
		folder = Text.dirname(path)
		if !($by_folder.contains(folder)) {
			main = if folder == "" or folder == "." {
				"main.roc"
			} else {
				"${folder}/main.roc"
			}
			exposed = match Shale.read!(main) {
				Found(text) => Headers.exposed_by(text).modules
				Missing => []
			}
			$by_folder = $by_folder.insert(folder, exposed)
		}
	}
	$by_folder
}

## After the summary: the files that didn't parse, and those no root of the
## types reaches (judged without them), named, then a stop
## (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale's `fail_if_refused`).
fail_if_refused! : List(Str), List(Str) => {}
fail_if_refused! = |refused, unreached| {
	if !(refused.is_empty()) or !(unreached.is_empty()) {
		for refusal in refused {
			Shale.print!("refused: ${refusal}")
		}
		for missed in unreached {
			Shale.print!(missed)
		}
		var $why = []
		if !(refused.is_empty()) {
			$why = $why.append("roc-ast refused ${refused.len().to_str()} files (named above), which have no tree to judge")
		}
		if !(unreached.is_empty()) {
			$why = $why.append("${unreached.len().to_str()} files (named above) are reached by no root of the types, so were judged without them")
		}
		Shale.fail!("check_boundaries: ${Str.join_with($why, "; ")}; every other file was judged")
	}
}

cookbook/roc/check_boundaries/Checks.roc, 264 lines

## The checks of check_boundaries, each function judged in the order of its
## key, then each `if`: `dead` or `unused_api`, `single`, `fixed` or
## `entry`, `constant`, `bool_param` and `same_branches`. The launcher's
## header says each rule.
import lib.Finding
import lib.Forest
import lib.Headers
import lib.RocTypes
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree
import Functions
import References
import Source

Checks := [].{

	## What the checks read: the forest and each file's lines; the
	## functions and their tallies; the checked files; each file's header
	## names; the modules each folder's main.roc exposes; the types; the
	## words that end a finding's count of the files read; and whether only a
	## production call keeps a member out of `dead`.
	Judging : {
		forest : Forest,
		lines_of : Dict(Str, List(Str)),
		defined : Functions.Defined,
		tallies : List(References.Tally),
		checked : Set(Str),
		headers : Dict(Str, { dictated : Set(Str), exposed : Set(Str) }),
		exposed_modules : Dict(Str, List(Str)),
		typing : RocTypes.Typing,
		files_read : Str,
		is_dead_by_production : Bool,
	}

	## Every finding, in the order the Shale original reported them.
	judge : Checks.Judging -> List(Finding)
	judge = |judging| {
		defined = judging.defined
		order = |first, second| Text.byte_order(Functions.at(defined, first).key, Functions.at(defined, second).key)
		var $places = []
		$index : U64
		var $index = 0
		for _ in defined.functions {
			$places = $places.append($index)
			$index = $index + 1
		}
		var $findings = []
		for place in $places.sort_with(order) {
			function = Functions.at(defined, place)
			counted = judging.tallies.get(place) ?? crash "check_boundaries: a function with no tally"
			$findings = $findings.concat(judge_function(judging, function, counted))
		}
		$findings.concat(same_branches(judging))
	}
}

## A function and what reaches it.
Judged : { function : Functions.Function, counted : References.Tally }

judge_function : Checks.Judging, Functions.Function, References.Tally -> List(Finding)
judge_function = |judging, function, counted| {
	judged = { function, counted }
	is_test = References.is_test_file(function.path)
	is_judged = !(counted.is_ambiguous) and !(is_test)
	at = |check, what| { path: function.path, line: function.line, check, what }
	name = display_name(function)
	read = judging.files_read
	var $findings = []
	if !(is_test) and has_no_caller(judging, judged) and !(is_called_from_outside(judging, function)) {
		$findings = $findings.append(
			if is_library_api(judging, function) {
				at("unused_api", "`${name}` is exposed, and nothing${read} calls or tests it: API with no user here, or left behind?")
			} else if counted.expect_refs + counted.test_refs > 0 {
				at("dead", "`${name}` has no production caller${read}, only an expect or a test: delete it with its tests, or say who calls it")
			} else {
				at("dead", "`${name}` has no caller${read}, and no expect or test reaches it: delete it, or say who calls it")
			},
		)
	}
	if is_judged and reads_better_inline(judged) {
		said = "`${name}` (${function.size}) has one caller${read}, ${counted.first_prod_caller}, and no expect, test or doc"
		$findings = $findings.append(at("single", "${said}: read it inline there, or say why it stands alone"))
	}
	if is_judged and counted.prod_calls.len() >= 2 and counted.value_refs == 0 {
		$findings = $findings.concat(fixed_slots(judging, judged))
	}
	if function.takes_empty_record_alone and !(function.name.contains("!")) and !(is_test) and function.doc_lines == 0 {
		effect = "a constant (`${function.name} = ...`), or a `!` if it has an effect"
		$findings = $findings.append(at("constant", "`${name}` takes `{}` alone and names no effect, so it gives the same value every call: ${effect}"))
	}
	if is_judged and function.params.len() > 1 and judging.typing.real.contains(function.path) {
		$findings = $findings.concat(bool_params(judging, judged))
	}
	$findings
}

## The slots the production calls agree on with a literal: `fixed` if the
## function's own calls agree with them too, `entry` if they vary it.
fixed_slots : Checks.Judging, Judged -> List(Finding)
fixed_slots = |judging, judged| {
	function = judged.function
	counted = judged.counted
	outside = Source.agreed(judging.lines_of, judging.forest, counted.prod_calls)
	every = Source.agreed(judging.lines_of, judging.forest, counted.prod_calls.concat(counted.self_calls))
	own = if counted.self_calls.is_empty() {
		""
	} else {
		" and ${counted.self_calls.len().to_str()} of its own"
	}
	name = display_name(function)
	read = judging.files_read
	at = |check, what| { path: function.path, line: function.line, check, what }
	var $findings = []
	for slot in Text.sort_bytewise(outside.keys()) {
		match outside.get(slot) {
			Ok(Agreed(text)) if Source.is_literal(text) => {
				said = "`${name}`'s argument ${slot} is `${text}` in all ${counted.prod_calls.len().to_str()} production calls"
				match every.get(slot) {
					Ok(Agreed(_)) =>
						if !(is_library_api(judging, function)) {
							$findings = $findings.append(at("fixed", "${said}${own}${read}: no parameter, or an entry function that takes only what varies"))
						}
					_ => {
						varies = "its own calls vary it: an entry function that takes only what varies and passes `${text}` itself, its one outside call"
						$findings = $findings.append(at("entry", "${said}${read}, and ${varies}"))
					}
				}
			}
			_ => {}
		}
	}
	$findings
}

## Each `Bool` parameter, by the checker's type, that some call passes a
## literal: every call counts, a test's and the function's own too.
bool_params : Checks.Judging, Judged -> List(Finding)
bool_params = |judging, judged| {
	function = judged.function
	counted = judged.counted
	every = counted.prod_calls.concat(counted.self_calls).concat(counted.test_calls)
	var $findings = []
	$number : U64
	var $number = 0
	for param in function.params {
		$number = $number + 1
		node = Forest.node(judging.forest, param)
		is_bool = node.kind == "p-ident" and RocTypes.type_at(judging.typing, function.path, node) == Ok("Bool")
		if is_bool {
			var $literal_calls = []
			for call in every {
				text = Source.argument_texts(judging.lines_of, judging.forest, call).get($number.to_str()) ?? ""
				if bool_literals.contains(text) {
					$literal_calls = $literal_calls.append("${call.path}:${call.line.to_str()} `${text}`")
				}
			}
			if !($literal_calls.is_empty()) {
				more = if $literal_calls.len() > 3 {
					", ..."
				} else {
					""
				}
				shown = "${Str.join_with($literal_calls.take_first(3), ", ")}${more}"
				counts = "at ${$literal_calls.len().to_str()} of its ${every.len().to_str()} calls (${shown})"
				param_said = "`${display_name(function)}`'s parameter ${$number.to_str()}, `${Tree.attribute(node, "raw")}`"
				tag = "a flag a caller passes is a tag, named for what it means (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md)"
				what = "${param_said}, is a `Bool` (the checker's type) passed as a literal ${counts}: ${tag}"
				$findings = $findings.append({ path: function.path, line: function.line, check: "bool_param", what })
			}
		}
	}
	$findings
}

## Each `if` in a checked file but a test whose two branches are the same
## text, braces aside.
same_branches : Checks.Judging -> List(Finding)
same_branches = |judging| {
	forest = judging.forest
	var $findings = []
	$at : U64
	var $at = 1
	while $at <= Forest.count(forest) {
		path = Forest.path(forest, $at)
		is_judged = !(References.is_test_file(path)) and judging.checked.contains(path)
		if Forest.kind(forest, $at) == "e-if-then-else" and is_judged and Forest.kids(forest, $at).len() == 3 {
			shown = Source.branch_text(judging.lines_of, forest, Forest.kid(forest, $at, 2))
			if shown != "?" and shown == Source.branch_text(judging.lines_of, forest, Forest.kid(forest, $at, 3)) {
				cut = Str.from_utf8_lossy(shown.to_utf8().take_first(40))
				what = "both branches of this `if` are `${cut}`: the condition decides nothing"
				$findings = $findings.append({ path, line: Forest.node(forest, $at).line, check: "same_branches", what })
			}
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	$findings
}

## The pinned Roc defines `Bool := [False, True]`.
bool_literals : Set(Str)
bool_literals = Set.from_list(["Bool.True", "Bool.False", "True", "False"])

display_name : Functions.Function -> Str
display_name = |function|
	if function.owner.starts_with("@") {
		function.name
	} else {
		"${function.owner}.${function.name}"
	}

## A function that would read better inline at its one production call: a
## small wrapper with no other reference, no doc, no recursion and not a
## question.
reads_better_inline : Judged -> Bool
reads_better_inline = |judged| {
	counted = judged.counted
	function = judged.function
	is_question = function.name.starts_with("is_") or function.name.starts_with("has_")
	is_alone = counted.prod_refs == 1 and counted.value_refs == 0 and counted.expect_refs == 0 and counted.test_refs == 0
	is_alone and function.doc_lines == 0 and function.is_wrapper and !(counted.is_recursive) and !(counted.is_entry) and !(is_question)
}

## Whether a function is part of a library's API: a name its own `module`
## header exposes, or a module type's member in a file under a `lib/`
## folder or in a module its package or platform exposes.
is_library_api : Checks.Judging, Functions.Function -> Bool
is_library_api = |judging, function| {
	path = function.path
	header = judging.headers.get(path) ?? { dictated: Set.empty(), exposed: Set.empty() }
	if header.exposed.contains(function.name) {
		Bool.True
	} else if function.owner.starts_with("@") {
		Bool.False
	} else if path.starts_with("lib/") or path.contains("/lib/") or path.contains(":lib/") {
		Bool.True
	} else {
		(judging.exposed_modules.get(Text.dirname(path)) ?? []).contains(Tree.module_name(path))
	}
}

## A function something outside the files calls: what its header dictates,
## or a member Roc calls by name.
is_called_from_outside : Checks.Judging, Functions.Function -> Bool
is_called_from_outside = |judging, function|
	if function.owner.starts_with("@") {
		header = judging.headers.get(function.path) ?? { dictated: Set.empty(), exposed: Set.empty() }
		header.dictated.contains(function.name)
	} else {
		Headers.language_fixed_names.contains(function.name)
	}

## Whether nothing reaches a function. A test of a library's API is a user
## of it, so `unused_api` keeps it.
has_no_caller : Checks.Judging, Judged -> Bool
has_no_caller = |judging, judged| {
	counted = judged.counted
	is_member = !(judged.function.owner.starts_with("@"))
	unreached = counted.prod_refs == 0 and !(counted.is_mentioned)
	if judging.is_dead_by_production and is_member and !(is_library_api(judging, judged.function)) {
		unreached
	} else {
		unreached and counted.expect_refs == 0 and counted.test_refs == 0
	}
}

cookbook/roc/check_boundaries/Functions.roc, 325 lines

## The first pass of check_boundaries: what each node's ancestors say, and
## each function defined at a file's top level or as a module type's member,
## with what the checks read of its body, its `##` doc and its parameters.
import lib.Forest
import lib.Text

Functions := [].{

	## What each node's ancestors say, by place counted from 1: `top`, every
	## ancestor is a file, its statements, a module type or its block of
	## members; `owner`, the name of the nearest module type around it, or
	## `""`; `enclosing`, the name of the outermost declaration around it, or
	## `?`; `in_expect`, it is inside an `expect`.
	Ancestry : {
		top : List(Bool),
		owner : List(Str),
		enclosing : List(Str),
		in_expect : List(Bool),
	}

	## A function: its key is `owner|name`, the owner its module type's name
	## or `@path` for a file's own; `line` and `end_line` its definition's;
	## whether its body is small enough for `single` to call it a wrapper, and
	## its size in words; the `##` lines above it; whether it takes `{}`
	## alone; and its parameter patterns' places.
	Function : {
		key : Str,
		path : Str,
		owner : Str,
		name : Str,
		line : U64,
		end_line : U64,
		is_wrapper : Bool,
		size : Str,
		doc_lines : U64,
		takes_empty_record_alone : Bool,
		params : List(U64),
	}

	## The functions found, each key's place among them, and the keys of the
	## module types' members by name, a key listed again when its name is
	## declared again.
	Defined : {
		functions : List(Functions.Function),
		by_key : Dict(Str, U64),
		member_keys : Dict(Str, List(Str)),
	}

	## The most ways and nodes in a body `single` still calls a wrapper.
	Limits : { ways : I64, nodes : I64 }

	## Each node's ancestry, worked out from its parent's, which comes
	## before it in the forest.
	ancestry : Forest -> Functions.Ancestry
	ancestry = |forest| {
		var $top = []
		var $owner = []
		var $enclosing = []
		var $in_expect = []
		$at : U64
		var $at = 1
		while $at <= Forest.count(forest) {
			above = Forest.parent(forest, $at)
			if above == 0 {
				$top = $top.append(Bool.True)
				$owner = $owner.append("")
				$enclosing = $enclosing.append("?")
				$in_expect = $in_expect.append(Bool.False)
			} else {
				kind = Forest.kind(forest, above)
				is_top = Functions.flag_at($top, above) and top_level_kinds.contains(kind)
				$top = $top.append(is_top)
				owner = if kind == "s-type-decl" {
					type_decl_name(forest, above)
				} else {
					Functions.text_at($owner, above)
				}
				$owner = $owner.append(owner)
				enclosing = enclosing_name(forest, above, Functions.text_at($enclosing, above))
				$enclosing = $enclosing.append(enclosing)
				in_expect = Functions.flag_at($in_expect, above) or kind == "s-expect"
				$in_expect = $in_expect.append(in_expect)
			}
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		{ top: $top, owner: $owner, enclosing: $enclosing, in_expect: $in_expect }
	}

	## The functions declared in the checked files, `lines_of` each file's
	## lines. A key declared twice keeps its last declaration.
	read : Forest, Functions.Ancestry, { checked : Set(Str), lines_of : Dict(Str, List(Str)), limits : Functions.Limits } -> Functions.Defined
	read = |forest, ancestors, given| {
		var $functions = []
		var $by_key = Dict.empty()
		var $member_keys = Dict.empty()
		$at : U64
		var $at = 1
		while $at <= Forest.count(forest) {
			name_at = Forest.kid(forest, $at, 1)
			lambda = Forest.kid(forest, $at, 2)
			path = Forest.path(forest, $at)
			is_declared = Forest.kind(forest, $at) == "s-decl" and lambda != 0
			is_function = is_declared and Forest.kind(forest, name_at) == "p-ident" and Forest.kind(forest, lambda) == "e-lambda"
			if is_function and Functions.flag_at(ancestors.top, $at) and given.checked.contains(path) {
				owned_by = Functions.text_at(ancestors.owner, $at)
				owner = if owned_by != "" {
					owned_by
				} else {
					"@${path}"
				}
				node = Forest.node(forest, $at)
				name = Forest.raw(forest, name_at)
				key = "${owner}|${name}"
				body = body_measure(forest, lambda, given.limits)
				function = {
					key,
					path,
					owner,
					name,
					line: node.line,
					end_line: node.end_line,
					is_wrapper: body.is_wrapper,
					size: body.size,
					doc_lines: doc_comment_lines(given.lines_of.get(path) ?? [], name, node.line),
					takes_empty_record_alone: takes_empty_record_alone(forest, $at, name),
					params: lambda_params(forest, lambda),
				}
				match $by_key.get(key) {
					Ok(index) => {
						$functions = $functions.set(index, function) ?? crash "check_boundaries: a key past the functions"
					}
					Err(_) => {
						$by_key = $by_key.insert(key, $functions.len())
						$functions = $functions.append(function)
					}
				}
				if !(owner.starts_with("@")) {
					keys = $member_keys.get(name) ?? []
					$member_keys = $member_keys.insert(name, keys.append(key))
				}
			}
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		{ functions: $functions, by_key: $by_key, member_keys: $member_keys }
	}

	## The function at a place among them.
	at : Functions.Defined, U64 -> Functions.Function
	at = |defined, index| defined.functions.get(index) ?? crash "check_boundaries: no function ${index.to_str()}"

	## A node's flag, by its place counted from 1.
	flag_at : List(Bool), U64 -> Bool
	flag_at = |flags, place| flags.get(place - 1) ?? Bool.False

	## A node's text, by its place counted from 1.
	text_at : List(Str), U64 -> Str
	text_at = |texts, place| texts.get(place - 1) ?? ""
}

## The kinds of node that can hold a top-level function: a file, its
## statements, a module type's declaration, and the block of its members.
top_level_kinds : Set(Str)
top_level_kinds = Set.from_list(["file", "statements", "s-type-decl", "associated"])

## The name in the header of the module type declared at `at`.
type_decl_name : Forest, U64 -> Str
type_decl_name = |forest, at| {
	header = Forest.kid(forest, at, 1)
	if header == 0 {
		""
	} else {
		Forest.name(forest, header)
	}
}

## The outermost declaration's name below the node at `above`, whose own is
## `was`: a declaration of a plain name is the first to give one.
enclosing_name : Forest, U64, Str -> Str
enclosing_name = |forest, above, was| {
	pattern = Forest.kid(forest, above, 1)
	is_named = pattern != 0 and Forest.kind(forest, pattern) == "p-ident"
	if was == "?" and Forest.kind(forest, above) == "s-decl" and is_named {
		Forest.raw(forest, pattern)
	} else {
		was
	}
}

## How many `##` lines stand just above the function defined at `line`, or
## above its annotation (`name : ...`, on one line or several) if it has one.
doc_comment_lines : List(Str), Str, U64 -> U64
doc_comment_lines = |source_lines, name, line| {
	trimmed_at = |number| Text.trim(source_lines.get(number - 1) ?? "")
	$top : U64
	var $top = line - 1
	$up : U64
	var $up = $top
	while $up >= 1 and $up + 12 > line and trimmed_at($up) != "" and !(trimmed_at($up).starts_with("#")) {
		if trimmed_at($up).starts_with("${name} :") {
			$top = $up - 1
		}
		$up = $up - 1
	}
	$count : U64
	var $count = 0
	while $top >= 1 and trimmed_at($top).starts_with("##") {
		$count = $count + 1
		$top = $top - 1
	}
	$count
}

## Whether the body of the lambda at `lambda` is small enough for `single` to
## call it a wrapper, and its size in words for the finding. A wrapper's body
## is one statement: a block of one, or an expression. Its size counts
## syntax-tree nodes, so the layout of its lines changes nothing. It has one
## way through, and one more for each `if` and each `match` arm past the
## first, so only a two-way choice reads as a wrapper.
body_measure : Forest, U64, Functions.Limits -> { is_wrapper : Bool, size : Str }
body_measure = |forest, lambda, limits| {
	outer = Forest.kids(forest, lambda).last() ?? crash "check_boundaries: a lambda with no body"
	var $body = outer
	if Forest.kind(forest, outer) == "e-block" {
		var $statements = []
		for kid in Forest.kids(forest, outer) {
			if Forest.kind(forest, kid) == "statements" {
				$statements = Forest.kids(forest, kid)
			}
		}
		if $statements.len() != 1 {
			return { is_wrapper: Bool.False, size: "${$statements.len().to_str()} statements" }
		}
		$body = $statements.first() ?? outer
	}
	last = Forest.last_descendant(forest, $body)
	$ways : I64
	var $ways = 1
	$place : U64
	var $place = $body
	while $place <= last {
		kind = Forest.kind(forest, $place)
		if kind == "e-if-then-else" {
			$ways = $ways + 1
		}
		if kind == "branches" {
			$ways = $ways + Forest.kids(forest, $place).len().to_i64_wrap() - 1
		}
		$place = $place + 1
	}
	count = (last - $body + 1).to_i64_wrap()
	is_small = count <= limits.nodes
	if $ways > 1 {
		{ is_wrapper: is_small and $ways <= limits.ways, size: "a decision of ${$ways.to_str()} ways, ${count.to_str()} nodes" }
	} else {
		{ is_wrapper: is_small, size: "one expression of ${count.to_str()} nodes" }
	}
}

## Whether the subtree at `at` holds a node of `kind`.
holds_kind : Forest, U64, Str -> Bool
holds_kind = |forest, at, kind| {
	last = Forest.last_descendant(forest, at)
	var $place = at
	while $place <= last {
		if Forest.kind(forest, $place) == kind {
			return Bool.True
		}
		$place = $place + 1
	}
	Bool.False
}

## The function type of the annotation just before the declaration at
## `decl`, when that annotation is for `name`, or 0.
annotation_function_type : Forest, U64, Str -> U64
annotation_function_type = |forest, decl, name| {
	above = Forest.parent(forest, decl)
	if above == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	siblings = Forest.kids(forest, above)
	before = match siblings.find_first_index(|kid| kid == decl) {
		Ok(index) if index > 0 => siblings.get(index - 1) ?? 0
		_ => 0
	}
	if before == 0 or Forest.kind(forest, before) != "s-type-anno" or Forest.name(forest, before) != name {
		0
	} else {
		signature = Forest.kid(forest, before, 1)
		if signature != 0 and Forest.kind(forest, signature) == "ty-fn" {
			signature
		} else {
			0
		}
	}
}

## Whether the function declared at `decl` takes `{}` alone, by its lambda's
## one pattern or its annotation's one argument, and could be a constant: an
## annotated return type holding a type variable rules that out.
takes_empty_record_alone : Forest, U64, Str -> Bool
takes_empty_record_alone = |forest, decl, name| {
	lambda = Forest.kid(forest, decl, 2)
	is_empty_record = |at, kind| at != 0 and Forest.kind(forest, at) == kind and Forest.kids(forest, at).is_empty()
	by_pattern = Forest.kids(forest, lambda).any(
		|kid| Forest.kind(forest, kid) == "args" and Forest.kids(forest, kid).len() == 1 and is_empty_record(Forest.kid(forest, kid, 1), "p-record"),
	)
	fn_type = annotation_function_type(forest, decl, name)
	if fn_type == 0 {
		by_pattern
	} else {
		parts = Forest.kids(forest, fn_type)
		by_type = parts.len() == 2 and is_empty_record(parts.first() ?? 0, "ty-record")
		result = parts.last() ?? 0
		(by_pattern or by_type) and (result == 0 or !(holds_kind(forest, result, "ty-var")))
	}
}

## The parameter patterns of the lambda at `lambda`, by position.
lambda_params : Forest, U64 -> List(U64)
lambda_params = |forest, lambda|
	match Forest.kids(forest, lambda).find_first(|kid| Forest.kind(forest, kid) == "args") {
		Ok(args) => Forest.kids(forest, args)
		Err(_) => []
	}

cookbook/roc/check_boundaries/References.roc, 358 lines

## The second pass of check_boundaries: every reference to a function the
## checked files declare, with the call it heads, tallied by function. A
## reference is a function's bare name in the file that defines it,
## `Type.name` anywhere (the type read through the file's `import ... as`),
## a method call `.name(...)`, which counts for every member of that name, or
## a record's shorthand (`{ helper }`). A reference within the function's own
## lines makes it recursive; any other is a test file's, an `expect`'s or
## production's. A name that may reach a member by a way this cannot follow
## (an alias of a type, a name an import exposes) is a mention, which keeps
## every member of that name out of `dead`.
import lib.Forest
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree
import Functions

References := [].{

	## A call: the arguments' places, and an arrow or method call's receiver,
	## its first argument, or 0 for none.
	Call : { path : Str, line : U64, args : List(U64), receiver : U64 }

	## What reaches a function, by kind, in the order the forest holds them.
	Tally : {
		prod_refs : U64,
		value_refs : U64,
		expect_refs : U64,
		test_refs : U64,
		first_prod_caller : Str,
		prod_calls : List(References.Call),
		self_calls : List(References.Call),
		test_calls : List(References.Call),
		is_recursive : Bool,
		is_entry : Bool,
		is_ambiguous : Bool,
		is_mentioned : Bool,
	}

	## Each function's tally, by its place among the functions. `test_paths`
	## are the files `tests=` names: a reference from one of them to a
	## function outside them is a test's.
	tally : Forest, Functions.Ancestry, Functions.Defined, Set(Str) -> List(References.Tally)
	tally = |forest, ancestry, defined, test_paths| {
		found = references_of({ forest, ancestry, defined, aliases: import_aliases(forest) })
		sorted = found.events.sort_with(event_order)
		var $tallies = []
		$cursor : U64
		var $cursor = 0
		for function in defined.functions {
			index = $tallies.len()
			$end : U64
			var $end = $cursor
			while $end < sorted.len() and ((sorted.get($end) ?? crash "check_boundaries: no event").function == index) {
				$end = $end + 1
			}
			own = sorted.sublist({ start: $cursor, len: $end - $cursor })
			$cursor = $end
			counted = tally_of(function, own, test_paths)
			$tallies = $tallies.append({
				..counted,
				is_ambiguous: found.ambiguous.contains(index),
				is_mentioned: !(function.owner.starts_with("@")) and found.mentioned.contains(function.name),
			})
		}
		entries = entries_of(defined, $tallies)
		$tallies.map_with_index(|counted, index| { ..counted, is_entry: entries.contains(index) })
	}

	## Whether the file is a test of the rest: a name ending in `twin.roc`, a
	## file under a `twin/` or `test/` folder, or a spec app named for its
	## module followed by `Spec.roc` (`BlitSpec.roc`).
	is_test_file : Str -> Bool
	is_test_file = |path| {
		in_folder = path.contains("/twin/") or path.contains("/test/") or path.starts_with("test/") or path.starts_with("twin/")
		is_spec(Text.basename(path)) or path.ends_with("twin.roc") or in_folder
	}
}

## Where a reference is: its file and line, whether an `expect` holds it,
## and the declaration around it.
Reference : { path : Str, line : U64, in_expect : Bool, enclosing : Str }

## A reference to the function at `function` among them, the `seq`th found:
## the call it heads, or none when the function is passed as a value.
Event : { function : U64, seq : U64, reference : Reference, use : [Called(References.Call), AsValue] }

## What the pass reads: the forest, its ancestry, the functions, and the
## module each file's import aliases stand for, by `path|alias`.
Reading : { forest : Forest, ancestry : Functions.Ancestry, defined : Functions.Defined, aliases : Dict(Str, Str) }

## Each file's import aliases, `path|alias`, and the module each names.
import_aliases : Forest -> Dict(Str, Str)
import_aliases = |forest| {
	var $aliases = Dict.empty()
	$at : U64
	var $at = 1
	while $at <= Forest.count(forest) {
		if Forest.kind(forest, $at) == "s-import" {
			match Tree.find_attribute(Forest.node(forest, $at), "alias") {
				Ok(alias) => {
					$aliases = $aliases.insert("${Forest.path(forest, $at)}|${alias}", Tree.last_part(Forest.raw(forest, $at)))
				}
				Err(_) => {}
			}
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	$aliases
}

## Every reference in the forest, in its order; the functions a method call
## of a shared name reaches; and the names mentioned.
references_of : Reading -> { events : List(Event), ambiguous : Set(U64), mentioned : Set(Str) }
references_of = |reading| {
	forest = reading.forest
	var $events = []
	var $ambiguous = Set.empty()
	var $mentioned = Set.empty()
	$at : U64
	var $at = 1
	while $at <= Forest.count(forest) {
		kind = Forest.kind(forest, $at)
		parent_kind = Forest.kind_or_none(forest, Forest.parent(forest, $at))
		if kind == "e-method-call" {
			name = Str.from_utf8_lossy(Forest.attribute(forest, $at, "method").to_utf8().drop_first(1))
			if name != "" {
				call = method_call(forest, $at)
				keys = reading.defined.member_keys.get(name) ?? []
				for key in keys {
					index = reading.defined.by_key.get(key) ?? crash "check_boundaries: a member key with no function"
					$events = $events.append({ function: index, seq: $events.len(), reference: reference_at(reading, $at), use: Called(call) })
					if keys.len() > 1 {
						$ambiguous = $ambiguous.insert(index)
					}
				}
			}
		} else if kind == "e-ident" {
			name = Forest.raw(forest, $at)
			found = if name == "" {
				Err(NoFunction)
			} else {
				referenced(reading, $at, name)
			}
			match found {
				Ok(index) => {
					$events = $events.append({ function: index, seq: $events.len(), reference: reference_at(reading, $at), use: call_headed_by(forest, $at) })
				}
				Err(_) =>
					if name.contains(".") {
						$mentioned = $mentioned.insert(Tree.last_part(name))
					}
			}
		} else if kind == "field" and Forest.kids(forest, $at).is_empty() and parent_kind == "e-record" {
			# `{ helper }` names `helper` with no identifier node. The field has
			# no span, so its record says where it is.
			match referenced(reading, $at, Forest.attribute(forest, $at, "field")) {
				Ok(index) => {
					record = Forest.parent(forest, $at)
					$events = $events.append({ function: index, seq: $events.len(), reference: reference_at(reading, record), use: AsValue })
				}
				Err(_) => {}
			}
		} else if kind == "text" and parent_kind == "exposed-lower-ident" {
			match Tree.find_attribute(Forest.node(forest, $at), "value") {
				Ok(value) => {
					$mentioned = $mentioned.insert(value)
				}
				Err(_) => {}
			}
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	{ events: $events, ambiguous: $ambiguous, mentioned: $mentioned }
}

reference_at : Reading, U64 -> Reference
reference_at = |reading, at| {
	path = Forest.path(reading.forest, at)
	line = Forest.node(reading.forest, at).line
	in_expect = Functions.flag_at(reading.ancestry.in_expect, at)
	{ path, line, in_expect, enclosing: Functions.text_at(reading.ancestry.enclosing, at) }
}

## The function the name at `at` refers to, by its place among them.
referenced : Reading, U64, Str -> Try(U64, [NoFunction])
referenced = |reading, at, name| {
	path = Forest.path(reading.forest, at)
	by_key = reading.defined.by_key
	known = |key|
		match by_key.get(key) {
			Ok(index) => Ok(index)
			Err(_) => Err(NoFunction)
		}
	if name.contains(".") {
		parts = name.split_on(".")
		owner = parts.get(parts.len() - 2) ?? ""
		type_name = reading.aliases.get("${path}|${owner}") ?? owner
		known("${type_name}|${Tree.last_part(name)}")
	} else {
		owner = Functions.text_at(reading.ancestry.owner, at)
		if owner != "" and by_key.contains("${owner}|${name}") {
			known("${owner}|${name}")
		} else if by_key.contains("@${path}|${name}") {
			known("@${path}|${name}")
		} else {
			var $found = Err(NoFunction)
			for key in reading.defined.member_keys.get(name) ?? [] {
				index = by_key.get(key) ?? crash "check_boundaries: a member key with no function"
				if Functions.at(reading.defined, index).path == path {
					$found = Ok(index)
				}
			}
			$found
		}
	}
}

## The call whose head is the identifier at `at`, or none. In `x->f(a)`, the
## apply `f(a)` is the arrow call's second kid, and `x` its receiver.
call_headed_by : Forest, U64 -> [Called(References.Call), AsValue]
call_headed_by = |forest, at| {
	apply = Forest.parent(forest, at)
	if Forest.kind_or_none(forest, apply) != "e-apply" or Forest.kid(forest, apply, 1) != at {
		AsValue
	} else {
		arrow = Forest.parent(forest, apply)
		is_arrow = Forest.kind_or_none(forest, arrow) == "e-arrow-call" and Forest.kid(forest, arrow, 2) == apply
		receiver = if is_arrow {
			Forest.kid(forest, arrow, 1)
		} else {
			0
		}
		args = Forest.kids(forest, apply).drop_first(1)
		Called({ path: Forest.path(forest, at), line: Forest.node(forest, at).line, args, receiver })
	}
}

## The method call at `at`, its receiver the receiver node's value.
method_call : Forest, U64 -> References.Call
method_call = |forest, at| {
	var $args = []
	var $receiver = 0
	for kid in Forest.kids(forest, at) {
		kind = Forest.kind(forest, kid)
		if kind == "receiver" {
			$receiver = Forest.kid(forest, kid, 1)
		}
		if kind.starts_with("args") {
			$args = Forest.kids(forest, kid)
		}
	}
	{ path: Forest.path(forest, at), line: Forest.node(forest, at).line, args: $args, receiver: $receiver }
}

## By function, then in the order found.
event_order : Event, Event -> [Before, Same, After]
event_order = |first, second|
	if first.function != second.function {
		if first.function < second.function {
			Before
		} else {
			After
		}
	} else if first.seq < second.seq {
		Before
	} else if first.seq > second.seq {
		After
	} else {
		Same
	}

## A function's tally from its own references, in the order found.
tally_of : Functions.Function, List(Event), Set(Str) -> References.Tally
tally_of = |function, events, test_paths| {
	is_own = |event| event.reference.path == function.path and event.reference.line >= function.line and event.reference.line <= function.end_line
	own = events.keep_if(is_own)
	outside = events.drop_if(is_own)
	is_from_test_file = |event| References.is_test_file(event.reference.path) or (test_paths.contains(event.reference.path) and !(test_paths.contains(function.path)))
	from_tests = outside.keep_if(is_from_test_file)
	from_expects = outside.drop_if(is_from_test_file).keep_if(|event| event.reference.in_expect)
	production = outside.drop_if(is_from_test_file).drop_if(|event| event.reference.in_expect)
	prod_calls = calls_of(production)
	first_prod_caller = match production.first() {
		Ok(event) => "${event.reference.path}:${event.reference.line.to_str()} in ${event.reference.enclosing}"
		Err(_) => ""
	}
	{
		prod_refs: production.len(),
		value_refs: production.len() - prod_calls.len(),
		expect_refs: from_expects.len(),
		test_refs: from_tests.len(),
		first_prod_caller,
		prod_calls,
		self_calls: calls_of(own),
		test_calls: calls_of(outside.keep_if(|event| is_from_test_file(event) or event.reference.in_expect)),
		is_recursive: !(own.is_empty()),
		is_entry: Bool.False,
		is_ambiguous: Bool.False,
		is_mentioned: Bool.False,
	}
}

## The functions holding a production call of a recursive function: the
## entries into a recursion, by their places among the functions.
entries_of : Functions.Defined, List(References.Tally) -> Set(U64)
entries_of = |defined, tallies| {
	var $by_path = Dict.empty()
	$index : U64
	var $index = 0
	for function in defined.functions {
		$by_path = $by_path.insert(function.path, ($by_path.get(function.path) ?? []).append($index))
		$index = $index + 1
	}
	var $entries = Set.empty()
	for counted in tallies {
		if counted.is_recursive {
			for call in counted.prod_calls {
				for index in $by_path.get(call.path) ?? [] {
					holder = Functions.at(defined, index)
					if call.line >= holder.line and call.line <= holder.end_line {
						$entries = $entries.insert(index)
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	$entries
}

## Whether a file's name is a spec app's: `Spec.roc` after a run of letters
## and digits that holds a capital.
is_spec : Str -> Bool
is_spec = |base|
	if !(base.ends_with("Spec.roc")) {
		Bool.False
	} else {
		before = base.drop_suffix("Spec.roc").to_utf8()
		is_alphanumeric = |byte| (byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or (byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z') or (byte >= '0' and byte <= '9')
		run_start = match before.find_last_index(|byte| !(is_alphanumeric(byte))) {
			Ok(index) => index + 1
			Err(_) => 0
		}
		before.drop_first(run_start).any(|byte| byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z')
	}

## The calls among the references, in their order.
calls_of : List(Event) -> List(References.Call)
calls_of = |events| {
	var $calls = []
	for event in events {
		match event.use {
			Called(call) => {
				$calls = $calls.append(call)
			}
			AsValue => {}
		}
	}
	$calls
}

cookbook/roc/check_boundaries/SelfTest.roc, 107 lines

## The recipe's self-test, run after the checks over the plants in
## cookbook/roc/plants/check_boundaries/: each plant is named for the check it
## holds (`fixed_string.roc` holds `fixed`), and each check must fire on its
## own plants and on no others, and on no client; a `quiet_*.roc` plant gives
## no finding. A plant under `typed/` or `dead/` is a module, read in snake
## case (`BoolParam.roc` as `bool_param.roc`).
import pf.Shale
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text

SelfTest := [].{

	## What the checks found over the plants: the checked files, the clients,
	## how many files `tests=` named, and the findings printed.
	Judged : {
		paths : List(Str),
		clients : List(Str),
		test_count : U64,
		findings : List(Finding),
	}

	## The plants' verdict printed, then a stop when any plant is wrong.
	run! : SelfTest.Judged, List(Str) => {}
	run! = |judged, checks| {
		fired = Set.from_list(judged.findings.map(|finding| "${finding.path}|${finding.check}"))
		var $failures = []
		for check in checks {
			$planted : U64
			var $planted = 0
			for path in judged.paths {
				name = plant_name(path)
				is_mine = name == "${check}.roc" or name.starts_with("${check}_")
				if is_mine {
					$planted = $planted + 1
				}
				did_fire = fired.contains("${path}|${check}")
				if is_mine and !(did_fire) {
					$failures = $failures.append("`${check}` does not fire on its plant ${path}")
				}
				if did_fire and !(is_mine) {
					$failures = $failures.append("`${check}` fires on ${path}, another check's plant")
				}
			}
			if $planted == 0 {
				$failures = $failures.append("`${check}` has no plant")
			}
			for path in judged.clients {
				if fired.contains("${path}|${check}") {
					$failures = $failures.append("`${check}` fires on the client ${path}, which is read only for its calls")
				}
			}
		}
		if judged.clients.is_empty() or judged.test_count == 0 {
			$failures = $failures.append("no client or no gate plant read")
		}
		for failure in $failures {
			Shale.print!("FAIL ${failure}")
		}
		if !($failures.is_empty()) {
			Shale.fail!("check_boundaries self_test: ${$failures.len().to_str()} plants wrong")
		}
		Shale.print!("check_boundaries (Roc) self_test: PASS (each check fires on its plants alone, the quiet_ plants on none)")
	}

	## The plants' folder.
	plants : Str
	plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_boundaries/"

	## The typed plants, judged with the types under `QuietApp.roc`.
	typed_plants : Str
	typed_plants = "${SelfTest.plants}typed/"

	## The plants `dead` and `unused_api` are judged on, since nothing calls
	## the others.
	dead_plants : Str
	dead_plants = "${SelfTest.plants}dead/"
}

## A plant's file name as the self-test reads it: a typed or `dead/` plant's
## in snake case.
plant_name : Str -> Str
plant_name = |path| {
	base = Text.basename(path)
	if path.starts_with(SelfTest.typed_plants) or path.starts_with(SelfTest.dead_plants) {
		snake_case(base)
	} else {
		base
	}
}

## A CamelCase file name in snake case: `_` before each capital but a first,
## and the capital made small.
snake_case : Str -> Str
snake_case = |name| {
	var $out = []
	for byte in name.to_utf8() {
		if Text.is_capital(byte) {
			if !($out.is_empty()) {
				$out = $out.append('_')
			}
			$out = $out.append(byte + 32)
		} else {
			$out = $out.append(byte)
		}
	}
	Str.from_utf8_lossy($out)
}

## The effects of a recipe's `types=1`: the tree's Roc found, and roc-types
## (Roc's own checker, https://github.com/showell/roc-types) run on each app
## of `root=`, its pin held to the tree's Roc. Reading and joining its output
## is cookbook/roc/lib/'s RocTypes; this file is the same in check_errors,
## hunt_names and check_boundaries, since a package reaches no effect.
import pf.Shale
import lib.RocTypes
import lib.Text

Types := [].{

	## The OS path of the tree's Roc: the pin in `roc-version` where the run
	## starts, or the self-test's pin, which cookbook/roc/pinned.shale names.
	## `who` names the recipe in a refusal.
	roc_bin! : Str, Bool => Str
	roc_bin! = |who, self_test| {
		pin = if self_test {
			pinned = read_text!(who, "cookbook:roc/pinned.shale")
			must!(RocTypes.self_test_pin(pinned).map_err(|_| "${who}: cookbook/roc/pinned.shale names no SELF_TEST_PIN"))
		} else if Shale.exists!("roc-version") {
			Text.trim(read_text!(who, "roc-version"))
		} else {
			must!(Err("${who}: no roc-version where the run starts: run it from the repository's root, whose roc-version pins its Roc"))
		}
		roc = RocTypes.roc_of_pin(pin)
		if !(Shale.exists!(roc)) {
			must!(Err("${who}: no ${roc}: install Roc ${pin} into ~/tools/roc-${pin}/ (roc-apps's toolchain release carries it)"))
		} else {
			Shale.real!(roc)
		}
	}

	## The types of the nodes of `kind` in the files `paths`, from roc-types
	## run on each app of `root` with the Roc at `roc`, and a line for each
	## file no app reaches, except those in `exempt`.
	gather! : { who : Str, kind : RocTypes.Kind, root : Str, roc : Str, paths : List(Str), exempt : Set(Str) } => { typing : RocTypes.Typing, unreached : List(Str) }
	gather! = |asked| {
		roots = must!(RocTypes.root_apps(asked.who, asked.root))
		var $by_module = Dict.empty()
		for root in roots {
			got = modules_of!(root, asked.roc)
			$by_module = RocTypes.joined($by_module, got, asked.kind)
			for warning in got.warnings {
				Shale.print!("${asked.who}: roc-types ${root}: ${warning}")
			}
		}
		var $named = []
		for path in asked.paths {
			$named = $named.append({ path, real: Shale.real!(path) })
		}
		RocTypes.typing_of({ by_module: $by_module, named: $named, exempt: asked.exempt, roots })
	}
}

## The modules roc-types reports for the app `root`, built with the Roc at
## `roc`, or a stop: roc-types missing, of another format, built for another
## Roc, or refusing the app.
modules_of! : Str, Str => RocTypes.Modules
modules_of! = |root, roc| {
	pinned = RocTypes.pinned_checker(roc) ?? RocTypes.default_checker
	exe = if Shale.exists!(pinned) {
		pinned
	} else {
		RocTypes.default_checker
	}
	if !(Shale.exists!(exe)) {
		Shale.fail!("`roc_types`: no ${exe}: ${RocTypes.install_hint}")
	}
	ran = Shale.run!({
		argv: [Shale.real!(exe), Shale.real!(root)],
		keep: Whole(64000000),
		timeout_ms: 300000,
		want: "",
	})
	output_lines = Text.lines(ran.out)
	pin = must!(RocTypes.pin_of(output_lines, root))
	own = RocTypes.roc_of_pin(pin)
	if !(Shale.exists!(own)) or Shale.real!(own) != roc {
		Shale.fail!(RocTypes.another_compiler(pin, root, roc))
	}
	must!(RocTypes.modules_ran(output_lines, ran.code, root))
}

read_text! : Str, Str => Str
read_text! = |who, path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => must!(Err("${who}: no ${path}"))
	}

## What `tried` holds, or the run stopped with its refusal.
must! : Try(a, Str) => a
must! = |tried|
	match tried {
		Ok(value) => value
		Err(why) => {
			Shale.fail!(why)
			crash "Types: Shale.fail! returned"
		}
	}

## The source text the checks compare: a node's text squeezed onto one line,
## a call's argument texts slot by slot and the texts its calls agree on, a
## branch's text without its braces, and whether a text is a literal.
import lib.Bytes
import lib.Forest
import lib.Text
import References

Source := [].{

	## What a slot of a function's calls holds: the text every call gives it,
	## or `Differs` where the calls differ.
	Slot : [Agreed(Str), Differs]

	## The node's source text, squeezed onto one line, `?` for a node with no
	## span. `lines_of` is each file's lines; a node's end column is one past
	## its last byte.
	text_of : Dict(Str, List(Str)), Forest, U64 -> Str
	text_of = |lines_of, forest, at| {
		node = Forest.node(forest, at)
		source_lines = lines_of.get(Forest.path(forest, at)) ?? []
		line_bytes = |number| Bytes.line_of(source_lines, number)
		before_end = if node.end_column == 0 {
			0
		} else {
			node.end_column - 1
		}
		if node.line == 0 {
			"?"
		} else if node.line == node.end_line {
			Str.from_utf8_lossy(Bytes.span(line_bytes(node.line), node.column, before_end))
		} else {
			var $parts = [Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.rest_from(line_bytes(node.line), node.column))]
			var $number = node.line + 1
			while $number < node.end_line {
				$parts = $parts.append(Bytes.trimmed(line_bytes($number)))
				$number = $number + 1
			}
			$parts = $parts.append(Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.span(line_bytes(node.end_line), 1, before_end)))
			Str.join_with($parts.map(Str.from_utf8_lossy), " ")
		}
	}

	## A call's argument texts by slot (`1`, `2`, ...), the receiver first. A
	## record argument gives its fields instead, as `N.field`, so that
	## `{ needle, at: 0 }` is judged field by field.
	argument_texts : Dict(Str, List(Str)), Forest, References.Call -> Dict(Str, Str)
	argument_texts = |lines_of, forest, call| {
		arguments = if call.receiver != 0 {
			[call.receiver].concat(call.args)
		} else {
			call.args
		}
		var $texts = Dict.empty()
		$slot : U64
		var $slot = 0
		for argument in arguments {
			$slot = $slot + 1
			if Forest.kind(forest, argument) == "e-record" {
				for field in Forest.kids(forest, argument) {
					field_name = if Forest.kind(forest, field) == "field" {
						Forest.attribute(forest, field, "field")
					} else {
						""
					}
					if field_name != "" {
						value = Forest.kid(forest, field, 1)
						text = if value != 0 {
							Source.text_of(lines_of, forest, value)
						} else {
							field_name
						}
						$texts = $texts.insert("${$slot.to_str()}.${field_name}", text)
					}
				}
			} else {
				$texts = $texts.insert($slot.to_str(), Source.text_of(lines_of, forest, argument))
			}
		}
		$texts
	}

	## For each slot of `calls`, the text every call gives it, or `Differs`.
	agreed : Dict(Str, List(Str)), Forest, List(References.Call) -> Dict(Str, Source.Slot)
	agreed = |lines_of, forest, calls| {
		var $agreed = Dict.empty()
		var $is_first = Bool.True
		for call in calls {
			texts = Source.argument_texts(lines_of, forest, call)
			if $is_first {
				for (slot, text) in texts.to_list() {
					$agreed = $agreed.insert(slot, Agreed(text))
				}
				$is_first = Bool.False
			} else {
				for (slot, was) in $agreed.to_list() {
					match was {
						Agreed(text) =>
							if texts.get(slot) != Ok(text) {
								$agreed = $agreed.insert(slot, Differs)
							}
						Differs => {}
					}
				}
				for (slot, _) in texts.to_list() {
					if !($agreed.contains(slot)) {
						$agreed = $agreed.insert(slot, Differs)
					}
				}
			}
		}
		$agreed
	}

	## The text of one branch of an `if`, its braces left out when it holds
	## one statement.
	branch_text : Dict(Str, List(Str)), Forest, U64 -> Str
	branch_text = |lines_of, forest, at| {
		is_one = |kid| Forest.kind(forest, kid) == "statements" and Forest.kids(forest, kid).len() == 1
		if Forest.kind(forest, at) == "e-block" {
			match Forest.kids(forest, at).find_first(is_one) {
				Ok(statements) => Source.text_of(lines_of, forest, Forest.kid(forest, statements, 1))
				Err(_) => Source.text_of(lines_of, forest, at)
			}
		} else {
			Source.text_of(lines_of, forest, at)
		}
	}

	## Whether a text is a literal: a number, a string, a character, a tag
	## (`Begin`) or a module's constant (`Limits.max`).
	is_literal : Str -> Bool
	is_literal = |text| {
		bytes = text.to_utf8()
		first = bytes.first() ?? 0
		second = bytes.get(1) ?? 0
		if first == '"' or first == '\'' or Text.is_digit(first) or (first == '-' and Text.is_digit(second)) {
			Bool.True
		} else if !(Text.is_capital(first)) {
			Bool.False
		} else {
			is_name_byte = |byte| Bytes.is_letter(byte) or Text.is_digit(byte)
			after = bytes.drop_first(1)
			rest = after.drop_first(after.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_name_byte(byte))) ?? after.len())
			is_lower_byte = |byte| Text.is_small_letter(byte) or Text.is_digit(byte) or byte == '_'
			starts_constant = (rest.first() ?? 0) == '.' and Bytes.starts_lower_name(rest.get(1) ?? 0)
			rest.is_empty() or (starts_constant and rest.drop_first(2).all(is_lower_byte))
		}
	}
}
