The libraries it loads: cookbook/roc/headers.shale (96 lines), cookbook/roc/house.shale (46 lines), cookbook/roc/parsed.shale (34 lines), cookbook/roc/pinned.shale (20 lines), cookbook/roc/types.shale (301 lines).

-- This recipe asks of every function in a tree of .roc files whether its
-- boundary earns its keep, and whether each of its parameters is really a
-- parameter. It reads each file's syntax tree from Roc's own parser
-- (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale), and it checks the functions defined at the
-- top level of a file or as members of a module type, not those inside
-- another function. A finding is a question for a reader, not a verdict.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_boundaries.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc
--   shale cookbook:roc/check_boundaries.shale self_test=1
--
-- The arguments:
--   glob   the files to read, `**/*.roc` by default. Read the whole tree,
--          tests too, because a test that reaches a function keeps it
--          quiet, and calls are counted only in the files read;
--   ways   the most ways through a body that `single` still calls a
--          wrapper, 2 by default;
--   nodes  the most syntax-tree nodes in such a body, 24 by default;
--   house  with `house=0`, leave out what is only our house style
--          (cookbook/roc/house.shale), for another project's code;
--   types  with `types=1`, Roc's checker gives the types
--          (cookbook/roc/types.shale), which `bool_param` needs. It is off
--          by default, and needs the tree's `roc-version` file;
--   root   with `types=1`, the app that imports the files read, or several
--          apps separated by commas (`root=a.roc,b.roc`);
--   clients  globs separated by commas, of files read only for the calls
--          they make into the files checked, as apps that import a game.
--          Their own functions and `if`s are not checked, even where `glob`
--          matches them too;
--   tests  globs separated by commas, of checked files that are tests of
--          the rest, as a tree's gate apps. A reference from one of them to
--          a function outside them counts as a test's;
--   test_reach  `keeps` by default, so an `expect` or a test that reaches a
--          function keeps it out of `dead` and `unused_api`. With
--          `test_reach=dead`, only a production call or reference keeps a
--          module type's member out of `dead`. A file's own top-level
--          function is private to it, so its tests may still be all that
--          reach it, and a test of a library's API is a user of it.
--
-- The checks, most from the Roc style guide (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md):
--
--   single      A small function with exactly one production call, and no
--               `expect`, test file or `##` doc comment that reaches or
--               explains it, would read better inline at that call ("A
--               function earns its boundary"; the guide calls it a rule of
--               thumb). Its body must be one statement of at most `nodes`
--               nodes and `ways` ways through: an `if` adds a way, and a
--               `match` adds one for each arm past its first. A function
--               passed as a value (`map_ok(Uid.to_str)`), a question named
--               `is_*` or `has_*`, a recursive function and an entry into
--               one (see `entry`) are quiet.
--   fixed       Every production call, two or more, passes the same
--               literal for one parameter, or for one field of a record
--               argument. A literal is a number, a string, a character, a
--               tag (`Begin`, `Bool.True`) or a module's constant
--               (`Limits.max`). "A parameter every caller passes the same
--               value is no parameter": drop it, or add an entry function
--               that takes only what varies. A recursive function's calls
--               to itself must pass the same literal too. The same variable
--               or call at every call site (`me`, `req.me`,
--               `Host.list_srcs!({})`) is the caller's own value handed on,
--               and is not a literal. A library's API keeps its parameters
--               whatever this tree's callers pass, so `fixed` skips a
--               module type's member in a file under a `lib/` folder, or in
--               a module exposed by a `package` or `platform` header in the
--               `main.roc` beside it. A file's own top-level functions there
--               are checked.
--   entry       Every production call, two or more, passes the same literal
--               for a parameter that the recursive function's own calls
--               vary (`at: 0` outside, `at + 1` inside). The recursion
--               needs the parameter, so the fix is an entry function that
--               takes only what varies and passes the literal itself
--               (`count = |xs| count_from(xs, 0)`). That entry function
--               makes the one outside call, so it does not fire again.
--   constant    A function whose one argument is `{}`, by its annotation or
--               its lambda's pattern, and whose name has no `!`, gives the
--               same value at every call, so it can be a constant
--               (`board = ...`, not `board = |{}| ...`). A function with an
--               effect needs a `!` in its name. Roc refuses a generic
--               constant, so a function whose annotated return type holds a
--               type variable (`{} -> Viewer(id)`) is quiet. An unannotated
--               function's type is unknown, so it is checked. A `##` doc
--               above it (or its annotation) answers it, giving the reason
--               it stays a function, as a `##` doc answers `single`.
--   dead        A top-level or member function that nothing reaches in the
--               files read: no production call, no `expect`, no test file, and
--               no reference to it as a value, a record's shorthand
--               (`{ helper }`) included. Its calls to itself don't count. A
--               top-level function is private to its file, even in a package,
--               and a member of a module no package exposes has no caller to
--               come. Left alone are the names something else calls: what an
--               app's header provides, what a platform requires and provides,
--               and a method Roc calls by name (`is_eq`, `to_hash`).
--   unused_api  The same, for a member of a module its package or platform
--               exposes, a member under a `lib/` folder, or a name a `module`
--               header exposes. The callers of a public name are mostly
--               outside the tree, so this is a question and not a verdict, and
--               it has its own count. A member only an `expect` reaches is in
--               neither, unless `test_reach=dead`.
--   same_branches  An `if` whose two branches are the same text, braces aside
--               (`if m.over { m } else m`). The condition decides nothing, so
--               a rule was lost, or the `if` should go.
--   bool_param  With `types=1` only: a parameter whose type is `Bool` is
--               passed `Bool.True`, `Bool.False`, `True` or `False` by some
--               call. "A flag a caller passes is a tag", named for what it
--               means (`Loud`, not `Bool.True`). Every call counts, from an
--               `expect`, a test file or the function itself too. A
--               function with one parameter is quiet, as that parameter is
--               the value it converts (`bool : Bool -> JsonOut`), and so is
--               a field of a record argument.
--
-- A reference to a function is its bare name in the file that defines it,
-- `Type.name` anywhere, the type read through the file's `import ... as`, or
-- a method call `.name(...)`. The receiver of a method call or of an arrow call (`x->f(a)`) is its first argument. A
-- method call counts for every module type with a member of that name, so
-- a member whose name another type's member shares is ambiguous, and only
-- `constant` checks it. A test file is a file whose name ends in
-- `twin.roc`, a file under a `twin/` or `test/` folder, or a spec app,
-- named for its module followed by `Spec.roc` (`BlitSpec.roc`). Its
-- references count as an `expect`'s do, never as production calls, and
-- its own functions are not checked.
--
-- Each finding is one line, `path:line: <check>: <why>`, where the line is
-- the function's definition, and the findings are followed by a summary
-- line of the counts. Files that don't parse are listed after the summary,
-- with the files no root reaches under `types=1`, and then the run fails.
--
-- `self_test=1` checks the plants in `cookbook/roc/plants/check_boundaries/`.
-- Each plant is named for the check it holds (`fixed_string.roc` holds
-- `fixed`), and each check must fire on its own plants and on no others; a
-- `quiet_*.roc` plant must give no finding. `dead` and `unused_api` are judged
-- only under `dead/`, since nothing calls the other plants. The plants under
-- `typed/` are type modules checked with the types under the app `QuietApp.roc`, and
-- their names are read in snake case (`BoolParam.roc` as `bool_param`).
-- The rest are checked without types. The self-test runs with
-- `test_reach=dead`, the plants under `dead/clients/` as `clients`, and those
-- under `dead/gates/` as `tests`. The self-test fails if roc-types is not
-- installed.
-- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=3000000000

const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_boundaries/"
const TYPED_PLANTS = PLANTS .. "typed/"
const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "**/*.roc") or arg("glob", "**/*.roc")
const MAX_WAYS = arg("ways", 2)
const MAX_NODES = arg("nodes", 24)
const DEAD_PLANTS = PLANTS .. "dead/"
const CHECKS = {"single", "fixed", "entry", "constant", "bool_param", "dead", "unused_api", "same_branches"}
use("./headers.shale")
use("./house.shale")
use("./parsed.shale")
use("./pinned.shale")
use("./types.shale")
const TYPES_ARG = arg("types", "0")
if TYPES_ARG ~= "0" and TYPES_ARG ~= "1" then fail("check_boundaries: types must be 0 (the default) or 1, not " .. TYPES_ARG) end
const USE_TYPES = SELF_TEST or TYPES_ARG == "1"
const ROOT = SELF_TEST and (TYPED_PLANTS .. "QuietApp.roc") or arg("root", "")
-- The self-test reads the plants under `dead/clients/` as clients, and those
-- under `dead/gates/` as tests.
const CLIENTS_ARG = SELF_TEST and (DEAD_PLANTS .. "clients/*.roc") or arg("clients", "")
const TESTS_ARG = SELF_TEST and (DEAD_PLANTS .. "gates/*.roc") or arg("tests", "")
const TEST_REACH = SELF_TEST and "dead" or arg("test_reach", "keeps")
if TEST_REACH ~= "keeps" and TEST_REACH ~= "dead" then fail("check_boundaries: test_reach must be keeps (the default) or dead, not " .. TEST_REACH) end
-- The pinned Roc defines `Bool := [False, True]`.
const BOOL_LITERALS = {["Bool.True"] = true, ["Bool.False"] = true, True = true, False = true}

-- Every file's syntax-tree nodes in one list, so that one index names a
-- node anywhere. `NODE_PATH[g]` is node g's file. A node's `parent` and
-- `kids` count from its own file's first node, so `NODE_OFFSET[g]` is
-- added to them.
const NODES = {}
const NODE_PATH = {}
const NODE_OFFSET = {}
const SOURCE_LINES = {}
-- Each file's `header_names`, and the module each of its import aliases
-- stands for, by `path|alias`.
const HEADER_NAMES = {}
const IMPORT_ALIASES = {}
-- The kinds of node that can hold a top-level function: a file, its
-- statements, a module type's declaration, and the block of its members.
const TOP_LEVEL_KINDS = {file = true, statements = true, ["s-type-decl"] = true, associated = true}

const finding_counts = {}
for c in CHECKS do finding_counts[c] = 0 end
-- The self-test's record of which checks fired on which files, by `path|check`.
const fired = {}

function report(path, line, check, why)
  if house_leaves_out("check_boundaries", check) then return nil end
  -- The other plants exist to be read by the other checks, and nothing calls them.
  if SELF_TEST and (check == "dead" or check == "unused_api") and not starts_with(path, DEAD_PLANTS) then return nil end
  print(path .. ":" .. line .. ": " .. check .. ": " .. why)
  finding_counts[check] = finding_counts[check] + 1
  fired[path .. "|" .. check] = true
  return nil
end

function children(g)
  local out = {}
  for k in NODES[g].kids do push(out, NODE_OFFSET[g] + k) end
  return out
end

function parent(g)
  local p = NODES[g].parent
  if p == 0 then return 0 end
  return NODE_OFFSET[g] + p
end

function kind(g)
  return NODES[g].kind
end

function raw_text(g)
  return get(NODES[g], "raw", "")
end

-- Node g's source text, squeezed onto one line. A node's end column is one
-- past its last character.
function source_text(path, g)
  local n = NODES[g]
  if n.line == 0 then return "?" end
  local src = SOURCE_LINES[path]
  if n.line == n.end_line then return sub(src[n.line], n.column, n.end_column - 1) end
  local parts = {trim(sub(src[n.line], n.column))}
  for l = n.line + 1, n.end_line - 1 do push(parts, trim(src[l])) end
  push(parts, trim(sub(src[n.end_line], 1, n.end_column - 1)))
  return join(parts, " ")
end

function is_literal(s)
  local c = sub(s, 1, 1)
  if c == "\"" or c == "'" then return true end
  if re_find(s, "^-?[0-9]") ~= nil then return true end
  if re_find(s, "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\\.[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*)?$") ~= nil then return true end
  return false
end

function is_question_name(name)
  return starts_with(name, "is_") or starts_with(name, "has_")
end

function is_test_file(path)
  if re_find(basename(path), "[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*Spec\\.roc$") ~= nil then return true end
  return ends_with(path, "twin.roc") or contains(path, "/twin/") or contains(path, "/test/") or starts_with(path, "test/") or starts_with(path, "twin/")
end

-- Whether a function is part of a library's API: a module type's member in a
-- file under a `lib/` folder, or in a module its package or platform exposes,
-- or a name its own `module` header exposes.
function is_library_api(func)
  if has_key(HEADER_NAMES[func.path].exposed, func.name) then return true end
  if sub(func.owner, 1, 1) == "@" then return false end
  local p = func.path
  if starts_with(p, "lib/") or contains(p, "/lib/") or contains(p, ":lib/") then return true end
  return is_exposed_module(p)
end

-- The name in the header of the module type declared at `g`.
function type_decl_name(g)
  local kids = children(g)
  if #kids == 0 then return "" end
  return get(NODES[kids[1]], "name", "")
end

-- ── the syntax trees ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- The files matched by `globs`, a list separated by commas, as a set when
-- `as_set`.
function globbed(globs, as_set)
  local paths = {}
  local set = {}
  for g in split(globs, ",") do
    if trim(g) ~= "" then
      for p in glob(trim(g)) do
        push(paths, p)
        set[p] = true
      end
    end
  end
  return as_set and set or paths
end

-- A file that `clients` and `glob` both match is a client, and not checked.
const CLIENT_FILES = globbed(CLIENTS_ARG, false)
const CLIENT_SET = globbed(CLIENTS_ARG, true)
local checked_files = {}
local checked_set = {}
for p in globbed(GLOB, false) do
  if not has_key(CLIENT_SET, p) then
    push(checked_files, p)
    checked_set[p] = true
  end
end
const ROC_FILES = checked_files
const CHECKED = checked_set
const TEST_PATHS = globbed(TESTS_ARG, true)
local untyped_plants = {}
if SELF_TEST then
  for p in ROC_FILES do
    if not starts_with(p, TYPED_PLANTS) then untyped_plants[p] = true end
  end
end
local checker_types = USE_TYPES and roc_types_for_files("check_boundaries", ROOT, roc_bin("check_boundaries", SELF_TEST), ROC_FILES, untyped_plants) or {real = {}, pats = {}, exprs = {}, unreached = {}}
local files_parsed = {}
for p in ROC_FILES do push(files_parsed, p) end
for p in CLIENT_FILES do push(files_parsed, p) end
local parsed = parse_roc_files(files_parsed)
for f in parsed.files do
  SOURCE_LINES[f.path] = split(read(f.path), "\n")
  HEADER_NAMES[f.path] = header_names(f.nodes)
  local offset = #NODES
  for n in f.nodes do
    push(NODES, n)
    push(NODE_PATH, f.path)
    push(NODE_OFFSET, offset)
  end
end

-- What each node's ancestors say, worked out from its parent's, which
-- comes before it in the list:
--   AT_TOP_LEVEL[g]    every ancestor is of a kind in `TOP_LEVEL_KINDS`;
--   OWNER_TYPE[g]      the name of the nearest module type around it, or "";
--   ENCLOSING_DECL[g]  the name of the outermost declaration around it, or "?";
--   IN_EXPECT[g]       it is inside an `expect`.
const AT_TOP_LEVEL = {}
const OWNER_TYPE = {}
const ENCLOSING_DECL = {}
const IN_EXPECT = {}
for g = 1, #NODES do
  local p = parent(g)
  if p == 0 then
    push(AT_TOP_LEVEL, true)
    push(OWNER_TYPE, "")
    push(ENCLOSING_DECL, "?")
    push(IN_EXPECT, false)
  else
    local parent_kind = kind(p)
    push(AT_TOP_LEVEL, AT_TOP_LEVEL[p] and has_key(TOP_LEVEL_KINDS, parent_kind))
    push(OWNER_TYPE, parent_kind == "s-type-decl" and type_decl_name(p) or OWNER_TYPE[p])
    local enclosing = ENCLOSING_DECL[p]
    if enclosing == "?" and parent_kind == "s-decl" then
      local pattern = children(p)
      if #pattern > 0 and kind(pattern[1]) == "p-ident" then enclosing = raw_text(pattern[1]) end
    end
    push(ENCLOSING_DECL, enclosing)
    push(IN_EXPECT, IN_EXPECT[p] or parent_kind == "s-expect")
  end
end

-- How many `##` lines stand just above the function defined at `line`,
-- or above its annotation (`name : ...`, on one line or several) if it
-- has one.
function doc_comment_lines(src, name, line)
  local top = line - 1
  local k = top
  while k >= 1 and k > line - 12 and trim(src[k]) ~= "" and not starts_with(trim(src[k]), "#") do
    if starts_with(trim(src[k]), name .. " :") then top = k - 1 end
    k = k - 1
  end
  local n = 0
  while top >= 1 and starts_with(trim(src[top]), "##") do
    n = n + 1
    top = top - 1
  end
  return n
end

-- The nodes of the subtree at `g`, `g` first.
function subtree_nodes(g)
  local out = {g}
  local i = 1
  while i <= #out do
    for k in children(out[i]) do push(out, k) end
    i = i + 1
  end
  return out
end

-- Whether the body of the lambda at `g` is small enough for `single` to
-- call it a wrapper, as `is_wrapper`, and its size in words for the
-- finding, as `size`. A wrapper's body is one statement: a block of one,
-- or an expression. Its size counts syntax-tree nodes, so the layout of
-- its lines changes nothing. It has one way through it, and one more for
-- each `if` and for each `match` arm past the first. So only a two-way
-- choice reads as a wrapper, and an `else if` chain or a nested `if` is a
-- rule of its own however few lines it takes.
function body_measure(g)
  local kids = children(g)
  local body = kids[#kids]
  if kind(body) == "e-block" then
    local statements = {}
    for k in children(body) do
      if kind(k) == "statements" then statements = children(k) end
    end
    if #statements ~= 1 then return {is_wrapper = false, size = #statements .. " statements"} end
    body = statements[1]
  end
  local all = subtree_nodes(body)
  local ways = 1
  for k in all do
    if kind(k) == "e-if-then-else" then ways = ways + 1 end
    if kind(k) == "branches" then ways = ways + #children(k) - 1 end
  end
  local small = #all <= MAX_NODES
  if ways > 1 then return {is_wrapper = small and ways <= MAX_WAYS, size = "a decision of " .. ways .. " ways, " .. #all .. " nodes"} end
  return {is_wrapper = small, size = "one expression of " .. #all .. " nodes"}
end

-- The function type in the annotation just before the declaration at `g`,
-- if that annotation is for `name`, or 0.
function annotation_function_type(g, name)
  local p = parent(g)
  if p == 0 then return 0 end
  local before = 0
  local prev = 0
  for k in children(p) do
    if k == g then before = prev end
    prev = k
  end
  if before == 0 or kind(before) ~= "s-type-anno" or get(NODES[before], "name", "") ~= name then return 0 end
  local ty = children(before)
  if #ty == 0 or kind(ty[1]) ~= "ty-fn" then return 0 end
  return ty[1]
end

-- Whether the function declared at `g` takes `{}` alone, by its lambda's
-- one pattern or its annotation's one argument, and could be a constant:
-- an annotated return type holding a type variable (`ty-var`) rules that
-- out.
function takes_empty_record_alone(g, name)
  local takes_it = false
  local lambda = children(g)[2]
  for k in children(lambda) do
    if kind(k) == "args" then
      local patterns = children(k)
      if #patterns == 1 and kind(patterns[1]) == "p-record" and #children(patterns[1]) == 0 then takes_it = true end
    end
  end
  local fn_type = annotation_function_type(g, name)
  if fn_type == 0 then return takes_it end
  local parts = children(fn_type)
  if #parts == 2 and kind(parts[1]) == "ty-record" and #children(parts[1]) == 0 then takes_it = true end
  if not takes_it then return false end
  for k in subtree_nodes(parts[#parts]) do
    if kind(k) == "ty-var" then return false end
  end
  return true
end

-- The parameter patterns of the lambda at `g`, by position.
function lambda_params(g)
  for k in children(g) do
    if kind(k) == "args" then return children(k) end
  end
  return {}
end

-- ── pass 1: the functions ────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- Each function by `owner|name`, where the owner is its module type's name,
-- or `@path` for a file's own top-level function.
const FUNCTIONS = {}
-- The keys of the module types' members, by name.
const MEMBER_KEYS = {}
for g = 1, #NODES do
  if kind(g) == "s-decl" then
    local kids = children(g)
    if #kids > 1 and kind(kids[1]) == "p-ident" and kind(kids[2]) == "e-lambda" and AT_TOP_LEVEL[g] and has_key(CHECKED, NODE_PATH[g]) then
      local path = NODE_PATH[g]
      local owner = OWNER_TYPE[g] ~= "" and OWNER_TYPE[g] or ("@" .. path)
      local n = NODES[g]
      local name = raw_text(kids[1])
      local key = owner .. "|" .. name
      local body = body_measure(kids[2])
      FUNCTIONS[key] = {
        key = key, path = path, owner = owner, name = name, line = n.line, end_line = n.end_line,
        is_wrapper = body.is_wrapper, size = body.size, doc_lines = doc_comment_lines(SOURCE_LINES[path], name, n.line),
        takes_empty_record_alone = takes_empty_record_alone(g, name), params = lambda_params(kids[2]),
        prod_refs = 0, value_refs = 0, expect_refs = 0, test_refs = 0, prod_callers = {},
        prod_calls = {}, self_calls = {}, test_calls = {}, mentions = 0,
        is_ambiguous = false, is_recursive = false, is_entry = false,
      }
      if sub(owner, 1, 1) ~= "@" then
        if not has_key(MEMBER_KEYS, name) then MEMBER_KEYS[name] = {} end
        push(MEMBER_KEYS[name], key)
      end
    end
  end
end

-- ── pass 2: the references ───────────────────────────────────────────────

-- A call is `{path, line, args, receiver}`, where `args` are the argument
-- nodes and `receiver` is an arrow or method call's receiver, which is
-- the first argument, or 0 for none.

-- The call whose head is the identifier at `g`, or nil if it heads none.
function call_headed_by(g)
  local apply = parent(g)
  if apply == 0 or kind(apply) ~= "e-apply" then return nil end
  local kids = children(apply)
  if kids[1] ~= g then return nil end
  local call = {path = NODE_PATH[g], line = NODES[g].line, args = drop(kids, 1), receiver = 0}
  -- In `x->f(a)`, the apply `f(a)` is the arrow call's second child.
  local arrow = parent(apply)
  if arrow ~= 0 and kind(arrow) == "e-arrow-call" then
    local arrow_kids = children(arrow)
    if arrow_kids[2] == apply then call.receiver = arrow_kids[1] end
  end
  return call
end

function method_call(g)
  local args = {}
  local receiver = 0
  for k in children(g) do
    if kind(k) == "receiver" then receiver = children(k)[1] end
    if starts_with(kind(k), "args") then args = children(k) end
  end
  return {path = NODE_PATH[g], line = NODES[g].line, args = args, receiver = receiver}
end

-- The key of the function that the name at `g` refers to, or "".
function referenced_key(g, name)
  local path = NODE_PATH[g]
  if contains(name, ".") then
    local parts = split(name, ".")
    local owner = parts[#parts - 1]
    local key = get(IMPORT_ALIASES, path .. "|" .. owner, owner) .. "|" .. parts[#parts]
    return has_key(FUNCTIONS, key) and key or ""
  end
  local owner = OWNER_TYPE[g]
  if owner ~= "" and has_key(FUNCTIONS, owner .. "|" .. name) then return owner .. "|" .. name end
  if has_key(FUNCTIONS, "@" .. path .. "|" .. name) then return "@" .. path .. "|" .. name end
  local key = ""
  for m in get(MEMBER_KEYS, name, {}) do
    if FUNCTIONS[m].path == path then key = m end
  end
  return key
end

-- A reference within the function's own lines makes it recursive. Any
-- other is from a test file, from an `expect`, or from production, and
-- `call` is nil when the function is passed as a value.
function record_reference(func, ref, call)
  if ref.path == func.path and ref.line >= func.line and ref.line <= func.end_line then
    func.is_recursive = true
    if call ~= nil then push(func.self_calls, call) end
    return nil
  end
  local from_test_file = is_test_file(ref.path) or (has_key(TEST_PATHS, ref.path) and not has_key(TEST_PATHS, func.path))
  if (from_test_file or ref.in_expect) and call ~= nil then push(func.test_calls, call) end
  if from_test_file then
    func.test_refs = func.test_refs + 1
  elseif ref.in_expect then
    func.expect_refs = func.expect_refs + 1
  else
    func.prod_refs = func.prod_refs + 1
    push(func.prod_callers, ref.path .. ":" .. ref.line .. " in " .. ref.enclosing)
    if call == nil then func.value_refs = func.value_refs + 1 else push(func.prod_calls, call) end
  end
  return nil
end

function reference_at(g)
  return {path = NODE_PATH[g], line = NODES[g].line, in_expect = IN_EXPECT[g], enclosing = ENCLOSING_DECL[g]}
end

-- A name that may reach a member by a way this recipe can't follow: an alias
-- of a type, or a name an import exposes. It keeps every member of that name
-- out of `dead`, and counts as no call for the other checks.
function note_mention(name)
  for key in get(MEMBER_KEYS, name, {}) do FUNCTIONS[key].mentions = FUNCTIONS[key].mentions + 1 end
  return nil
end

function last_dotted_part(name)
  local parts = split(name, ".")
  return parts[#parts]
end

for g = 1, #NODES do
  if kind(g) == "s-import" and has_key(NODES[g], "alias") then
    IMPORT_ALIASES[NODE_PATH[g] .. "|" .. NODES[g].alias] = last_dotted_part(raw_text(g))
  end
end

for g = 1, #NODES do
  local node_kind = kind(g)
  if node_kind == "e-method-call" then
    local name = sub(get(NODES[g], "method", ""), 2)
    if name ~= "" then
      local call = method_call(g)
      local keys_of_name = get(MEMBER_KEYS, name, {})
      for key in keys_of_name do
        record_reference(FUNCTIONS[key], reference_at(g), call)
        if #keys_of_name > 1 then FUNCTIONS[key].is_ambiguous = true end
      end
    end
  elseif node_kind == "e-ident" then
    local name = raw_text(g)
    local key = name ~= "" and referenced_key(g, name) or ""
    if key ~= "" then record_reference(FUNCTIONS[key], reference_at(g), call_headed_by(g)) end
    if key == "" and contains(name, ".") then note_mention(last_dotted_part(name)) end
  elseif node_kind == "field" and #children(g) == 0 and kind(parent(g)) == "e-record" then
    -- `{ helper }` names `helper` with no identifier node. The field has no
    -- span, so its record says where it is.
    local key = referenced_key(g, get(NODES[g], "field", ""))
    if key ~= "" then record_reference(FUNCTIONS[key], reference_at(parent(g)), nil) end
  elseif node_kind == "text" and has_key(NODES[g], "value") and kind(parent(g)) == "exposed-lower-ident" then
    note_mention(NODES[g].value)
  end
end

-- A function holding a production call of a recursive function is an
-- entry into the recursion.
local functions_by_path = {}
for key in keys(FUNCTIONS) do push_at(functions_by_path, FUNCTIONS[key].path, FUNCTIONS[key]) end
for key in keys(FUNCTIONS) do
  local recursive = FUNCTIONS[key]
  if recursive.is_recursive then
    for c in recursive.prod_calls do
      for f in get(functions_by_path, c.path, {}) do
        if c.line >= f.line and c.line <= f.end_line then f.is_entry = true end
      end
    end
  end
end

-- ── the checks ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function display_name(func)
  if sub(func.owner, 1, 1) == "@" then return func.name end
  return func.owner .. "." .. func.name
end

-- A call's argument texts by position ("1", "2", ...), the receiver first.
-- A record argument gives its fields instead, as "N.field", so that
-- `{ needle, at: 0 }` is judged field by field.
function argument_texts(call)
  local out = {}
  local list = {}
  if call.receiver ~= 0 then push(list, call.receiver) end
  for a in call.args do push(list, a) end
  local n = 0
  for a in list do
    n = n + 1
    if kind(a) == "e-record" then
      for f in children(a) do
        local field_name = kind(f) == "field" and get(NODES[f], "field", "") or ""
        if field_name ~= "" then
          local value = children(f)
          out[n .. "." .. field_name] = #value > 0 and source_text(call.path, value[1]) or field_name
        end
      end
    else
      out[tostring(n)] = source_text(call.path, a)
    end
  end
  return out
end

-- No argument's text can be this, so it marks a slot where calls differ.
const DIFFERS = "\n differs"

-- For each argument slot of `calls`, by `argument_texts`'s keys, the text
-- every call gives it, or `DIFFERS`.
function agreed_argument_texts(calls)
  local agreed = {}
  local first = true
  for c in calls do
    local texts = argument_texts(c)
    if first then
      for k in keys(texts) do agreed[k] = texts[k] end
      first = false
    else
      for k in keys(agreed) do
        if agreed[k] ~= DIFFERS and (not has_key(texts, k) or texts[k] ~= agreed[k]) then agreed[k] = DIFFERS end
      end
      for k in keys(texts) do
        if not has_key(agreed, k) then agreed[k] = DIFFERS end
      end
    end
  end
  return agreed
end

function concatenated(lists)
  local out = {}
  for l in lists do
    for x in l do push(out, x) end
  end
  return out
end

function reads_better_inline(func)
  return func.prod_refs == 1 and func.value_refs == 0 and func.expect_refs == 0 and func.test_refs == 0 and func.doc_lines == 0 and func.is_wrapper and not func.is_recursive and not func.is_entry and not is_question_name(func.name)
end

const CLIENTS_READ = #CLIENT_FILES > 0 and (" and " .. #CLIENT_FILES .. " clients") or ""
const FILES_READ = " in the " .. #ROC_FILES .. " files read" .. CLIENTS_READ

-- A function something outside the files calls: what its header dictates, or
-- a member Roc calls by name.
function is_called_from_outside(func)
  if sub(func.owner, 1, 1) == "@" then return has_key(HEADER_NAMES[func.path].dictated, func.name) end
  return has_key(LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES, func.name)
end

-- A test of a library's API is a user of it, so `unused_api` keeps it.
function has_no_caller(func)
  local is_member = sub(func.owner, 1, 1) ~= "@"
  if TEST_REACH == "dead" and is_member and not is_library_api(func) then return func.prod_refs == 0 and func.mentions == 0 end
  return func.prod_refs == 0 and func.expect_refs == 0 and func.test_refs == 0 and func.mentions == 0
end

function is_test_only(func)
  return func.expect_refs + func.test_refs > 0
end

-- The text of one branch of an `if`, its braces left out when it holds one
-- statement.
function branch_text(path, g)
  if kind(g) == "e-block" then
    for k in children(g) do
      if kind(k) == "statements" and #children(k) == 1 then return source_text(path, children(k)[1]) end
    end
  end
  return source_text(path, g)
end

for key in sort(keys(FUNCTIONS)) do
  local func = FUNCTIONS[key]
  local name = display_name(func)
  local judged = not func.is_ambiguous and not is_test_file(func.path)
  if not is_test_file(func.path) and has_no_caller(func) and not is_called_from_outside(func) then
    if is_library_api(func) then
      report(func.path, func.line, "unused_api", "`" .. name .. "` is exposed, and nothing" .. FILES_READ .. " calls or tests it: API with no user here, or left behind?")
    elseif is_test_only(func) then
      report(func.path, func.line, "dead", "`" .. name .. "` has no production caller" .. FILES_READ .. ", only an expect or a test: delete it with its tests, or say who calls it")
    else
      report(func.path, func.line, "dead", "`" .. name .. "` has no caller" .. FILES_READ .. ", and no expect or test reaches it: delete it, or say who calls it")
    end
  end
  if judged and reads_better_inline(func) then
    report(func.path, func.line, "single", "`" .. name .. "` (" .. func.size .. ") has one caller" .. FILES_READ .. ", " .. func.prod_callers[1] .. ", and no expect, test or doc: read it inline there, or say why it stands alone")
  end
  if judged and #func.prod_calls >= 2 and func.value_refs == 0 then
    -- A slot the production calls agree on is `fixed` if the function's
    -- own calls agree with them too, and `entry` if they vary it.
    local outside = agreed_argument_texts(func.prod_calls)
    local all = agreed_argument_texts(concatenated({func.prod_calls, func.self_calls}))
    local own = #func.self_calls > 0 and (" and " .. #func.self_calls .. " of its own") or ""
    for k in sort(keys(outside)) do
      local v = outside[k]
      if v ~= DIFFERS and is_literal(v) then
        local said = "`" .. name .. "`'s argument " .. k .. " is `" .. v .. "` in all " .. #func.prod_calls .. " production calls"
        if all[k] ~= DIFFERS then
          if not is_library_api(func) then report(func.path, func.line, "fixed", said .. own .. FILES_READ .. ": no parameter, or an entry function that takes only what varies") end
        else
          report(func.path, func.line, "entry", said .. FILES_READ .. ", and its own calls vary it: an entry function that takes only what varies and passes `" .. v .. "` itself, its one outside call")
        end
      end
    end
  end
  if func.takes_empty_record_alone and not contains(func.name, "!") and not is_test_file(func.path) and func.doc_lines == 0 then
    report(func.path, func.line, "constant", "`" .. name .. "` takes `{}` alone and names no effect, so it gives the same value every call: a constant (`" .. func.name .. " = ...`), or a `!` if it has an effect")
  end
  if judged and #func.params > 1 and has_key(checker_types.real, func.path) then
    local every = concatenated({func.prod_calls, func.self_calls, func.test_calls})
    for i = 1, #func.params do
      local param = func.params[i]
      local ty = kind(param) == "p-ident" and roc_type_at(checker_types, "pat", func.path, NODES[param]) or nil
      if ty == "Bool" then
        local literal_calls = {}
        for c in every do
          local v = get(argument_texts(c), tostring(i), "")
          if has_key(BOOL_LITERALS, v) then push(literal_calls, c.path .. ":" .. c.line .. " `" .. v .. "`") end
        end
        if #literal_calls > 0 then report(func.path, func.line, "bool_param", "`" .. name .. "`'s parameter " .. i .. ", `" .. raw_text(param) .. "`, is a `Bool` (the checker's type) passed as a literal at " .. #literal_calls .. " of its " .. #every .. " calls (" .. join(take(literal_calls, 3), ", ") .. (#literal_calls > 3 and ", ..." or "") .. "): a flag a caller passes is a tag, named for what it means (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md)") end
      end
    end
  end
end

for g = 1, #NODES do
  if kind(g) == "e-if-then-else" and not is_test_file(NODE_PATH[g]) and has_key(CHECKED, NODE_PATH[g]) then
    local kids = children(g)
    local shown = #kids == 3 and branch_text(NODE_PATH[g], kids[2]) or "?"
    if shown ~= "?" and shown == branch_text(NODE_PATH[g], kids[3]) then
      report(NODE_PATH[g], NODES[g].line, "same_branches", "both branches of this `if` are `" .. sub(shown, 1, 40) .. "`: the condition decides nothing")
    end
  end
end

local counts = {}
for c in CHECKS do push(counts, c .. " " .. finding_counts[c]) end
print("check_boundaries (Roc): " .. #ROC_FILES .. " files" .. CLIENTS_READ .. ", " .. #keys(FUNCTIONS) .. " functions; " .. join(counts, ", ") .. house_note("check_boundaries"))
fail_if_refused("check_boundaries", parsed.refused, checker_types.unreached)

-- A plant's file name as the self-test reads it. A typed plant is a type
-- module, so `typed/BoolParam.roc` reads as `bool_param.roc`, and so does a
-- plant under `dead/`, as a package's header names its modules.
function plant_check_name(p)
  if starts_with(p, TYPED_PLANTS) or starts_with(p, DEAD_PLANTS) then return snake_case_plant_name(basename(p)) end
  return basename(p)
end

if SELF_TEST then
  local wrong = {}
  for c in CHECKS do
    local planted = 0
    for p in ROC_FILES do
      local base = plant_check_name(p)
      local planted_here = base == c .. ".roc" or starts_with(base, c .. "_")
      if planted_here then planted = planted + 1 end
      local fired_here = has_key(fired, p .. "|" .. c)
      if planted_here and not fired_here then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` does not fire on its plant " .. p) end
      if fired_here and not planted_here then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` fires on " .. p .. ", another check's plant") end
    end
    if planted == 0 then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` has no plant") end
    for p in CLIENT_FILES do
      if has_key(fired, p .. "|" .. c) then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` fires on the client " .. p .. ", which is read only for its calls") end
    end
  end
  if #CLIENT_FILES == 0 or #keys(TEST_PATHS) == 0 then push(wrong, "no client or no gate plant read") end
  for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end
  if #wrong > 0 then fail("check_boundaries self_test: " .. #wrong .. " plants wrong") end
  print("check_boundaries (Roc) self_test: PASS (each check fires on its plants alone, the quiet_ plants on none)")
end

wrap_long_lines

Long Roc lines shortened and groups laid out by the stacking rule, through trailing commas that roc fmt reads, on a work copy pass after pass until nothing changes, by the Roc library that is now the rule's one home, the lines left wide listed after.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.exists!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.mkdir!, Shale.print!, Shale.re_find!, Shale.re_replace!, Shale.read!, Shale.real!, Shale.remove_tree!, Shale.roc_tree!, Shale.run!, Shale.write!.
Roc: 725 lines in 4 files. Shale original: 405 lines, plus 540 lines in the 4 libraries it loads, which other recipes share.

Roc

It also imports Bytes, Stacking, Text from the shared Roc library.

cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines/wrap_long_lines.roc, 158 lines

## wrap_long_lines, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md): long
## Roc lines shortened, and with `tokens=N` groups laid out by the stacking
## rule, by trailing commas that `roc fmt` reads. Its launcher,
## cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines.shale, is how it is run, and its header says
## the rule, the rewrite and the list it prints. check_goldens.shale, beside
## this, holds its output and the files it rewrites to its goldens.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/wrap_long_lines.shale dir=roc width=100
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/wrap_long_lines.shale dir=app,platform tokens=6
##   shale cookbook:roc/wrap_long_lines.shale self_test=1
##
## The arguments: `dir` (`roc`; several, comma-separated), `width` (100),
## `tokens` (0, wide lines alone), `write` (`write=0` reports and writes
## nothing), `self_test` and `work_base`, the folder the work copies go in,
## which the launcher gives.
##
## This root reads the arguments, rewrites each folder (Rewrite) and prints
## the lines left wide (WideLines); SelfTest is the self-test. Groups,
## Stacking, Packed and Bytes are the cookbook's Roc library,
## cookbook/roc/lib/, the one home of the stacking rule.
## budget: steps=1000000000 read_bytes=2000000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 changes=5000 roc_cpu_ms=600000
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import lib.Stacking
import lib.Text
import Rewrite
import SelfTest
import WideLines

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	self_test = Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1"
	work_base = Shale.arg!("work_base", "scratch:")
	dirs_given = Shale.arg!("dir", "roc")
	width = integer_of!("width", Shale.arg!("width", "100"))
	tokens = if self_test {
		Stacking.stack_tokens
	} else {
		integer_of!("tokens", Shale.arg!("tokens", "0"))
	}
	write_given = Shale.arg!("write", "1")
	if write_given != "0" and write_given != "1" {
		Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: write=${write_given}: write must be 1 (the default) or 0")
	}
	write = self_test or write_given == "1"
	roc = Rewrite.roc_bin!(self_test)
	settings = { rule: { tokens, width }, roc, work_base }
	if self_test {
		SelfTest.run!(settings)
	} else {
		var $report = WideLines.fresh
		for dir in dirs_of!(dirs_given) {
			work = Rewrite.work_of!(dir, { self_test: Bool.False, work_base })
			done = match Rewrite.rewrite_in_work!(dir, { work, settings }) {
				Ok(finished) => finished
				Err(StillChanging(touched)) => {
					Shale.fail!(Rewrite.still_changing(touched))
					{ work, paths: [] }
				}
			}
			at = if write {
				Rewrite.write_back!(dir, done)
				dir
			} else {
				done.work
			}
			$report = WideLines.report_wide_lines!($report, { dir, at, paths: done.paths, width })
			Shale.remove_tree!(done.work)
		}
		remove_work_base!(work_base)
		report = $report
		said = if write {
			""
		} else {
			"report, nothing written: "
		}
		print_findings!("${said}${WideLines.summary(report, width)}", report.long)
		fail_if_refused!(report.refused)
	}
	if self_test {
		remove_work_base!(work_base)
	}
}

## The whole number an argument gives; another value stops the run, as
## Shale's `arg` does for an integer default. (Each `Shale.arg!` names its
## argument as a literal, so the launcher's check of the values finds it.)
integer_of! : Str, Str => U64
integer_of! = |name, given|
	match I64.from_str(given) {
		Ok(value) if value >= 0 => value.to_u64_wrap()
		Ok(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: ${name}=${given} is below 0")
			0
		}
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("`arg`: ${name}=${given} is not an integer, and its default is one")
			0
		}
	}

## The folders `dir=` names, each held to be a path and not an option.
dirs_of! : Str => List(Str)
dirs_of! = |given| {
	var $dirs = []
	for piece in given.split_on(",") {
		dir = Text.trim(piece)
		if dir.starts_with("-") {
			Shale.fail!("`wrap_long_lines`'s `dir` is \"${dir}\": a value that starts with `-` would be one of the program's options")
		}
		if dir != "" {
			$dirs = $dirs.append(dir)
		}
	}
	if $dirs.is_empty() {
		Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: dir= names no folder")
	}
	$dirs
}

## The work folder, when the launcher made a fresh one for want of a
## `scratch:` mount, removed once the run has finished.
remove_work_base! : Str => {}
remove_work_base! = |work_base| {
	if work_base != "scratch:" {
		Shale.remove_tree!(work_base)
	}
}

## The summary, each line listed, then the summary again
## (cookbook/findings.shale): the first copy survives a cut output, and a
## gate reads the last line.
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, listed| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(listed.is_empty()) {
		for line in listed {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

## The files Roc's parser refused, named, then a stop
## (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale's `fail_if_refused`); nothing when it refused
## none.
fail_if_refused! : List(Str) => {}
fail_if_refused! = |refused| {
	if !(refused.is_empty()) {
		for refusal in refused {
			Shale.print!("refused: ${refusal}")
		}
		refusals = "roc-ast refused ${refused.len().to_str()} files (named above)"
		why = "which have no tree to judge; every other file was judged"
		Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: ${refusals}, ${why}")
	}
}

cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines/Rewrite.roc, 271 lines

## The rewrite of a folder: its .roc files copied to a work copy, then pass
## after pass, each a trailing comma given to each line's group that should
## stack and taken from each stacked group that should sit on one line, with
## `roc fmt` run on the work copy after each, until a pass changes nothing.
## The changed files are written back only once the rewrite has finished, so
## a rewrite that never settles leaves the folder as it was. The rule and its
## pieces are the cookbook's Roc library's Stacking; the Roc is the tree's
## own (cookbook/roc/pinned.shale), run by its OS path.
import pf.Shale
import lib.Bytes
import lib.Stacking
import lib.Text

Rewrite := [].{

	## What a rewrite runs by: the stacking rule (`tokens` 0 wraps wide lines
	## alone), the Roc's OS path, and the folder the work copies go in.
	Settings : { rule : Stacking.Rule, roc : Str, work_base : Str }

	## A finished rewrite: the work copy that holds it, and the folder's .roc
	## files, each as its path inside the folder.
	Done : { work : Str, paths : List(Str) }

	## The most passes a rewrite makes.
	max_passes : U64
	max_passes = 8

	## The work copy of folder `dir`: the self-test's is a name of its own,
	## any other's is named for the folder's OS path.
	work_of! : Str, { self_test : Bool, work_base : Str } => Str
	work_of! = |dir, given|
		if given.self_test {
			Text.path_under(given.work_base, "roc_commas_work/self_test")
		} else {
			named = Shale.re_replace!(Shale.real!(dir), "[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_")
			Text.path_under(given.work_base, "roc_commas_work/${named}")
		}

	## The .roc files of folder `dir`, each as its path inside it.
	roc_paths_in_dir! : Str => List(Str)
	roc_paths_in_dir! = |dir| {
		cut = dir.count_utf8_bytes() + 1
		Shale.glob!("${dir}/**/*.roc").map(|path| Text.bytes_of(path, { start: cut, count: path.count_utf8_bytes() }))
	}

	## Rewrites the work copy `work` of folder `dir` until a pass changes
	## nothing, printing each pass. A rewrite still changing after
	## `max_passes` passes is `StillChanging`, with the files the last pass
	## changed, named as the folder's.
	rewrite_in_work! : Str, { work : Str, settings : Rewrite.Settings } => Try(Rewrite.Done, [StillChanging(List(Str))])
	rewrite_in_work! = |dir, at| {
		work = at.work
		rule = at.settings.rule
		paths = Rewrite.roc_paths_in_dir!(dir)
		fresh_work_copy!(dir, { work, paths })
		run_roc_fmt!(work, at.settings.roc)
		$pass : U64
		var $pass = 1
		$changed : U64
		var $changed = 1
		var $touched = []
		# A file's text when a pass last left it alone. A later pass would
		# leave the same text alone again, so it is not read for groups twice.
		var $settled = Dict.empty()
		while $changed > 0 and $pass <= Rewrite.max_passes {
			$changed = 0
			$touched = []
			for path in paths {
				text = Rewrite.read_text!("${work}/${path}")
				if $settled.get(path) != Ok(text) {
					n = rewrite_file!("${work}/${path}", { text, rule })
					if n > 0 {
						$changed = $changed + n
						$touched = $touched.append("${dir}/${path}")
					} else {
						$settled = $settled.insert(path, text)
					}
				}
			}
			Shale.print!("${dir}: pass ${$pass.to_str()}: ${$changed.to_str()} trailing commas added or taken out")
			run_roc_fmt!(work, at.settings.roc)
			$pass = $pass + 1
		}
		if $changed > 0 {
			Err(StillChanging($touched))
		} else {
			Ok({ work, paths })
		}
	}

	## The stop a rewrite still changing makes, naming the files it changed.
	still_changing : List(Str) -> Str
	still_changing = |touched|
		"wrap_long_lines: still changing after ${Rewrite.max_passes.to_str()} passes, so no file was written: ${Str.join_with(touched, ", ")}"

	## Writes each file the rewrite changed back to folder `dir`, and says
	## how many.
	write_back! : Str, Rewrite.Done => {}
	write_back! = |dir, done| {
		var $changed = []
		for path in done.paths {
			text = Rewrite.read_text!("${done.work}/${path}")
			if text != Rewrite.read_text!("${dir}/${path}") {
				$changed = $changed.append({ path: "${dir}/${path}", text })
			}
		}
		for change in $changed {
			Shale.write!(change.path, change.text)
		}
		Shale.print!("${dir}: ${$changed.len().to_str()} files rewritten")
	}

	## A file's text; a file gone since the glob stops the run.
	read_text! : Str => Str
	read_text! = |path|
		match Shale.read!(path) {
			Found(text) => text
			Missing => {
				Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: no file ${path}")
				""
			}
		}

	## Whether a line is a comment's, which no trailing comma shortens.
	is_comment : Str -> Bool
	is_comment = |text| Text.trim(text).starts_with("#")

	## The OS path of the Roc to rewrite with: in a self-test the pin every
	## recipe's self-test runs (pinned.shale's `SELF_TEST_PIN`, read there),
	## else the one the `roc-version` where the run starts names.
	roc_bin! : Bool => Str
	roc_bin! = |self_test| {
		pin = if self_test {
			self_test_pin!({})
		} else {
			if !(Shale.exists!("roc-version")) {
				Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: no roc-version where the run starts: run it from the repository's root, whose roc-version pins its Roc")
			}
			Text.trim(Rewrite.read_text!("roc-version"))
		}
		roc = "tools:roc-${pin}/roc"
		if !(Shale.exists!(roc)) {
			Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: no ${roc}: install Roc ${pin} into ~/tools/roc-${pin}/ (roc-apps's toolchain release carries it)")
		}
		Shale.real!(roc)
	}
}

## The work copy made afresh: the folder's .roc files copied into it.
fresh_work_copy! : Str, { work : Str, paths : List(Str) } => {}
fresh_work_copy! = |dir, copy| {
	if Shale.exists!(copy.work) {
		Shale.remove_tree!(copy.work)
	}
	Shale.mkdir!(copy.work)
	for path in copy.paths {
		Shale.write!("${copy.work}/${path}", Rewrite.read_text!("${dir}/${path}"))
	}
}

## `roc fmt` run on the work copy; a file that does not parse stops the run,
## after its output.
run_roc_fmt! : Str, Str => {}
run_roc_fmt! = |work, roc| {
	result = Shale.run!({
		argv: [roc, "fmt", Shale.real!(work)],
		keep: Tail(20),
		timeout_ms: 60000,
		want: "",
	})
	if result.code != 0 {
		Shale.print!(result.out)
		Shale.fail!("roc fmt failed")
	}
}

## One pass over one file, whose text is `text`: the groups that should
## unstack lose their trailing commas, then each code line gets one for its
## group that should stack, if any; the file is written when any changed,
## and the answer is how many did.
rewrite_file! : Str, { text : Str, rule : Stacking.Rule } => U64
rewrite_file! = |path, given| {
	rule = given.rule
	source_lines = given.text.split_on("\n")
	unstacked = if rule.tokens > 0 {
		match Stacking.groups_to_unstack(source_lines, rule) {
			Ok(found) => found
			Err(NoComma(line)) => {
				Shale.fail!("groups: line ${line.to_str()} does not end in its group's trailing comma")
				[]
			}
		}
	} else {
		[]
	}
	unstacked_lines = Stacking.without_trailing_commas(source_lines, unstacked)
	reachable = Stacking.without_targets_section(unstacked_lines)
	var $lines = unstacked_lines
	$changed : U64
	var $changed = unstacked.len()
	$index : U64
	var $index = 0
	for text in unstacked_lines {
		if !(Rewrite.is_comment(text)) {
			match line_with_comma(reachable.get($index) ?? "", rule) {
				Ok(with_comma) => {
					$lines = $lines.set($index, with_comma) ?? crash "wrap_long_lines: a line past the file's end"
					$changed = $changed + 1
				}
				Err(_) => {}
			}
		}
		$index = $index + 1
	}
	if $changed > 0 {
		Shale.write!(path, Str.join_with($lines, "\n"))
	}
	$changed
}

## The line with a trailing comma for its outermost group that should
## stack, or else, when it is wider than the width, for the group that
## stacking brings within it. A line of data gets none.
line_with_comma : Str, Stacking.Rule -> Try(Str, [NoComma])
line_with_comma = |text, rule| {
	few_commas = rule.tokens == 0 or commas_before_the_last(text) < Stacking.stack_items - 1
	if Bytes.line_width(text) <= rule.width and few_commas {
		Err(NoComma)
	} else {
		match Stacking.group_to_stack(text, rule) {
			Ok(group) => Ok(Stacking.with_trailing_comma({ line: text, group }))
			Err(_) => Err(NoComma)
		}
	}
}

## How many commas a line holds, not counting one that ends it. A group of
## `stack_items` items that opens and closes on the line holds one fewer at
## least, so a line that fits with fewer has no group to stack. Counting is
## far cheaper than reading the line's groups, and most of a data file's
## lines are like `{ x: 0.5, y: 0.25 },`.
commas_before_the_last : Str -> U64
commas_before_the_last = |text| {
	bytes = text.to_utf8()
	commas = bytes.count_if(|byte| byte == ',')
	if Bytes.trimmed_end(bytes).last() == Ok(',') {
		commas - 1
	} else {
		commas
	}
}

## pinned.shale's `SELF_TEST_PIN`, the one home of the self-tests' Roc.
self_test_pin! : {} => Str
self_test_pin! = |{}| {
	pinned = "cookbook:roc/pinned.shale"
	groups = match Shale.re_find!(
		Rewrite.read_text!(pinned),
		"\nconst SELF_TEST_PIN = \"([^\"]+)\"",
	) {
		Found(found) => found.groups
		NoMatch => []
	}
	match groups {
		[pin, ..] => pin
		[] => {
			Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: no SELF_TEST_PIN in ${pinned}")
			""
		}
	}
}

cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines/SelfTest.roc, 171 lines

## The recipe's self-test, the Shale original's: the plants in
## cookbook/roc/plants/wrap_long_lines/ are copied into the work folder and
## rewritten there with the rule's six tokens and the self-tests' Roc. The
## rewrite must end, each plant must come out as its `.want` file, no group
## may be left to stack or to unstack, and the lines left wide must be
## exactly `long_plants`' listed, with `wide_string_plants` wide strings and
## `data_plants` lines of data counted. Then `too_deep/too_deep.roc`, one
## group deeper than the passes reach, must stop the rewrite, naming its
## file, and be left as it was.
import pf.Shale
import lib.Stacking
import lib.Text
import Rewrite
import WideLines

SelfTest := [].{

	## The self-test, its copies and work copies under `settings.work_base`.
	run! : Rewrite.Settings => {}
	run! = |settings| {
		dir = Text.path_under(settings.work_base, "wrap_long_lines")
		work = Rewrite.work_of!(dir, { self_test: Bool.True, work_base: settings.work_base })
		fresh_copies!(dir, plants)
		match Rewrite.rewrite_in_work!(dir, { work, settings }) {
			Ok(done) => {
				Rewrite.write_back!(dir, done)
				Shale.remove_tree!(done.work)
			}
			Err(StillChanging(touched)) => Shale.fail!(Rewrite.still_changing(touched))
		}
		$bad : U64
		var $bad = 0
		for plant in Shale.glob!("${plants}/*.roc") {
			$bad = $bad + plant_wrong!(plant, { dir, rule: settings.rule })
		}
		$bad = $bad + report_wrong!(dir, settings.rule.width)
		if $bad > 0 {
			Shale.fail!("${$bad.to_str()} checks failed")
		}
		if Shale.exists!(work) {
			Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: a finished rewrite should remove its work copy, ${work}")
		}
		fresh_copies!(dir, "${plants}/too_deep")
		named = Rewrite.still_changing(["${dir}/too_deep.roc"])
		stopped = match Rewrite.rewrite_in_work!(dir, { work, settings }) {
			Ok(_) => Bool.False
			Err(StillChanging(touched)) => Rewrite.still_changing(touched) == named
		}
		if !(stopped) {
			Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: too_deep.roc should stop with `${named.drop_prefix("wrap_long_lines: ")}`")
		}
		copy = Rewrite.read_text!("${dir}/too_deep.roc")
		if copy != Rewrite.read_text!("${plants}/too_deep/too_deep.roc") {
			Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: a rewrite that stops should leave too_deep.roc as it was")
		}
		Shale.print!("ok   too_deep.roc: stops naming its file, and is left as it was")
		Shale.remove_tree!(work)
		Shale.remove_tree!(dir)
		Shale.print!("PASS: the rewrite ends, every plant comes out as its .want, no group is left to stack or to unstack, the lines left wide are listed or counted, and a rewrite past its passes stops naming its file and changes none")
	}
}

## The plants, whose `*.roc` the self-test rewrites.
plants : Str
plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/wrap_long_lines"

## The plant lines left wide with nothing to stack.
long_plants : List(Str)
long_plants = ["function_type.roc:4"]

## How many plant lines are wide only for their strings.
wide_string_plants : U64
wide_string_plants = 1

## How many plant lines are numeric data.
data_plants : U64
data_plants = 2

## The start of a verdict's line.
verdict : Bool -> Str
verdict = |ok|
	if ok {
		"ok   "
	} else {
		"FAIL "
	}

## Folder `dir` made afresh with a copy of each `*.roc` in folder `from`.
fresh_copies! : Str, Str => {}
fresh_copies! = |dir, from| {
	if Shale.exists!(dir) {
		Shale.remove_tree!(dir)
	}
	Shale.mkdir!(dir)
	for plant in Shale.glob!("${from}/*.roc") {
		Shale.write!("${dir}/${Text.basename(plant)}", Rewrite.read_text!(plant))
	}
}

## One plant's rewrite held to its `.want`, and to no group left to stack or
## to unstack, a line printed for each wrong: the answer is how many were.
plant_wrong! : Str, { dir : Str, rule : Stacking.Rule } => U64
plant_wrong! = |plant, given| {
	name = Text.basename(plant)
	want = "${plants}/${name.drop_suffix(".roc")}.want"
	got = Rewrite.read_text!("${given.dir}/${name}")
	ok = got == Rewrite.read_text!(want)
	Shale.print!("${verdict(ok)}${name}: comes out as its .want")
	$bad : U64
	var $bad = if ok {
		0
	} else {
		1
	}
	got_lines = got.split_on("\n")
	$number : U64
	var $number = 0
	for text in Stacking.without_targets_section(got_lines) {
		$number = $number + 1
		left = !(Rewrite.is_comment(text)) and Stacking.group_to_stack(text, given.rule) != Err(NoGroup)
		if left {
			Shale.print!("FAIL ${name}:${$number.to_str()}: a group left to stack: ${Text.trim(text)}")
			$bad = $bad + 1
		}
	}
	unstacked = match Stacking.groups_to_unstack(got_lines, given.rule) {
		Ok(found) => found
		Err(NoComma(line)) => {
			Shale.fail!("groups: line ${line.to_str()} does not end in its group's trailing comma")
			[]
		}
	}
	for found in unstacked {
		Shale.print!("FAIL ${name}:${found.group.line.to_str()}: a group left to unstack")
		$bad = $bad + 1
	}
	$bad
}

## The lines the rewrite left wide held to `long_plants`, and the wide
## strings and data counted, a line printed for each: the answer is how many
## were wrong.
report_wrong! : Str, U64 => U64
report_wrong! = |dir, width| {
	report = WideLines.report_wide_lines!(
		WideLines.fresh,
		{ dir, at: dir, paths: Rewrite.roc_paths_in_dir!(dir), width },
	)
	cut = dir.count_utf8_bytes() + 1
	listed = report.long.map(
		|line| {
			place = Text.before_first(line, " ")
			Text.bytes_of(place, { start: cut, count: place.count_utf8_bytes() })
		},
	)
	list_ok = Text.sort_bytewise(listed) == Text.sort_bytewise(long_plants)
	Shale.print!("${verdict(list_ok)}the list of lines left wide is ${Str.join_with(long_plants, ", ")} (${Str.join_with(report.long, "; ")})")
	counts = "${report.wide_strings.to_str()} lines wide only for their strings and ${report.data.to_str()} of numeric data"
	wanted = "want ${wide_string_plants.to_str()} and ${data_plants.to_str()} (${report.refused.len().to_str()} refused)"
	counts_ok = report.wide_strings == wide_string_plants and report.data == data_plants and report.refused.is_empty()
	Shale.print!("${verdict(counts_ok)}${counts}, counted and not listed, ${wanted}")
	$bad : U64
	var $bad = 0
	if !(list_ok) {
		$bad = $bad + 1
	}
	if !(counts_ok) {
		$bad = $bad + 1
	}
	$bad
}

## The lines a rewrite leaves wider than the width. A comment, a line wide
## only for the text of its strings (by Roc's parser, as check_stacking's
## `wide string`) and a line of numeric data, which stays packed, are
## counted, as no trailing comma shortens one; any other is listed, as
## `path:line (width): nothing to stack: text`. Only a file with a wide line
## is parsed, for its strings.
import pf.Shale
import lib.Bytes
import lib.Stacking
import lib.Text
import Rewrite

WideLines := [].{

	## The lines left wide so far: those listed, the counts of the rest, and
	## why each file roc-ast refused was refused.
	Report : {
		long : List(Str),
		wide_strings : U64,
		data : U64,
		comments : U64,
		refused : List(Str),
	}

	## A report with nothing in it yet.
	fresh : WideLines.Report
	fresh = { long: [], wide_strings: 0, data: 0, comments: 0, refused: [] }

	## The report with the lines wider than `width` in the files `paths` of
	## folder `at` added, each named as folder `dir`'s.
	report_wide_lines! : WideLines.Report,
	{
		dir : Str,
		at : Str,
		paths : List(Str),
		width : U64,
	} => WideLines.Report
	report_wide_lines! = |before, given| {
		width = given.width
		is_wide = |text| Bytes.line_width(text) > width
		var $wide = []
		for path in given.paths {
			at_path = "${given.at}/${path}"
			if Rewrite.read_text!(at_path).split_on("\n").any(is_wide) {
				$wide = $wide.append(at_path)
			}
		}
		wide = $wide
		if wide.is_empty() {
			return before
		}
		var $report = before
		var $parsed = []
		for file in Shale.roc_tree!(wide) {
			if file.err == "" {
				$parsed = $parsed.append(file)
			} else if file.err.starts_with(file.path) {
				$report = { ..$report, refused: $report.refused.append(file.err) }
			} else {
				$report = { ..$report, refused: $report.refused.append("${file.path}: ${file.err}") }
			}
		}
		cut = given.at.count_utf8_bytes()
		for file in $parsed {
			source_lines = Rewrite.read_text!(file.path).split_on("\n")
			strings = match Stacking.string_columns_on_lines(file.nodes, source_lines) {
				Ok(by_line) => by_line
				Err(CrossesLine(line)) => {
					Shale.fail!("wrap_long_lines: ${file.path}: line ${line.to_str()}: a run of string text crosses a line")
					Dict.empty()
				}
			}
			named = "${given.dir}${Text.bytes_of(file.path, { start: cut, count: file.path.count_utf8_bytes() })}"
			$number : U64
			var $number = 0
			for text in source_lines {
				$number = $number + 1
				line_width = Bytes.line_width(text)
				if line_width > width {
					$report = judged_line(
						$report,
						{
							text,
							line_width,
							string_width: strings.get($number) ?? 0,
							place: "${named}:${$number.to_str()}",
							width,
						},
					)
				}
			}
		}
		$report
	}

	## The report's counts, as its summary line says them.
	summary : WideLines.Report, U64 -> Str
	summary = |report, width| {
		listed = "${report.long.len().to_str()} code lines with nothing to stack"
		counted = "${report.wide_strings.to_str()} wide only for their strings, ${report.data.to_str()} of numeric data, ${report.comments.to_str()} comment lines"
		"still over ${width.to_str()}: ${listed}, ${counted}"
	}
}

## The report with one line wider than the width counted or listed.
judged_line : WideLines.Report,
{
	text : Str,
	line_width : U64,
	string_width : U64,
	place : Str,
	width : U64,
} -> WideLines.Report
judged_line = |report, line|
	if Rewrite.is_comment(line.text) {
		{ ..report, comments: report.comments + 1 }
	} else if line.line_width - line.string_width <= line.width {
		{ ..report, wide_strings: report.wide_strings + 1 }
	} else if Stacking.is_data_line(line.text, line.width) {
		{ ..report, data: report.data + 1 }
	} else {
		shown = Str.from_utf8_lossy(Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.span(line.text.to_utf8(), 1, 140)))
		listed = "${line.place} (${line.line_width.to_str()}): nothing to stack: ${shown}"
		{ ..report, long: report.long.append(listed) }
	}
