-- Shorten long Roc lines by letting `roc fmt` lay them out. roc fmt never
-- wraps a line, but it puts the items of a record, list, call or lambda's
-- arguments one to a line when the last item has a trailing comma. For each
-- code line wider than `width`, this script adds that comma to the widest
-- group of two or more items whose stacking brings the line within `width`:
-- the text up to its opening bracket fits, and so does its closing bracket
-- with what follows it (groups.shale's `group_to_wrap`). A group beside the
-- wide part, as a list pattern in a `match` arm whose string makes the line
-- wide, is left alone, and so are a function type's arguments, which can't
-- take the comma. It runs roc fmt, and repeats until no line changes; a
-- folder still changing after 8 passes stops the run, naming its files. The
-- passes work on a copy of the folder's .roc files under
-- `scratch:roc_commas_work/`, and the changed files are written back only
-- once the rewrite has finished, so a run that stops, on a pass too many or
-- on a budget, leaves the folder as it was. Under a mounts file with no
-- `scratch:` mount, the copies go in a fresh hidden folder at the root
-- instead (`.wrap_long_lines.XXXXXX`, named in the output), removed when the
-- run ends; a run that stops leaves it, for `git status` to show.
--
-- Then it lists each code line still too wide, as `path:line (width): why:
-- text`, `why` being `nothing to stack`: no group whose stacking would bring
-- it within `width`. A line wide only for the text of its strings, by Roc's
-- parser (as check_stacking.shale's `wide string`), and a comment line are
-- counted, not listed, as no trailing comma shortens either; so is a line
-- of numeric data, which stays packed (below). The list is
-- printed between its counts, as cookbook/findings.shale describes. It runs
-- the Roc that the repository's roc-version file names.
--
-- With `tokens=N`, the script holds the folder to roc-style.md's stacking
-- rule, whose six tokens are `tokens=6`, whatever a line's width: a group of
-- three or more items and N or more tokens gets the trailing comma, and a
-- stacked group that should sit on one line loses it, which is how `roc fmt`
-- is asked to join it. A group and its tokens are read as check_stacking.shale reads
-- them (cookbook/roc/groups.shale), so after `tokens=6` check_stacking.shale finds no
-- group left to stack or to unstack. A line's outermost group goes first, and
-- the next pass reaches the groups inside it. A function type's arguments and
-- a row of literals are left alone, as check_stacking.shale leaves them, and so is a
-- platform header's `targets:` section, which `roc fmt` lays out by itself.
--
-- The arguments:
--   dir     the folders to rewrite, `roc` by default; several may be given,
--           separated by commas, each rewritten in turn.
--   width   the widest a line may be, 100 by default.
--   tokens  the stacking rule's tokens, as above; 0 (the default) wraps
--           wide lines alone.
--   write   with `write=0`, the rewrite runs in the work copy, the list is
--           of the lines it would leave, and no folder is written: a
--           report.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines.shale dir=roc width=100
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines.shale dir=app,platform tokens=6
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/wrap_long_lines.shale dir=roc tokens=6 write=0
--   shale cookbook:roc/wrap_long_lines.shale self_test=1
--
-- `self_test=1` copies the plants in `cookbook/roc/plants/wrap_long_lines/` to
-- `scratch:wrap_long_lines/` (or the hidden folder above), rewrites them there with `tokens=6` and the
-- self-test's Roc, and checks that the rewrite ends, that each plant comes
-- out as its `.want` file, that no group is left to stack or to unstack, and
-- that the list holds exactly `LONG_PLANTS`' lines and counts
-- `WIDE_STRING_PLANTS` wide strings and `DATA_PLANTS` lines of data.
-- `at_the_cap.roc` nests as deep as 8 passes reach, and `too_deep/` one group
-- deeper, which has to stop the rewrite, name its file and leave it as it was.
--
-- Numeric data stays packed, as groups.shale's is_data_line and
-- is_number_data say: a number list never stacks, and nothing on a line wider
-- than `width` that holds one does. `numbers.roc` in the plants checks both
-- and that a list of names beside them still stacks.
--
-- roc-apps' canvas_apps/safari, with its 70,000-byte lines of polygon data,
-- takes about 160,000,000 steps with `tokens=6`.
--
-- budget: steps=1000000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 changes=5000

use("cookbook:findings.shale")
use("./pinned.shale")
use("./groups.shale")
use("./parsed.shale")
const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/wrap_long_lines"

-- Where the work copies go: `scratch:` when the mounts file has it, else a
-- fresh hidden folder at the root, which the run removes when it ends.
function work_base()
  if attempt(real, "scratch:.").ok then return "scratch:" end
  local base = fresh_dir("", ".wrap_long_lines")
  print("wrap_long_lines: no `scratch:` mount, so the work copies go in " .. base .. ", removed when the run ends")
  return base
end

const WORK_BASE = work_base()
const SELF_TEST_DIR = path_under(WORK_BASE, "wrap_long_lines")
const DIRS_ARG = SELF_TEST and SELF_TEST_DIR or arg("dir", "roc")
const WIDTH = arg("width", 100)
const TOKENS = SELF_TEST and STACK_TOKENS or arg("tokens", 0)
const WRITE_ARG = arg("write", "1")
if WRITE_ARG ~= "0" and WRITE_ARG ~= "1" then fail("wrap_long_lines: write=" .. WRITE_ARG .. ": write must be 1 (the default) or 0") end
const WRITE = SELF_TEST or WRITE_ARG == "1"
const MAX_PASSES = 8
const ROC = roc_bin("wrap_long_lines", SELF_TEST)

-- The self-test's list: the plant lines left wide with nothing to stack, and
-- how many lines are wide only for their strings.
const LONG_PLANTS = {"function_type.roc:4"}
const WIDE_STRING_PLANTS = 1
const DATA_PLANTS = 2

function is_comment(line)
  return starts_with(trim(line), "#")
end

-- The folders of `dir=`, each held to be a path and not an option.
function dirs_of(text)
  local out = {}
  for d in split(text, ",") do
    local dir = trim(d)
    not_option("wrap_long_lines", "dir", dir)
    if dir ~= "" then push(out, dir) end
  end
  if #out == 0 then fail("wrap_long_lines: dir= names no folder") end
  return out
end

function roc_files(dir)
  local out = {}
  for e in walk_all(dir) do
    if e.kind == "file" and ends_with(e.path, ".roc") then push(out, e.path) end
  end
  return out
end

-- The .roc files of `dir`, each as its path inside it.
function roc_paths_in_dir(dir)
  local out = {}
  for path in roc_files(dir) do push(out, sub(path, #dir + 2)) end
  return out
end

-- The rewrite of `dir` works on a copy of its .roc files, so a run that
-- stops, on a budget or a pass too many, leaves the folder as it was.
function work_of(dir)
  if SELF_TEST then return path_under(WORK_BASE, "roc_commas_work/self_test") end
  return path_under(WORK_BASE, "roc_commas_work/" .. re_replace(real(dir), "[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_"))
end

function fresh_work_copy(dir, work, paths)
  if is_dir(work) then remove_tree(work) end
  mkdir(work)
  for p in paths do replace(work .. "/" .. p, read(dir .. "/" .. p)) end
end

-- Writes each file the rewrite changed back to the folder. It reads them all
-- first and checks that what is left of the budgets covers every write, so
-- the folder gets all of the rewrite or none of it.
function write_back(dir, work, paths)
  local changed = {}
  local bytes = 0
  for p in paths do
    local text = read(work .. "/" .. p)
    if text ~= read(dir .. "/" .. p) then
      push(changed, {path = dir .. "/" .. p, text = text})
      bytes = bytes + #text
    end
  end
  local left = budget()
  if left.changes < #changed + 1 or left.change_bytes < bytes or left.steps < 2 * bytes + 1000 * #changed + 100000 then
    fail("wrap_long_lines: too little budget left to write the " .. #changed .. " changed files, so none was written")
  end
  for c in changed do replace(c.path, c.text) end
  print(dir .. ": " .. #changed .. " files rewritten")
end

function run_roc_fmt(work)
  local r = run({ROC, "fmt", real(work)}, {timeout_ms = 60000, tail = 20})
  if r.code ~= 0 then
    print(r.out)
    fail("roc fmt failed")
  end
end

-- How many commas line `l` holds, not counting one that ends it. A group of
-- STACK_ITEMS items that opens and closes on the line holds STACK_ITEMS - 1 of
-- them at least, and a comma that ends the line is inside no such group, so a
-- line that fits with fewer has no group to stack. Counting is far cheaper
-- than reading the line's groups, and most of a data file's lines are like
-- `{ x: 0.5, y: 0.25 },`.
function commas_before_the_last(l)
  local commas = #split(l, ",") - 1
  if ends_with(trim_end(l), ",") then commas = commas - 1 end
  return commas
end

-- Line `l` with a trailing comma for its outermost group that should stack,
-- or else, when it is wider than WIDTH, for groups.shale's `group_to_wrap`.
-- nil when it gets none. A line of data, by groups.shale's is_data_line,
-- gets none.
function line_with_comma(l)
  if line_width(l) <= WIDTH and (TOKENS == 0 or commas_before_the_last(l) < STACK_ITEMS - 1) then return nil end
  local g = group_to_stack(l, TOKENS, WIDTH)
  if g == nil then return nil end
  return with_trailing_comma(l, g)
end

-- Takes the trailing comma from each group of the file at `path`, whose text
-- is `text`, that should unstack, adds one to each code line that should get
-- one, and returns how many groups and lines it changed.
function rewrite_trailing_commas(path, text)
  local ls = split(text, "\n")
  local unstacked = {}
  if TOKENS > 0 then unstacked = groups_to_unstack(ls, TOKENS, WIDTH) end
  ls = without_trailing_commas(ls, unstacked)
  local reachable = without_targets_section(ls)
  local changed = #unstacked
  for i = 1, #ls do
    if not is_comment(ls[i]) then
      local with_comma = line_with_comma(reachable[i])
      if with_comma ~= nil then
        ls[i] = with_comma
        changed = changed + 1
      end
    end
  end
  if changed > 0 then replace(path, join(ls, "\n")) end
  return changed
end

-- Rewrites commas and runs roc fmt in `dir`'s work copy until a pass changes
-- nothing. Files still changing after MAX_PASSES stop the run, since the list
-- of long lines would otherwise judge a rewrite that never finished. Returns
-- `{work, paths}`, the work copy holding the rewrite.
function rewrite_in_work(dir)
  local work = work_of(dir)
  local paths = roc_paths_in_dir(dir)
  fresh_work_copy(dir, work, paths)
  run_roc_fmt(work)
  local pass = 1
  local changed = 1
  local touched = {}
  -- A file's text when a pass last left it alone. A later pass would leave
  -- the same text alone again, so it is not read for groups a second time.
  local settled = {}
  while changed > 0 and pass <= MAX_PASSES do
    changed = 0
    touched = {}
    for p in paths do
      local text = read(work .. "/" .. p)
      if not has_key(settled, p) or settled[p] ~= text then
        local n = rewrite_trailing_commas(work .. "/" .. p, text)
        if n > 0 then
          changed = changed + n
          push(touched, dir .. "/" .. p)
        else
          settled[p] = text
        end
      end
    end
    print(dir .. ": pass " .. pass .. ": " .. changed .. " trailing commas added or taken out")
    run_roc_fmt(work)
    pass = pass + 1
  end
  if changed > 0 then fail("wrap_long_lines: still changing after " .. MAX_PASSES .. " passes, so no file was written: " .. join(touched, ", ")) end
  return {work = work, paths = paths}
end

-- Rewrites `dir` and writes it back (with WRITE).
function rewrite_dir(dir)
  local r = rewrite_in_work(dir)
  if WRITE then write_back(dir, r.work, r.paths) end
  remove_tree(r.work)
  return nil
end

-- The self-test's folder rewritten, for its `attempt`, which takes no
-- arguments.
function rewrite_self_test_dir()
  return rewrite_dir(SELF_TEST_DIR)
end

-- The lines wider than WIDTH in the files `paths` of folder `at`, named as
-- `dir`'s, added to `report`: a comment and a line wide only for its strings'
-- text are counted, any other is listed. Only a file with a wide line is
-- parsed, for its strings; a file roc-ast refuses goes in `report.refused`.
function report_wide_lines(report, dir, at, paths)
  local wide = {}
  for p in paths do
    for l in lines(read(at .. "/" .. p)) do
      if line_width(l) > WIDTH then
        push(wide, at .. "/" .. p)
        break
      end
    end
  end
  if #wide == 0 then return nil end
  local parsed = parse_roc_files(wide)
  for r in parsed.refused do push(report.refused, r) end
  for f in parsed.files do
    local ls = split(read(f.path), "\n")
    local strings = string_columns_on_lines(f.nodes, ls, "wrap_long_lines: " .. f.path)
    local named = dir .. sub(f.path, #at + 1)
    for i = 1, #ls do
      local w = line_width(ls[i])
      if w > WIDTH then
        if is_comment(ls[i]) then
          report.comments = report.comments + 1
        elseif w - get(strings, "" .. i, 0) <= WIDTH then
          report.wide_strings = report.wide_strings + 1
        elseif is_data_line(ls[i], WIDTH) then
          report.data = report.data + 1
        else
          push(report.long, named .. ":" .. i .. " (" .. w .. "): nothing to stack: " .. trim(sub(ls[i], 1, 140)))
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return nil
end

function fresh_report()
  return {long = {}, wide_strings = 0, data = 0, comments = 0, refused = {}}
end

function report_summary(report)
  return "still over " .. WIDTH .. ": " .. #report.long .. " code lines with nothing to stack, " .. report.wide_strings .. " wide only for their strings, " .. report.data .. " of numeric data, " .. report.comments .. " comment lines"
end

function fresh_copies(plants)
  if is_dir(SELF_TEST_DIR) then remove_tree(SELF_TEST_DIR) end
  mkdir(SELF_TEST_DIR)
  for p in glob(plants .. "/*.roc") do replace(SELF_TEST_DIR .. "/" .. basename(p), read(p)) end
end

function self_test()
  local dir = SELF_TEST_DIR
  fresh_copies(PLANTS)
  rewrite_dir(dir)
  local bad = 0
  for p in glob(PLANTS .. "/*.roc") do
    local name = basename(p)
    local want = PLANTS .. "/" .. sub(name, 1, #name - 4) .. ".want"
    local got = read(dir .. "/" .. name)
    local ok = got == read(want)
    print((ok and "ok   " or "FAIL ") .. name .. ": comes out as its .want")
    if not ok then bad = bad + 1 end
    local reachable = without_targets_section(split(got, "\n"))
    for n = 1, #reachable do
      local l = reachable[n]
      if not is_comment(l) and group_to_stack(l, TOKENS, WIDTH) ~= nil then
        print("FAIL " .. name .. ":" .. n .. ": a group left to stack: " .. trim(l))
        bad = bad + 1
      end
    end
    for g in groups_to_unstack(split(got, "\n"), TOKENS, WIDTH) do
      print("FAIL " .. name .. ":" .. g.line .. ": a group left to unstack")
      bad = bad + 1
    end
  end
  -- The list after the rewrite: exactly LONG_PLANTS' lines, and the wide
  -- strings counted.
  local report = fresh_report()
  report_wide_lines(report, dir, dir, roc_paths_in_dir(dir))
  local listed = {}
  for l in report.long do push(listed, sub(split(l, " ")[1], #dir + 2)) end
  local list_ok = join(sort(listed), ",") == join(sort(LONG_PLANTS), ",")
  print((list_ok and "ok   " or "FAIL ") .. "the list of lines left wide is " .. join(LONG_PLANTS, ", ") .. " (" .. join(report.long, "; ") .. ")")
  if not list_ok then bad = bad + 1 end
  local wide_ok = report.wide_strings == WIDE_STRING_PLANTS and report.data == DATA_PLANTS and #report.refused == 0
  print((wide_ok and "ok   " or "FAIL ") .. report.wide_strings .. " lines wide only for their strings and " .. report.data .. " of numeric data, counted and not listed, want " .. WIDE_STRING_PLANTS .. " and " .. DATA_PLANTS .. " (" .. #report.refused .. " refused)")
  if not wide_ok then bad = bad + 1 end
  if bad > 0 then fail(bad .. " checks failed") end
  if is_dir(work_of(dir)) then fail("wrap_long_lines: a finished rewrite should remove its work copy, " .. work_of(dir)) end
  fresh_copies(PLANTS .. "/too_deep")
  local stopped = attempt(rewrite_self_test_dir)
  local named = "still changing after " .. MAX_PASSES .. " passes, so no file was written: " .. dir .. "/too_deep.roc"
  if stopped.ok or not contains(stopped.error, named) then fail("wrap_long_lines: too_deep.roc should stop with `" .. named .. "`") end
  if read(dir .. "/too_deep.roc") ~= read(PLANTS .. "/too_deep/too_deep.roc") then fail("wrap_long_lines: a rewrite that stops should leave too_deep.roc as it was") end
  print("ok   too_deep.roc: stops naming its file, and is left as it was")
  remove_tree(work_of(dir))
  remove_tree(SELF_TEST_DIR)
  print("PASS: the rewrite ends, every plant comes out as its .want, no group is left to stack or to unstack, the lines left wide are listed or counted, and a rewrite past its passes stops naming its file and changes none")
end

-- The hidden work folder, when there is no `scratch:`, goes once the run
-- has finished.
function remove_work_base()
  if WORK_BASE ~= "scratch:" then remove_tree(WORK_BASE) end
end

if SELF_TEST then
  self_test()
  remove_work_base()
else
  local report = fresh_report()
  for dir in dirs_of(DIRS_ARG) do
    local r = rewrite_in_work(dir)
    if WRITE then
      write_back(dir, r.work, r.paths)
      report_wide_lines(report, dir, dir, r.paths)
    else
      report_wide_lines(report, dir, r.work, r.paths)
    end
    remove_tree(r.work)
  end
  remove_work_base()
  print_findings((WRITE and "" or "report, nothing written: ") .. report_summary(report), report.long)
  fail_if_refused("wrap_long_lines", report.refused)
end

rewrite_method_calls

Old-style calls such as List.map(xs, f) rewritten as method calls where Roc's own type checker proves the first argument the module's own type or the compiler, trial by trial, accepts the rewrite with roc test unchanged, each call that stays given its reason and each file a failed trial touched put back byte for byte.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.exists!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.list!, Shale.mkdir!, Shale.print!, Shale.re_find!, Shale.read!, Shale.real!, Shale.remove_tree!, Shale.roc_tree!, Shale.run!, Shale.write!.
Roc: 2,840 lines in 15 files. Shale original: 1,195 lines, plus 888 lines in the 7 libraries it loads, which other recipes share.

Roc

It also imports Imports, RocTypes, Text, Tree from the shared Roc library.

cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls/rewrite_method_calls.roc, 151 lines

## rewrite_method_calls, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md):
## old-style Roc calls rewritten as method calls, `List.map(xs, f)` as
## `xs.map(f)`, wherever the compiler agrees it is the same call. Its
## launcher, cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale, is how it is run, and
## its header says which calls turn, how the types and the compiler judge
## them, and the arguments. check_goldens.shale, beside this, holds its
## output and the files it rewrites on the plants to its goldens.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale glob=app/*.roc root=app/main.roc
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale glob=app/*.roc root=app/main.roc apply=1
##   shale cookbook:roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale self_test=1
##
## This root reads the arguments, globs the files and prints the verdict.
## Run is the rewrite: the trees (Source), the candidates (Candidates, with
## Literals), the types (Types, judging by Judging and Peers), the trial and
## the confirm (Trial, by Compiler, writing by Rewritten), all on a sheet
## (Tally); Sweep is what the rewrites leave for a sweep; SelfTest runs the
## plants of Plants. Imports, Text and RocTypes are the cookbook's Roc
## library, cookbook/roc/lib/.
## budget: steps=900000000 output_bytes=4000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 kept_bytes=256000000 changes=100000 change_bytes=2000000000 programs=1100 roc_cpu_ms=3600000
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import Compiler
import Run
import SelfTest
import Sweep
import lib.Text

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	self_test = Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1"
	apply = self_test or Shale.arg!("apply", "") == "1"
	use_types = either!("types", Shale.arg!("types", "1"))
	count_only = !(either!("trials", Shale.arg!("trials", "1")))
	if count_only and apply and !(self_test) {
		Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: trials=0 writes nothing, so not with apply=1")
	}
	if count_only and !(use_types) {
		Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: trials=0 counts by the types, so not with types=0")
	}
	peers = Shale.arg!("peers", "")
	if peers != "" and peers != "undo" {
		Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: peers=${peers}: peers takes only `undo`")
	}
	undo = peers == "undo"
	if undo and (count_only or !(use_types)) {
		Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: peers=undo judges peers by the types and turns them in trials, so not with trials=0 or types=0 (trials=0 counts them as peer_receiver)")
	}
	plant = Shale.arg!("plant", "")
	if plant != "" and !(self_test) {
		Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: plant= is for the self-test's child runs, and needs self_test=1")
	} else if self_test and plant != "" {
		SelfTest.plant!(plant, Compiler.roc_bin!(Bool.True))
	} else if self_test {
		SelfTest.run!({})
	} else {
		rewrite!({ apply, use_types, count_only, undo })
	}
}

## Whether the argument `name`, given as `value`, is 1 (its default) rather
## than 0; any other value stops the run.
either! : Str, Str => Bool
either! = |name, value| {
	if value != "0" and value != "1" {
		Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: ${name}=${value}: ${name} must be 1 (the default) or 0")
	}
	value == "1"
}

## The rewrite of the glob's files, its summary, its findings and the
## summary again (cookbook/findings.shale), then the files no root reaches.
rewrite! : { apply : Bool, use_types : Bool, count_only : Bool, undo : Bool } => {}
rewrite! = |mode| {
	root = Shale.arg!("root", "")
	from = U64.from_str(Shale.arg!("from", "1")) ?? 1
	types_from = Shale.arg!("types_from", "")
	paths = SelfTest.paths_of_globs!(Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc"))
	roc = Compiler.roc_bin!(Bool.False)
	total = Run.all!({
		paths,
		root,
		from,
		use_types: mode.use_types,
		types_roc: roc,
		judge: { roc, apply: mode.apply },
		count_only: mode.count_only,
		types_from,
		undo: mode.undo,
	})
	made = Sweep.made!(total.tally)
	summary = "${summary_of(mode, total, from, paths.len())}, made_unused_import ${made.unused.to_str()}, made_long_line ${made.long.to_str()}"
	kinds = total.tally.kind_counts
		.sort_with(|(first, _), (second, _)| Text.byte_order(first, second))
		.map(|(kind, count)| "${kind} ${count.to_str()}")
	judged = if mode.use_types {
		["types: the first arguments of the candidates the types judged: ${Str.join_with(kinds, ", ")}"]
	} else {
		[]
	}
	print_findings!(summary, total.lines.concat(made.lines).concat(judged))
	for path in total.unreached {
		Shale.print!("not reached by ${root}: ${path}")
	}
	if !(total.unreached.is_empty()) {
		Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: no root reaches ${total.unreached.len().to_str()} file(s) with a call to try, listed above: their calls were left untried")
	}
}

## The summary line's counts, and where to go on from when the programs ran
## out.
summary_of : { apply : Bool, use_types : Bool, count_only : Bool, undo : Bool }, Run.Total, U64, U64 -> Str
summary_of = |mode, total, from, file_count| {
	count = |n| n.to_str()
	programs = count(total.tally.programs_used)
	counted = if mode.count_only {
		"count: files ${count(total.files)}, candidates ${count(total.candidates)}, proven ${count(total.rewritten)}, unsettled ${count(total.unsettled)}, left ${count(total.left)}, peer_receiver ${count(total.peers)}, programs ${programs} (no trials: the types alone decide)"
	} else {
		undone = if mode.undo {
			"peers=undo, "
		} else {
			""
		}
		dry = if mode.apply {
			""
		} else {
			"dry run: "
		}
		checks = "checks: ${count(total.tally.confirms)} confirming proven calls, ${count(total.tally.rounds)} in trial rounds"
		"${undone}${dry}files ${count(total.files)}, candidates ${count(total.candidates)}, rewritten ${count(total.rewritten)}, left ${count(total.left)}, peer_receiver ${count(total.peers)}, programs ${programs} (${checks})"
	}
	if total.next > 0 {
		"${counted}, in files ${count(from)} to ${count(total.next - 1)} of ${count(file_count)}: a run holds ${count(Run.max_programs)} programs; go on with from=${count(total.next)}"
	} else {
		counted
	}
}

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale):
## the first copy survives a cut output, and a gate reads the last line.
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, finding_lines| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(finding_lines.is_empty()) {
		for line in finding_lines {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls/Compiler.roc, 119 lines

## The tree's own Roc, which judges each rewrite: `roc check` and its errors,
## `roc test`'s summary, and `roc fmt`. The Roc is the one the tree pins
## (its `roc-version`), since method lookup has changed
## between nightlies. Each refusal is worded as the Shale original's.
import pf.Shale
import Candidates
import lib.Text

Compiler := [].{

	## What `roc check` said: whether it passed, each error it reported (a
	## warning counts, since a warning fails the build), and its output.
	Check : { ok : Bool, errors : List(Candidates.CheckError), out : Str }

	## The OS path of the tree's Roc: the pin in `roc-version` where the run
	## starts, or in a self-test the pin pinned.shale names.
	roc_bin! : Bool => Str
	roc_bin! = |self_test| {
		pin = if self_test {
			Compiler.self_test_pin!({})
		} else if Shale.exists!("roc-version") {
			Text.trim(Compiler.read_text!("roc-version"))
		} else {
			Compiler.stop!("rewrite_method_calls: no roc-version where the run starts: run it from the repository's root, whose roc-version pins its Roc")
		}
		roc = "tools:roc-${pin}/roc"
		if Shale.exists!(roc) {
			Shale.real!(roc)
		} else {
			Compiler.stop!("rewrite_method_calls: no ${roc}: install Roc ${pin} into ~/tools/roc-${pin}/ (roc-apps's toolchain release carries it)")
		}
	}

	## The pin every recipe's self-test runs, from cookbook/roc/pinned.shale's
	## `SELF_TEST_PIN`, its one home.
	self_test_pin! : {} => Str
	self_test_pin! = |{}| {
		pinned = Compiler.read_text!("cookbook:roc/pinned.shale")
		match Shale.re_find!(pinned, "\nconst SELF_TEST_PIN = \"([^\"]+)\"") {
			Found(matched) => matched.groups.first() ?? ""
			NoMatch => Compiler.stop!("rewrite_method_calls: cookbook/roc/pinned.shale names no SELF_TEST_PIN")
		}
	}

	## `roc check` on the app `root`.
	check! : Str, Str => Compiler.Check
	check! = |roc, root| {
		ran = roc_run!([roc, "check", Shale.real!(root)], Whole(64000000), 900000)
		var $errors = []
		for said in Text.lines(ran.out) {
			# An error's heading is `── ✗ <title> ───── <path>:<line>:<col>`, and
			# a warning's has `●` in place of `✗`.
			if said.starts_with("── ✗ ") or said.starts_with("── ● ") {
				match Shale.re_find!(said, " ([^ ]+):([0-9]+):([0-9]+)$") {
					Found(at) => {
						heading = Str.from_utf8_lossy(said.to_utf8().drop_first(11))
						title = Text.trim(Text.before_first(heading, " ─"))
						place = at.groups.get(0) ?? ""
						line = U64.from_str(at.groups.get(1) ?? "") ?? 0
						$errors = $errors.append({ title, file: Text.basename(place), line })
					}
					NoMatch => {}
				}
			}
		}
		{ ok: ran.code == 0, errors: $errors, out: ran.out }
	}

	## The last line of `roc test` on `root`, without its time, and the exit
	## code: what a rewrite may not change.
	test_summary! : Str, Str => Str
	test_summary! = |roc, root| {
		ran = roc_run!([roc, "test", Shale.real!(root)], Whole(64000000), 900000)
		last = Text.lines(Text.trim(ran.out)).last() ?? ""
		summary = match Shale.re_find!(last, "^(.*) in [0-9.]+ ms\\.") {
			Found(matched) => matched.groups.first() ?? ""
			NoMatch => last
		}
		"${summary} (exit ${ran.code.to_str()})"
	}

	## Whether `roc fmt` finds the file as it would lay it out.
	is_fmt_clean! : Str, Str => Bool
	is_fmt_clean! = |roc, path| roc_run!([roc, "fmt", "--check", Shale.real!(path)], Tail(20), 120000).code == 0

	## The file laid out by `roc fmt`.
	fmt! : Str, Str => {}
	fmt! = |roc, path| {
		_ran = roc_run!([roc, "fmt", Shale.real!(path)], Tail(20), 120000)
		{}
	}

	## The first non-blank line of `out`, for a failure that names no error
	## (a crash).
	first_line_said : Str -> Str
	first_line_said = |out|
		match Text.lines(out).find_first(|said| Text.trim(said) != "") {
			Ok(said) => Text.trim(said)
			Err(_) => "nothing said"
		}

	## A file's text; a missing one stops the run.
	read_text! : Str => Str
	read_text! = |path|
		match Shale.read!(path) {
			Found(text) => text
			Missing => Compiler.stop!("rewrite_method_calls: no ${path}")
		}

	## The run stopped, saying why; the text is never used.
	stop! : Str => Str
	stop! = |why| {
		Shale.fail!(why)
		""
	}
}

roc_run! : List(Str), [Head(U64), Tail(U64), Whole(U64)], U64 => { code : I64, out : Str }
roc_run! = |argv, keep, timeout_ms| Shale.run!({ argv, keep, timeout_ms, want: "" })

cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls/Run.roc, 420 lines

## The rewrite of a list of files, each judged on its root: their trees read,
## their candidates found, the types read of each root and judging them, then
## the confirm and the trials in the files' order, as far as the run's
## programs allow (rewrite_method_calls.shale's `run_all`).
import pf.Shale
import Candidates
import Compiler
import Judging
import Peers
import Source
import Tally
import Trial
import Types
import lib.RocTypes
import lib.Text

Run := [].{

	## What to rewrite: the files, the roots (`a.roc,b.roc`), the file to
	## start at (counted from 1), whether the types are read, the Roc
	## roc-types' pin must match, the Roc that judges, and the modes:
	## `count_only` (`trials=0`), `types_from` and `undo` (`peers=undo`).
	Asked : {
		paths : List(Str),
		root : Str,
		from : U64,
		use_types : Bool,
		types_roc : Str,
		judge : Trial.Judge,
		count_only : Bool,
		types_from : Str,
		undo : Bool,
	}

	## What the run did: its counts, a line for each call that stays (and
	## each peer method call, and under `trials=0` each call the types left
	## unsettled), the file to go on from when the programs ran out (else 0),
	## its sheet, and the files with a call to try that no root reaches.
	Total : {
		files : U64,
		candidates : U64,
		rewritten : U64,
		left : U64,
		unsettled : U64,
		peers : U64,
		lines : List(Str),
		next : U64,
		tally : Tally.Sheet,
		unreached : List(Str),
	}

	## The programs a run may start, Shale's own budget unset.
	max_programs : U64
	max_programs = 1000

	## Rewrites the files of `asked.paths` from the `asked.from`th on.
	all! : Run.Asked => Run.Total
	all! = |asked| {
		if asked.use_types and asked.root == "" {
			Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: the types need root=, an app importing every file of the glob: roc-types reads an app, and a type module only through one. Give root=, or types=0 to run without them, every candidate tried")
		}
		if !(asked.use_types) and asked.root.contains(",") {
			Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: root=${asked.root}: several roots need the types, which say which root reaches a file; give one root, or run with the types")
		}
		roots = if asked.root == "" {
			[]
		} else {
			match RocTypes.root_apps("rewrite_method_calls", asked.root) {
				Ok(apps) => apps
				Err(why) => {
					Shale.fail!(why)
					[]
				}
			}
		}
		if asked.types_from != "" and roots.len() != 1 {
			Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: types_from= holds one root's types, and root= names ${roots.len().to_str()}")
		}
		files = parsed!(asked.paths)
		aliases = if asked.use_types {
			Peers.declared_aliases(files.values())
		} else {
			Dict.empty()
		}
		symmetric = match Peers.symmetric_table(Compiler.read_text!(symmetric_functions)) {
			Ok(names) => names
			Err(why) => {
				Shale.fail!(why)
				Set.empty()
			}
		}
		var $judged = []
		for path in asked.paths.drop_first(asked.from - 1) {
			file = match files.get(path) {
				Ok(found) => found
				Err(_) => {
					Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: roc-ast gave no tree for ${path}")
					Source.of(path, "", [])
				}
			}
			cands = Candidates.of_file(file, module_of_path(path))
			method_calls = if asked.use_types {
				Peers.method_calls(file, symmetric)
			} else {
				[]
			}
			open = cands.any(|cand| cand.why_left == "") or !(method_calls.is_empty())
			$judged = $judged.append({ path, file, real: Shale.real!(path), root: roots.first() ?? path, cands, counts: [], open, unreached: Bool.False, method_calls, peers: [] })
		}
		# The types judge only open candidates, so with none, roc-types never runs.
		read_types = asked.use_types and $judged.any(|one| one.open)
		typing = { by_region: Dict.empty(), aliases, symmetric }
		typed = if read_types {
			with_types!(asked, roots, typing, $judged)
		} else {
			{ tally: Tally.ran(Tally.empty), judged: $judged }
		}
		unreached = typed.judged.keep_if(|one| one.unreached).map(|one| one.path)
		in_mode = typed.judged.map(|one| as_undo(asked.undo, one))
		ready = in_mode.map(with_open_count)
		total = {
			files: 0,
			candidates: 0,
			rewritten: 0,
			left: 0,
			unsettled: 0,
			peers: 0,
			lines: [],
			next: 0,
			tally: typed.tally,
			unreached,
		}
		if asked.count_only {
			counted_by_types(total, ready)
		} else {
			tried!(asked, total, ready)
		}
	}
}

## The symmetric functions' list.
symmetric_functions : Str
symmetric_functions = "cookbook:roc/symmetric_functions.txt"

## A file as the run judges it: its tree, real path and root, its
## candidates, the kinds of type the types found, whether the types must
## judge it (`open`: a module call to try, or with the types a symmetric
## method call), whether no root reaches it, its symmetric method calls and
## its peer method calls; then how many calls are open and whether all are
## proven.
Judged : {
	path : Str,
	file : Source.File,
	real : Str,
	root : Str,
	cands : List(Candidates.Candidate),
	counts : Judging.KindCounts,
	open : Bool,
	unreached : Bool,
	method_calls : List(Peers.MethodCall),
	peers : List(Candidates.Candidate),
}

Ready : {
	path : Str,
	file : Source.File,
	root : Str,
	cands : List(Candidates.Candidate),
	counts : Judging.KindCounts,
	unreached : Bool,
	peers : List(Candidates.Candidate),
	open_count : U64,
	all_proven : Bool,
}

## The module a .roc file holds, its name without `.roc`.
module_of_path : Str -> Str
module_of_path = |path| Text.basename(path).drop_suffix(".roc")

## Every file's tree from Roc's parser and its text, by path: one program.
parsed! : List(Str) => Dict(Str, Source.File)
parsed! = |paths| {
	var $files = Dict.empty()
	if !(paths.is_empty()) {
		for tree in Shale.roc_tree!(paths) {
			if tree.err != "" {
				Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: roc-ast: ${tree.path}: ${tree.err}")
			}
			$files = $files.insert(tree.path, Source.of(tree.path, Compiler.read_text!(tree.path), tree.nodes))
		}
	}
	$files
}

## The types read of each root, one at a time, each file's root the first
## whose app reaches it, its open candidates judged by that root's types on
## the way. A file with a call to try that no root reaches is `unreached`,
## and the run goes on without it.
with_types! : Run.Asked, List(Str), Judging.Typing, List(Judged) => { tally : Tally.Sheet, judged : List(Judged) }
with_types! = |asked, roots, typing, judged| {
	only = if asked.types_from == "" {
		Set.empty()
	} else {
		var $reals = Set.empty()
		for path in asked.paths {
			$reals = $reals.insert(Shale.real!(path))
		}
		$reals
	}
	var $tally = Tally.ran(Tally.empty)
	var $judged = judged
	var $found = Set.empty()
	for root in roots {
		if asked.types_from == "" {
			$tally = Tally.ran($tally)
		}
		typed = Types.of_root!({ root, roc: asked.types_roc, types_from: asked.types_from, only })
		if !($tally.typed_roots.contains(root)) {
			$tally = { ..$tally, typed_roots: $tally.typed_roots.append(root) }
		}
		types_here = { ..typing, by_region: typed.by_region }
		var $judged_here = []
		for one in $judged {
			if one.open and !($found.contains(one.path)) and typed.modules.contains(one.real) {
				$found = $found.insert(one.path)
				by_types = Judging.by_types(one.counts, one.file, one.cands, one.real, types_here)
				peers = one.peers.concat(Judging.method_peers(one.file, one.method_calls, one.real, types_here))
				$judged_here = $judged_here.append({ ..one, root, counts: by_types.counts, cands: by_types.cands, peers })
			} else {
				$judged_here = $judged_here.append(one)
			}
		}
		$judged = $judged_here
	}
	var $marked = []
	for one in $judged {
		$marked = $marked.append({ ..one, unreached: one.open and !($found.contains(one.path)) })
	}
	{ tally: $tally, judged: $marked }
}

## Under `peers=undo`, a file's candidates are its peer method calls alone.
as_undo : Bool, Judged -> Judged
as_undo = |undo, one|
	if undo {
		{ ..one, cands: one.peers, peers: [], counts: [] }
	} else {
		one
	}

with_open_count : Judged -> Ready
with_open_count = |one| {
	open_cands = one.cands.keep_if(|cand| cand.why_left == "")
	all_proven = !(open_cands.is_empty()) and !(one.unreached) and open_cands.all(|cand| cand.proven)
	{
		path: one.path,
		file: one.file,
		root: one.root,
		cands: one.cands,
		counts: one.counts,
		unreached: one.unreached,
		peers: one.peers,
		open_count: open_cands.len(),
		all_proven,
	}
}

## The file's peer method calls added to the findings, a `path:line:
## peer_receiver: why` each, and to their count.
with_peer_findings : Run.Total, Ready -> Run.Total
with_peer_findings = |total, one| {
	said = one.peers.map(
		|cand| {
			why = "`.${cand.fn}` is symmetric and its receiver and first argument are both ${cand.module_name}s, so neither is the subject"
			"${one.path}:${cand.line.to_str()}: peer_receiver: ${why}: ${cand.module_name}.${cand.fn}(...)"
		},
	)
	{ ..total, peers: total.peers + one.peers.len(), lines: total.lines.concat(said) }
}

## A file's kinds of type added to the sheet's, once the file is begun.
with_counts : Run.Total, Ready -> Run.Total
with_counts = |total, one| {
	counts = one.counts.fold(total.tally.kind_counts, |all, (kind, count)| Judging.counted(all, kind, count))
	{ ..total, tally: { ..total.tally, kind_counts: counts } }
}

## A call that stays, as its finding line.
left_line : Str, Candidates.Candidate -> Str
left_line = |path, cand| "${path}:${cand.line.to_str()}: ${cand.module_name}.${cand.fn}: ${cand.why_left}"

## `trials=0`'s answer: a proven call counts as rewritten, an open one the
## types didn't settle as unsettled, with a line naming the kind of type
## they gave, and a call that stays as left, with its reason. Nothing is
## written or compiled.
counted_by_types : Run.Total, List(Ready) -> Run.Total
counted_by_types = |total, ready| {
	var $total = total
	for one in ready {
		cands = if one.unreached {
			[]
		} else {
			one.cands
		}
		proven = cands.keep_if(|cand| cand.why_left == "" and cand.proven)
		if !(proven.is_empty()) {
			$total = { ..$total, tally: Tally.noted($total.tally, one.file, proven) }
		}
		if !(one.unreached) {
			$total = { ..$total, files: $total.files + 1 }
		}
		$total = with_counts($total, one)
		$total = { ..$total, candidates: $total.candidates + cands.len() }
		$total = with_peer_findings($total, one)
		for cand in cands {
			if cand.why_left != "" {
				$total = { ..$total, left: $total.left + 1, lines: $total.lines.append(left_line(one.path, cand)) }
			} else if cand.proven {
				$total = { ..$total, rewritten: $total.rewritten + 1 }
			} else {
				unsettled = "${one.path}:${cand.line.to_str()}: ${cand.module_name}.${cand.fn}: unsettled: the types gave ${cand.kind}, and only a trial would tell"
				$total = { ..$total, unsettled: $total.unsettled + 1, lines: $total.lines.append(unsettled) }
			}
		}
	}
	$total
}

## The `roc test` summary of `root` before any rewrite, which every trial on
## that root must match: taken once a root, and `roc check` must pass first.
baseline! : Trial.Judge, Tally.Sheet, Dict(Str, Str), Str => { tally : Tally.Sheet, baselines : Dict(Str, Str), summary : Str }
baseline! = |judge, tally, baselines, root|
	match baselines.get(root) {
		Ok(summary) => { tally, baselines, summary }
		Err(_) => {
			if !(Compiler.check!(judge.roc, root).ok) {
				Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: `roc check ${root}` fails before any rewrite: fix it first")
			}
			summary = Compiler.test_summary!(judge.roc, root)
			{ tally: Tally.ran(Tally.ran(tally)), baselines: baselines.insert(root, summary), summary }
		}
	}

## The confirm and the trials, file by file. A file is begun only while the
## programs it may take are left: `Trial.max_rounds` checks, a test and,
## under `apply`, two `roc fmt`s, and the first file on a root also the
## baseline's check and test.
tried! : Run.Asked, Run.Total, List(Ready) => Run.Total
tried! = |asked, total, ready| {
	judge = asked.judge
	per_file = Trial.max_rounds + 5
	var $total = total
	var $baselines = Dict.empty()
	var $place = 0
	for one in ready {
		$place = $place + 1
		cands = if one.unreached {
			[]
		} else {
			one.cands
		}
		if !(one.unreached) and one.all_proven and !($total.tally.confirmed.contains(one.path)) {
			# The programs taken before this file's: the baseline's two, if its
			# root has none yet, the confirm's checks and test, and this file's
			# own trial, should the confirm set it aside. Under `apply` each file
			# in the confirm also takes two `roc fmt`s, so only as many join as
			# fit.
			baseline_programs = if $baselines.contains(one.root) {
				0
			} else {
				2
			}
			taken = $total.tally.programs_used + baseline_programs + Trial.max_rounds + 1 + per_file
			var $files = []
			for other in ready.drop_first($place - 1) {
				fits = !(judge.apply) or 2 * ($files.len() + 1) + taken <= Run.max_programs
				if other.all_proven and other.root == one.root and !($total.tally.confirmed.contains(other.path)) and fits {
					$files = $files.append({ path: other.path, file: other.file, cands: other.cands })
				}
			}
			if taken > Run.max_programs or $files.is_empty() {
				return { ..$total, next: asked.from + $place - 1 }
			}
			based = baseline!(judge, $total.tally, $baselines, one.root)
			$baselines = based.baselines
			$total = { ..$total, tally: Trial.confirm!(judge, based.tally, one.root, $files, based.summary) }
		}
		kept_by_confirm = $total.tally.confirmed.get(one.path) ?? 0
		if !(one.unreached) and one.open_count > 0 and kept_by_confirm == 0 and $total.tally.programs_used + per_file > Run.max_programs {
			return { ..$total, next: asked.from + $place - 1 }
		}
		if !(one.unreached) {
			$total = { ..$total, files: $total.files + 1 }
		}
		$total = with_counts($total, one)
		$total = with_peer_findings($total, one)
		if !(cands.is_empty()) {
			var $cands = Candidates.without_lines(cands)
			$kept : U64
			var $kept = kept_by_confirm
			if $kept == 0 and one.open_count > 0 {
				based = baseline!(judge, $total.tally, $baselines, one.root)
				$baselines = based.baselines
				done = Trial.try_file!(judge, based.tally, one.file, $cands, one.root, based.summary)
				$total = { ..$total, tally: done.tally }
				$cands = done.cands
				$kept = done.turned
			}
			left = $cands.keep_if(|cand| cand.why_left != "")
			$total = {
				..$total,
				candidates: $total.candidates + $cands.len(),
				rewritten: $total.rewritten + $kept,
				left: $total.left + left.len(),
				lines: $total.lines.concat(left.map(|cand| left_line(one.path, cand))),
			}
		}
	}
	$total
}

cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls/SelfTest.roc, 296 lines

## The recipe's self-test: each plant in
## cookbook/roc/plants/rewrite_method_calls/ judged in a child run of its own,
## through the launcher (`plant=<Name>`), so each plant gets a run's
## programs of its own. The child copies the plants to a fresh folder under
## `scratch:`, runs there with `apply=1` and checks what came out against
## the plant's expectation (Plants).
import pf.Shale
import Compiler
import Plants
import Run
import Sweep
import Types
import lib.Text

SelfTest := [].{

	## Every plant in a child run of its own; a failed plant is named, and
	## the rest still run.
	run! : {} => {}
	run! = |{}| {
		if !(Shale.exists!(Types.default_checker)) {
			Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: no ${Types.default_checker}, which the plants marked `types` are judged by: `shale install.shale` in a checkout of https://github.com/showell/roc-types installs it")
		}
		var $failed = []
		globbed = SelfTest.paths_of_globs!("${plants}/Proven.roc, ${plants}/NoC*.roc,${plants}/Proven.roc")
		held = globbed.len() == 2 and Text.basename(globbed.get(0) ?? "") == "Proven.roc" and Text.basename(globbed.get(1) ?? "") == "NoCalls.roc"
		Shale.print!("${verdict(held)}glob=: two globs and a repeat give Proven.roc, then NoCalls.roc, each once (${Str.join_with(globbed, ", ")})")
		if !(held) {
			$failed = $failed.append("glob=")
		}
		for name in listed!(plants) {
			plant = name.drop_suffix(".roc")
			judged = Plants.table.any(|want| want.name == plant) or Plants.root_plants.contains(plant)
			if name.ends_with(".roc") and !(judged) {
				Shale.print!("FAIL  ${name}: a plant the table does not judge")
				$failed = $failed.append(name)
			}
		}
		for want in Plants.table.sort_with(|first, second| Text.byte_order(first.name, second.name)) {
			ran = Shale.run!({
				argv: ["shale", "--root", ".", launcher, "self_test=1", "plant=${want.name}"],
				keep: Tail(200),
				timeout_ms: 3600000,
				want: "",
			})
			if want.stop != "" {
				stopped = ran.code > 0 and ran.out.contains(want.stop)
				shown = if stopped {
					""
				} else {
					": ${Text.trim(ran.out)}"
				}
				Shale.print!("${verdict(stopped)}${want.name}: stops, saying ${want.stop}${shown}")
				if !(stopped) {
					$failed = $failed.append(want.name)
				}
			} else {
				for said in Text.lines(ran.out) {
					if !(said.starts_with("── budgets")) {
						Shale.print!(said)
					}
				}
				if ran.code != 0 {
					$failed = $failed.append(want.name)
				}
			}
		}
		if !($failed.is_empty()) {
			Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: ${$failed.len().to_str()} plant(s) failed: ${Str.join_with($failed, ", ")}")
		}
		Shale.print!("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: every plant as it says")
	}

	## The child run `plant=<name>`: the plants copied to a fresh scratch
	## folder, the one plant run there with `apply=1`, and the result checked
	## against its expectation.
	plant! : Str, Str => {}
	plant! = |name, self_test_roc| {
		want = match Plants.table.find_first(|plant_want| plant_want.name == name) {
			Ok(found) => found
			Err(_) => {
				Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: no plant ${name} in the table")
				Plants.table.first() ?? crash "SelfTest: the table is empty"
			}
		}
		scratch = Sweep.fresh_dir!("methods")
		for listed_name in listed!(plants) {
			Shale.write!("${scratch}/${listed_name}", Compiler.read_text!("${plants}/${listed_name}"))
		}
		file = if want.file == "" {
			name
		} else {
			want.file
		}
		path = "${scratch}/${file}.roc"
		paths = if want.beside == "" {
			[path]
		} else {
			[path, "${scratch}/${want.beside}.roc"]
		}
		# A plant with `tree_pin` runs as though the tree pinned that Roc.
		types_roc = if want.tree_pin == "" {
			self_test_roc
		} else {
			Shale.real!("tools:roc-${want.tree_pin}/roc")
		}
		roots = want.root.split_on(",").keep_if(|root| root != "").map(|root| "${scratch}/${root}.roc")
		# A plant with `types_from` reads the types from a file, as a gate
		# keeps them: roc-types' output on the root, written here first.
		types_from = if want.types_from {
			written = "${scratch}/root.types"
			ran = Shale.run!({
				argv: [Shale.real!(Types.checker_for!(types_roc)), Shale.real!(roots.first() ?? "")],
				keep: Whole(64000000),
				timeout_ms: 300000,
				want: "",
			})
			if ran.code != 0 {
				Shale.print!(ran.out)
				Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: roc-types exited ${ran.code.to_str()}")
			}
			Shale.write!(written, ran.out)
			written
		} else {
			""
		}
		got = Run.all!({
			paths,
			root: Str.join_with(roots, ","),
			from: 1,
			use_types: want.types,
			types_roc,
			judge: { roc: self_test_roc, apply: Bool.True },
			count_only: want.count,
			types_from,
			undo: want.undo,
		})
		if want.stop != "" {
			Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: ${name} ran to its end, and was to stop: ${want.stop}")
		}
		checks = checks_of!({ want, got, path, plant_file: "${plants}/${file}.roc", roots, types_from, paths })
		failures = checks.count_if(|(passed, _)| !(passed))
		for (passed, what) in checks {
			Shale.print!("${verdict(passed)}${what}")
		}
		if failures > 0 {
			Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: ${name}: ${failures.to_str()} failed")
		}
		Shale.remove_tree!(scratch)
	}

	## The files of `globs`, several separated by commas, in the order the
	## globs give them, each once.
	paths_of_globs! : Str => List(Str)
	paths_of_globs! = |globs| {
		var $paths = []
		var $seen = Set.empty()
		for pattern in globs.split_on(",") {
			for path in Shale.glob!(Text.trim(pattern)) {
				if !($seen.contains(path)) {
					$seen = $seen.insert(path)
					$paths = $paths.append(path)
				}
			}
		}
		$paths
	}
}

## The launcher each plant's child run goes through.
launcher : Str
launcher = "cookbook:roc/rewrite_method_calls.shale"

plants : Str
plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/rewrite_method_calls"

verdict : Bool -> Str
verdict = |passed|
	if passed {
		"ok    "
	} else {
		"FAIL  "
	}

## The names in a folder, as Shale's `ls` gives them.
listed! : Str => List(Str)
listed! = |folder|
	match Shale.list!(folder) {
		Found(names) => names
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: self-test: no ${folder}")
			[]
		}
	}

## Each check of a plant's child run, in the Shale original's order: whether
## it passed and what it says.
checks_of! : { want : Plants.Expect, got : Run.Total, path : Str, plant_file : Str, roots : List(Str), types_from : Str, paths : List(Str) } => List((Bool, Str))
checks_of! = |asked| {
	want = asked.want
	got = asked.got
	name = want.name
	var $checks = []
	if want.count {
		$checks = $checks.append((got.rewritten == want.proven, "${name}: ${got.rewritten.to_str()} proven, want ${want.proven.to_str()}"))
		$checks = $checks.append((got.unsettled == want.unsettled, "${name}: ${got.unsettled.to_str()} unsettled, want ${want.unsettled.to_str()}"))
		$checks = $checks.append((Compiler.read_text!(asked.path) == Compiler.read_text!(asked.plant_file), "${name}: counted, and left as it was"))
	}
	match want.peers {
		Peers(peers) => {
			$checks = $checks.append((got.peers == peers, "${name}: ${got.peers.to_str()} peer_receiver, want ${peers.to_str()}"))
		}
		AnyPeers => {}
	}
	made = Sweep.made!(got.tally)
	listed = if made.lines.is_empty() {
		""
	} else {
		" (${Str.join_with(made.lines, "; ")})"
	}
	made_held = made.unused == want.made_unused and made.long == want.made_long
	made_counts = "${made.unused.to_str()} made_unused_import and ${made.long.to_str()} made_long_line"
	$checks = $checks.append((made_held, "${name}: ${made_counts}, want ${want.made_unused.to_str()} and ${want.made_long.to_str()}${listed}"))
	if want.made_says != "" {
		$checks = $checks.append((Str.join_with(made.lines, "\n").contains(want.made_says), "${name}: reports ${want.made_says}"))
	}
	if asked.types_from != "" {
		used = got.tally.programs_used
		$checks = $checks.append((used == 1, "${name}: the types read from a file, so roc-ast the one program (${used.to_str()})"))
	}
	unreached = got.unreached
	$checks = $checks.append((unreached.len() == want.unreached, "${name}: ${unreached.len().to_str()} not reached by a root, want ${want.unreached.to_str()} (${Str.join_with(unreached, ", ")})"))
	left = got.lines
	left_listed = if left.is_empty() {
		""
	} else {
		" (${Str.join_with(left, "; ")})"
	}
	$checks = $checks.append((left.len() == want.left, "${name}: ${left.len().to_str()} left, want ${want.left.to_str()}${left_listed}"))
	if want.why != "" {
		$checks = $checks.append((!(left.is_empty()) and Str.join_with(left, "\n").contains(want.why), "${name}: left because ${want.why}"))
	}
	file = Text.basename(asked.plant_file).drop_suffix(".roc")
	want_path = "${plants}/${file}.want"
	has_want = Shale.exists!(want_path)
	if has_want and !(want.count) {
		$checks = $checks.append((Compiler.read_text!(asked.path) == Compiler.read_text!(want_path), "${name}: comes out as ${file}.want"))
	}
	# In Typed, the types turn one call and leave the other, so the trial
	# decides neither.
	kinds = got.tally.kind_counts
	if name == "Typed" {
		count_of = |kind| kinds.find_first(|(named, _)| named == kind).map_ok(|(_, count)| count) ?? 0
		typed_held = kinds.len() == 2 and count_of("another type") == 1 and count_of("the module's type") == 1
		$checks = $checks.append((typed_held, "${name}: by type, ${json_of(kinds)}"))
	}
	confirms = got.tally.confirms
	$checks = $checks.append((confirms == want.confirms, "${name}: ${confirms.to_str()} confirm(s), want ${want.confirms.to_str()}"))
	match want.rounds {
		Rounds(rounds) => {
			got_rounds = got.tally.rounds
			$checks = $checks.append((got_rounds == rounds, "${name}: ${got_rounds.to_str()} round(s), want ${rounds.to_str()}"))
		}
		AnyRounds => {}
	}
	runs = got.tally.typed_roots.len()
	if !(want.types) {
		$checks = $checks.append((kinds.is_empty() and runs == 0, "${name}: under types=0, no roc-types run"))
	}
	# With the types, roc-types runs once per root when a candidate is open,
	# and not at all on a file with none (`no_types_run`).
	if want.types {
		want_runs = if want.no_types_run {
			0
		} else {
			asked.roots.len()
		}
		$checks = $checks.append((runs == want_runs, "${name}: ${runs.to_str()} roc-types run(s), want ${want_runs.to_str()}"))
	}
	if want.left > 0 and !(has_want) {
		$checks = $checks.append((Compiler.read_text!(asked.path) == Compiler.read_text!(asked.plant_file), "${name}: put back as it was"))
	}
	if want.beside != "" {
		beside = asked.paths.get(1) ?? ""
		$checks = $checks.append((Compiler.read_text!(beside) == Compiler.read_text!("${plants}/${want.beside}.roc"), "${name}: ${want.beside} left as it was"))
	}
	$checks
}

## The kinds' counts as Shale's `json_write` writes a map: `{"kind":1,...}`,
## in the order each was first counted.
json_of : List((Str, U64)) -> Str
json_of = |kinds| {
	members = kinds.map(|(kind, count)| "\"${kind}\":${count.to_str()}")
	"{${Str.join_with(members, ",")}}"
}

cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls/Sweep.roc, 111 lines

## What the rewrites left for a sweep to fix in the same pass, which the
## recipe reports and does not fix: each import that a file used before its
## rewrite and no longer uses after it, by the cookbook's one home of that
## rule (lib's Imports, find_unused_imports'), and each line wider than 100
## columns where a turned call joined its lines (a turn alone only shortens a
## line). A line is named by its number in the rewritten text, before any
## `roc fmt`.
import pf.Shale
import Tally
import lib.Imports
import lib.Text

Sweep := [].{

	## The findings, a `path:line: made_unused_import: why` or
	## `made_long_line` each, and the count of each kind.
	Made : { lines : List(Str), unused : U64, long : U64 }

	## What the rewrites on the sheet made. Roc's parser reads files, so both
	## texts of each are written to a scratch folder, removed after.
	made! : Tally.Sheet => Sweep.Made
	made! = |tally| {
		rewrites = tally.rewrites.to_list().sort_with(|(first, _), (second, _)| Text.byte_order(first, second))
		if rewrites.is_empty() {
			return { lines: [], unused: 0, long: 0 }
		}
		dir = Sweep.fresh_dir!("made_by_rewrites")
		var $files = []
		$number : U64
		var $number = 0
		for (_, rewrite) in rewrites {
			$number = $number + 1
			folder = "${dir}/${$number.to_str()}"
			Shale.mkdir!(folder)
			Shale.write!("${folder}/before.roc", rewrite.before)
			Shale.write!("${folder}/after.roc", rewrite.after)
			$files = $files.concat(["${folder}/before.roc", "${folder}/after.roc"])
		}
		var $trees = Dict.empty()
		for tree in Shale.roc_tree!($files) {
			if tree.err != "" {
				Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: roc-ast refused a rewritten text (${tree.path}): ${tree.err}")
			}
			$trees = $trees.insert(tree.path, tree.nodes)
		}
		var $made = { lines: [], unused: 0, long: 0 }
		$number = 0
		for (path, rewrite) in rewrites {
			$number = $number + 1
			folder = "${dir}/${$number.to_str()}"
			before = Imports.unused_imports($trees.get("${folder}/before.roc") ?? [], rewrite.before.split_on("\n"))
			was_unused = Set.from_list(before.map(|unused| unused.label))
			after_lines = rewrite.after.split_on("\n")
			for unused in Imports.unused_imports($trees.get("${folder}/after.roc") ?? [], after_lines) {
				if !(was_unused.contains(unused.label)) {
					said = "${path}:${unused.line.to_str()}: made_unused_import: ${unused.label} was used only by the calls the rewrite turned: delete the line"
					$made = { ..$made, unused: $made.unused + 1, lines: $made.lines.append(said) }
				}
			}
			var $seen = Set.empty()
			for number in rewrite.joined.sort_with(
				|first, second| if first < second {
					Before
				} else if first > second {
					After
				} else {
					Same
				},
			) {
				text_line = Text.line_at(after_lines, number)
				width = columns_of(text_line)
				if width > long_line and !($seen.contains(number)) {
					$seen = $seen.insert(number)
					shown = Text.trim(Text.bytes_of(text_line, { start: 0, count: 120 }))
					said = "${path}:${number.to_str()}: made_long_line: ${width.to_str()} columns after the rewrite joined a call's lines: stack it (wrap_long_lines.shale): ${shown}"
					$made = { ..$made, long: $made.long + 1, lines: $made.lines.append(said) }
				}
			}
		}
		Shale.remove_tree!(dir)
		$made
	}

	## A folder of the run's own below `scratch:`, `<prefix>.XXXXXX`, so two
	## runs at once never share one (Shale's `fresh_dir`); the caller removes
	## it.
	fresh_dir! : Str => Str
	fresh_dir! = |prefix| {
		made = Shale.run!({
			argv: ["mktemp", "-d", "${Shale.real!("scratch:")}/${prefix}.XXXXXX"],
			keep: Tail(2),
			timeout_ms: 10000,
			want: "",
		})
		if made.code != 0 {
			Shale.fail!("rewrite_method_calls: no scratch folder: ${made.out}")
		}
		"scratch:${Text.basename(Text.trim(made.out))}"
	}
}

## The width past which a line is long, as check_stacking's `width`.
long_line : U64
long_line = 100

## A line's width, a tab counting four columns.
columns_of : Str -> U64
columns_of = |text_line| {
	bytes = text_line.to_utf8()
	bytes.len() + 3 * bytes.count_if(|byte| byte == '\t')
}

cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls/Candidates.roc, 262 lines

## The calls a file offers to turn, `Module.fn(first, ...)`, each with why it
## must stay when it must, and what a trial's `roc check` errors say of them.
import Literals
import Rewritten
import Source

Candidates := [].{

	## A call to turn, by its node: the module and function it calls, its
	## line, why it stays (`""` while it is open to rewriting), whether the
	## types prove it, the kind of type they gave when they settled nothing,
	## and its lines in the last text that turned it (0 when it was not
	## turned). A peer method call turned back is `undo`, its receiver's
	## `type` kept.
	Candidate : {
		node : U64,
		module_name : Str,
		fn : Str,
		line : U64,
		why_left : Str,
		proven : Bool,
		kind : Str,
		from_line : U64,
		to_line : U64,
		undo : Bool,
		type : Str,
	}

	## An error `roc check` reports: its title, the file it names (its base
	## name) and the line.
	CheckError : { title : Str, file : Str, line : U64 }

	## The calls `Module.fn(first, ...)` in the file, except calls of the
	## file's own module (`own_module`), in the tree's order.
	of_file : Source.File, Str -> List(Candidates.Candidate)
	of_file = |file, own_module| {
		var $out = []
		for (node, place) in file.nodes.map_with_index(|node, index| (node, index + 1)) {
			if node.kind == "e-apply" and node.kids.len() >= 2 {
				callee = Source.kid_node(file, node, 1)
				match module_call(callee.raw) {
					Ok(called) if callee.kind == "e-ident" and called.module_name != own_module => {
						why = reason_call_stays(file, place, called.module_name, called.fn)
						line = Source.line_of_offset(file, node.from)
						$out = $out.append(candidate(place, called.module_name, called.fn, line, why))
					}
					_ => {}
				}
			}
		}
		$out
	}

	## A peer method call to turn back into a module call, proven by the
	## receiver's type, which `type` keeps.
	undoing : { place : U64, module_name : Str, fn : Str, line : U64, why_left : Str, type : Str } -> Candidates.Candidate
	undoing = |call| {
		..candidate(call.place, call.module_name, call.fn, call.line, call.why_left),
		proven: Bool.True,
		undo: Bool.True,
		type: call.type,
	}

	## The open candidates as the rewrite turns them, by node.
	turning : List(Candidates.Candidate) -> Dict(U64, Rewritten.Turn)
	turning = |cands| {
		var $turning = Dict.empty()
		for cand in cands {
			if cand.why_left == "" {
				$turning = $turning.insert(cand.node, { node: cand.node, module_name: cand.module_name, fn: cand.fn, undo: cand.undo })
			}
		}
		$turning
	}

	## How many candidates are open.
	open_count : List(Candidates.Candidate) -> U64
	open_count = |cands| cands.count_if(|cand| cand.why_left == "")

	## Every open candidate left, for `why`.
	leave_open : List(Candidates.Candidate), Str -> List(Candidates.Candidate)
	leave_open = |cands, why| cands.map(
		|cand| if cand.why_left == "" {
			{ ..cand, why_left: why }
		} else {
			cand
		},
	)

	## The candidates with the lines a rewrite gave the calls it turned; any
	## other keeps the lines it had.
	with_lines : List(Candidates.Candidate), Rewritten.Written -> List(Candidates.Candidate)
	with_lines = |cands, written|
		cands.map(
			|cand|
				match written.turned_lines.get(cand.node) {
					Ok(lines) => { ..cand, from_line: lines.from_line, to_line: lines.to_line }
					Err(_) => cand
				},
		)

	## The candidates with no lines: none turned.
	without_lines : List(Candidates.Candidate) -> List(Candidates.Candidate)
	without_lines = |cands| cands.map(|cand| { ..cand, from_line: 0 })

	## One error of a trial on the file, laid on each turned call whose lines
	## hold it (one error may fall on two calls), or else on a definition's
	## value: the candidates, each hit one left with the error's title, and
	## whether any call was hit.
	blame : Source.File, Dict(U64, U64), Candidates.CheckError, List(Candidates.Candidate) -> { cands : List(Candidates.Candidate), hit : Bool }
	blame = |file, line_of_node, error, cands| {
		on_lines = |cand| cand.from_line > 0 and error.line >= cand.from_line and error.line <= cand.to_line
		if cands.any(on_lines) {
			why = "roc check: ${error.title}"
			left = cands.map(
				|cand| if on_lines(cand) and cand.why_left == "" {
					{ ..cand, why_left: why }
				} else {
					cand
				},
			)
			{ cands: left, hit: Bool.True }
		} else {
			blame_definition(file, line_of_node, error, cands)
		}
	}
}

candidate : U64, Str, Str, U64, Str -> Candidates.Candidate
candidate = |place, module_name, fn, line, why_left| {
	node: place,
	module_name,
	fn,
	line,
	why_left,
	proven: Bool.False,
	kind: "",
	from_line: 0,
	to_line: 0,
	undo: Bool.False,
	type: "",
}

## A callee `Module.fn` split, when it is one: a capital and letters and
## digits, a `.`, then a small letter, letters, digits and `_`, and an
## optional last `!`.
module_call : Str -> Try({ module_name : Str, fn : Str }, [NoModuleCall])
module_call = |raw| {
	parts = raw.split_first(".") ?? { before: "", after: "" }
	module_name = parts.before.to_utf8()
	fn = parts.after.to_utf8()
	fn_body = if (fn.last() ?? 0) == '!' {
		fn.drop_last(1)
	} else {
		fn
	}
	is_module = match module_name.first() {
		Ok(first) => is_capital(first) and module_name.all(is_alphanumeric)
		Err(_) => Bool.False
	}
	is_fn = match fn_body.first() {
		Ok(first) => first >= 'a' and first <= 'z' and fn_body.all(|byte| is_alphanumeric(byte) or byte == '_')
		Err(_) => Bool.False
	}
	if is_module and is_fn {
		Ok({ module_name: parts.before, fn: parts.after })
	} else {
		Err(NoModuleCall)
	}
}

is_capital : U8 -> Bool
is_capital = |byte| byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z'

is_alphanumeric : U8 -> Bool
is_alphanumeric = |byte| is_capital(byte) or (byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or (byte >= '0' and byte <= '9')

## Why the call `module.fn(...)` at node `place` must stay whatever the
## types say, or `""` when it may be tried.
reason_call_stays : Source.File, U64, Str, Str -> Str
reason_call_stays = |file, place, module_name, fn| {
	node = Source.node_at(file, place)
	parent = if node.parent > 0 {
		Ok(Source.node_at(file, node.parent))
	} else {
		Err(NoParent)
	}
	is_piped = match parent {
		Ok(up) => up.kind == "e-arrow-call" and (up.kids.get(1) ?? 0) == place
		Err(_) => Bool.False
	}
	unspanned = node.kids.drop_first(1).find_first(|arg| !(Source.node_at(file, arg).has_span))
	first_place = Source.kid(node, 2)
	first = Source.node_at(file, first_place)
	if is_piped {
		"the right of a `|>`, whose first argument the pipe gives"
	} else if unspanned.is_ok() {
		kind = Source.node_at(file, unspanned ?? 0).kind
		"an argument with no span in the tree (${kind}), whose text cannot be moved"
	} else if Literals.is_constant_numeric(file, first_place) {
		written = Source.text_of(file, first)
		text = if first.kind == "e-tuple" {
			written
		} else {
			"(${written})"
		}
		"a number literal's type would default as a receiver (`${text}.${fn}()` is no longer a ${module_name})"
	} else if Literals.takes_literal_type(file, first_place) {
		text = Source.text_of(file, first)
		taken = "`${text}` takes its type from a number literal, unannotated"
		"a number literal's type would default as a receiver (${taken}, and `${text}.${fn}()` is no longer a ${module_name})"
	} else {
		""
	}
}

## Whether node `place` is below node `top`.
is_below : Source.File, U64, U64 -> Bool
is_below = |file, place, top| {
	var $at = Source.node_at(file, place).parent
	while $at > 0 {
		if $at == top {
			return Bool.True
		}
		$at = Source.node_at(file, $at).parent
	}
	Bool.False
}

## A `missing method` error on the value of a definition `name = <value>`
## means that value's type never resolved because its only use was a turned
## `name.fn()`: the error is laid on each turned call whose first argument
## is the plain `name` within the definition's statements.
blame_definition : Source.File, Dict(U64, U64), Candidates.CheckError, List(Candidates.Candidate) -> { cands : List(Candidates.Candidate), hit : Bool }
blame_definition = |file, line_of_node, error, cands| {
	if error.title != "missing method" {
		return { cands, hit: Bool.False }
	}
	var $cands = cands
	var $hit = Bool.False
	for definition in file.nodes {
		name = Literals.defined_name(file, definition)
		if name != "" and (line_of_node.get(Source.kid(definition, 2)) ?? 0) == error.line {
			why = "roc check: ${error.title} (on `${name}`'s definition)"
			is_blamed = |cand| {
				first = Source.kid_node(file, Source.node_at(file, cand.node), 2)
				cand.from_line > 0 and first.kind == "e-ident" and first.raw == name and is_below(file, cand.node, definition.parent)
			}
			if $cands.any(is_blamed) {
				$hit = Bool.True
				$cands = $cands.map(
					|cand| if is_blamed(cand) and cand.why_left == "" {
						{ ..cand, why_left: why }
					} else {
						cand
					},
				)
			}
		}
	}
	{ cands: $cands, hit: $hit }
}

cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls/Judging.roc, 158 lines

## The candidates of a file judged by Roc's own types, as roc-types gives
## them by region: a call whose first argument's type is the module's own is
## proven, one of a concrete other type stays, a symmetric call of peers
## stays a module call, and the rest are left to the trial. With
## `peers=undo`, the peer method calls are found here too.
import Candidates
import Peers
import Source

Judging := [].{

	## How many candidates the types judged of each kind, in the order each
	## kind was first counted.
	KindCounts : List((Str, U64))

	## What the types say: each expression's type by `<real path>|<region>`,
	## the aliases the files declare, and the symmetric functions.
	Typing : { by_region : Dict(Str, Str), aliases : Dict(Str, Str), symmetric : Set(Str) }

	## `counts` with one more of `kind`, or `count` more.
	counted : Judging.KindCounts, Str, U64 -> Judging.KindCounts
	counted = |counts, kind, count|
		if counts.any(|(named, _)| named == kind) {
			counts.map(
				|(named, had)| if named == kind {
					(named, had + count)
				} else {
					(named, had)
				},
			)
		} else {
			counts.append((kind, count))
		}

	## Judges each open candidate of the file, whose real path is
	## `real_path`, by its first argument's type, and counts each kind.
	by_types : Judging.KindCounts, Source.File, List(Candidates.Candidate), Str, Judging.Typing -> { counts : Judging.KindCounts, cands : List(Candidates.Candidate) }
	by_types = |counts, file, cands, real_path, typing| {
		var $counts = counts
		var $cands = []
		for cand in cands {
			if cand.why_left == "" {
				judged = judge_one(file, cand, real_path, typing)
				$counts = Judging.counted($counts, judged.kind, 1)
				$cands = $cands.append(judged.cand)
			} else {
				$cands = $cands.append(cand)
			}
		}
		{ counts: $counts, cands: $cands }
	}

	## The peer method calls of the file, `calls`: each whose receiver and
	## first argument are peers, with a module to call through, as a
	## candidate that turns it back (`a.max(b)` to `U64.max(a, b)`), proven,
	## as the receiver's type is where the method was found. A call with an
	## argument that has no span stays, as a module call's does.
	method_peers : Source.File, List(Peers.MethodCall), Str, Judging.Typing -> List(Candidates.Candidate)
	method_peers = |file, calls, real_path, typing| {
		type_at = |place| typing.by_region.get("${real_path}|${Source.node_at(file, place).region}") ?? ""
		calls.join_map(
			|call| {
				verdict = Peers.verdict(type_at(call.receiver), type_at(call.first), typing.aliases)
				if verdict.peers {
					why_left = if call.spanned {
						""
					} else {
						"an argument with no span in the tree, whose text cannot be moved"
					}
					line = Source.line_of_offset(file, Source.node_at(file, call.node).from)
					[Candidates.undoing({ place: call.node, module_name: verdict.module_name, fn: call.fn, line, why_left, type: verdict.type })]
				} else {
					[]
				}
			},
		)
	}
}

## A type's head: a type variable (`a`, `_a`, `a where [...]`), or its name
## (`List` of `List(U8)`, `Access.Viewer` of `Access.Viewer(Topic.At)`), a
## function's (an arrow outside every bracket) `function`, `{...}`'s
## `record`, `[...]`'s `tag union` and `(a, b)`'s `tuple`.
Head : [Variable, Named(Str)]

type_head : Str -> Head
type_head = |type_text| {
	bytes = type_text.to_utf8()
	first = bytes.first() ?? 0
	if Peers.has_top_arrow(bytes) {
		Named("function")
	} else if first == '{' {
		Named("record")
	} else if first == '[' {
		Named("tag union")
	} else if first == '(' {
		Named("tuple")
	} else if first < 'A' or first > 'Z' {
		Variable
	} else {
		length = bytes.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_head_byte(byte))) ?? bytes.len()
		Named(Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.take_first(length)))
	}
}

is_head_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_head_byte = |byte|
	(byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z') or (byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or (byte >= '0' and byte <= '9') or byte == '_' or byte == '.'

## `word` after its indefinite article: "an" before a vowel sound. A U
## usually sounds like "you" (U8, User), so it takes "an" only in `Un...`
## (Unvalidated).
with_article : Str -> Str
with_article = |word| {
	first = word.to_utf8().first() ?? 0
	vowel = first == 'A' or first == 'E' or first == 'I' or first == 'O' or first == 'a' or first == 'e' or first == 'i' or first == 'o'
	if vowel or word.starts_with("Un") or word.starts_with("un") {
		"an ${word}"
	} else {
		"a ${word}"
	}
}

## One open candidate judged: the kind it is counted as, and the candidate
## with what the types say. A first argument whose type has the module's own
## name, bare, proves the call: roc-types writes a type by the name it is
## declared with, so a qualified head never does, even one whose last
## segment names the module (`Type.Game` is Type's, not Game's).
judge_one : Source.File, Candidates.Candidate, Str, Judging.Typing -> { kind : Str, cand : Candidates.Candidate }
judge_one = |file, cand, real_path, typing| {
	call = Source.node_at(file, cand.node)
	type_at = |number| typing.by_region.get("${real_path}|${Source.kid_node(file, call, number).region}")
	peers =
		if call.kids.len() >= 3 and typing.symmetric.contains(cand.fn) {
			Peers.verdict(type_at(2) ?? "", type_at(3) ?? "", typing.aliases)
		} else {
			{ peers: Bool.False, type: "", module_name: "" }
		}
	if peers.peers {
		why = "peers: `${cand.fn}` is symmetric and both arguments are ${peers.module_name}s, so neither is the subject"
		{ kind: "peers", cand: { ..cand, why_left: why } }
	} else {
		match type_at(2) {
			Err(_) => { kind: "no type", cand: { ..cand, kind: "no type" } }
			Ok(type_text) =>
				match type_head(type_text) {
					Variable => { kind: "a type variable", cand: { ..cand, kind: "a type variable" } }
					Named(head) =>
						if head == cand.module_name {
							{ kind: "the module's type", cand: { ..cand, proven: Bool.True } }
						} else {
							why = "the first argument is ${with_article(head)}, not ${with_article(cand.module_name)}"
							{ kind: "another type", cand: { ..cand, why_left: why } }
						}
				}
		}
	}
}

cookbook/roc/rewrite_method_calls/Peers.roc, 267 lines

## Which calls are peer calls (peer_calls.shale). A method call names a
## subject, so a symmetric function, one where no argument is the subject, is
## called through its module: `U64.max(a, b)`, `Str.concat(a, b)`,
## `List.map2(xs, ys, f)`. The symmetric functions are a list of names,
## cookbook/roc/symmetric_functions.txt, and a call of one is a peer call
## when its first two arguments' types have one head, as roc-types writes
## them at the call with each alias read through to what it names (a `Hue :
## U32` is a `U32`). A function off the list (`starts_with`, a unit's `plus`)
## keeps its method call, whatever its arguments.
import Source
import lib.Text

Peers := [].{

	## Whether two arguments are peers, values of one type: `type` is the
	## first's type with its aliases read through, `module` that type's head.
	Verdict : { peers : Bool, type : Str, module_name : Str }

	## A symmetric method call that passes an argument, `x.max(y)`: its node,
	## its receiver's node, its first argument's, the function, and whether
	## every argument has a span, so its text can be moved.
	MethodCall : { node : U64, receiver : U64, first : U64, fn : Str, spanned : Bool }

	## Every alias the files declare (`Hue : U32`, never `:=` or `::`), by the
	## name roc-types gives it, to the text of the type it names. An alias
	## with parameters is left out: reading it through would need its
	## arguments bound. Where two files declare one name, the later file by
	## path wins.
	declared_aliases : List(Source.File) -> Dict(Str, Str)
	declared_aliases = |files| {
		var $out = Dict.empty()
		for file in files.sort_with(|first, second| Text.byte_order(first.path, second.path)) {
			for (node, place) in file.nodes.map_with_index(|node, index| (node, index + 1)) {
				if node.kind == "s-type-decl" and node.kids.len() == 2 {
					header = Source.kid_node(file, node, 1)
					target = Source.kid_node(file, node, 2)
					if is_bare_header(file, header) and header.has_span and target.has_span {
						between = Text.trim(Source.text_between(file, header.to, target.from))
						if between == ":" {
							$out = $out.insert(declared_name(file, place), Source.text_of(file, target))
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		$out
	}

	## Whether two arguments, of the types `first` and `second` as roc-types
	## gives them (`""` where it gives none), are peers: both types, their
	## aliases read through, have one head to call through (`List(U64)` and
	## `List(Str)` are peers to `map2`).
	verdict : Str, Str, Dict(Str, Str) -> Peers.Verdict
	verdict = |first, second, aliases|
		if first == "" or second == "" {
			{ peers: Bool.False, type: "", module_name: "" }
		} else {
			resolved = resolved_type(first, aliases, 0)
			module_name = Peers.module_of(resolved)
			peers = module_name != "" and module_name == Peers.module_of(resolved_type(second, aliases, 0))
			{ peers, type: resolved, module_name }
		}

	## The module a value of the type `type_text` takes its methods from, the
	## type's head (`List` for `List(U8)`, `Shelf.Book`), or `""` for a type
	## with none to call through: a type variable, a record, a tuple, a tag
	## union or a function.
	module_of : Str -> Str
	module_of = |type_text| {
		bytes = type_text.to_utf8()
		if Peers.has_top_arrow(bytes) {
			""
		} else {
			length = type_name_length(bytes, 0)
			Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.take_first(length))
		}
	}

	## Whether an arrow, `->` or `=>`, stands outside every bracket.
	has_top_arrow : List(U8) -> Bool
	has_top_arrow = |bytes| {
		$depth : I64
		var $depth = 0
		var $place = 0
		while $place + 1 < bytes.len() {
			byte = bytes.get($place) ?? 0
			if byte == '(' or byte == '[' or byte == '{' {
				$depth = $depth + 1
			}
			if byte == ')' or byte == ']' or byte == '}' {
				$depth = $depth - 1
			}
			next = bytes.get($place + 1) ?? 0
			if $depth == 0 and next == '>' and (byte == '-' or byte == '=') {
				return Bool.True
			}
			$place = $place + 1
		}
		Bool.False
	}

	## The symmetric functions in `text`, symmetric_functions.txt: a set of
	## names, one a line, `#` lines its comments; or why a line is no name.
	symmetric_table : Str -> Try(Set(Str), Str)
	symmetric_table = |text| {
		var $names = Set.empty()
		for text_line in Text.lines(text) {
			word = Text.trim(text_line)
			if word != "" and !(word.starts_with("#")) {
				if !(is_function_name(word.to_utf8())) {
					return Err("peer_calls: symmetric_functions.txt: `${word}` is not a function's name")
				}
				$names = $names.insert(word)
			}
		}
		Ok($names)
	}

	## The method calls in the file of a function in `symmetric` that pass an
	## argument.
	method_calls : Source.File, Set(Str) -> List(Peers.MethodCall)
	method_calls = |file, symmetric| {
		var $calls = []
		for (node, place) in file.nodes.map_with_index(|node, index| (node, index + 1)) {
			if node.kind == "e-method-call" and node.kids.len() == 2 {
				receiver = Source.kid_node(file, node, 1)
				if receiver.kind == "receiver" and receiver.kids.len() == 1 {
					args = Source.kid_node(file, node, 2)
					fn = if node.method.starts_with(".") {
						Str.from_utf8_lossy(node.method.to_utf8().drop_first(1))
					} else {
						node.method
					}
					if args.kind == "args" and !(args.kids.is_empty()) and symmetric.contains(fn) {
						value = Source.kid(receiver, 1)
						spanned = Source.node_at(file, value).has_span and args.kids.all(|arg| Source.node_at(file, arg).has_span)
						call = { node: place, receiver: value, first: args.kids.first() ?? 0, fn, spanned }
						$calls = $calls.append(call)
					}
				}
			}
		}
		$calls
	}
}

## Whether a type declaration's header has no parameters.
is_bare_header : Source.File, Source.Node -> Bool
is_bare_header = |file, header|
	header.kind == "header" and (header.kids.is_empty() or Source.kid_node(file, header, 1).kids.is_empty())

## The name roc-types gives the type declared at node `place`: the names of
## the declarations around it and its own, joined by dots (`Peers.Hue` for a
