cookbook/roc/count_roc/count_roc.roc, 240 lines

## count_roc is a test-density report for a tree of Roc projects: folder by
## folder, its modules and their lines, the same for its test modules, and
## its `expect`s. For one app's size, `roc loc main.roc` counts what its
## imports reach; count_roc counts every `.roc` file under each folder,
## with a row a folder, so it sees a whole tree of apps, the tests `roc loc`
## doesn't count, and the modules no import reaches (specs a test root
## alone imports). Its launcher,
## cookbook/roc/count_roc.shale, is how it is run, and says the arguments.
##
##   cd ~/showell_repos && shale cookbook:roc/count_roc.shale in=roc-chat,roc-markdown/package
##
## The work is plain Roc over two of Shale's effects: `Shale.glob!` names a
## folder's `.roc` files and `Shale.read!` gives each one's text. A folder
## that isn't there stops the run (`Shale.exists!`, `Shale.fail!`).
## budget: steps=400000000 reads=50000 arena_bytes=1000000000
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale

## What one folder holds.
Count : {
	place : Str,
	modules : U64,
	lines : U64,
	test_modules : U64,
	test_lines : U64,
	expects : U64,
}

## The literals that pick out the modules to treat apart: a path holding one
## of `tests` is a test module's, and one holding one of `skips` is left out.
Markers : { tests : List(Str), skips : List(Str) }

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	markers = {
		tests: literals(Shale.arg!("tests", default_tests)),
		skips: literals(Shale.arg!("skip", "")),
	}
	var $counts = []
	for place in literals(Shale.arg!("folders", ".")) {
		$counts = $counts.append(count_folder!(place, markers))
	}
	Shale.print!(count_table($counts))
}

## The literals of a test module's path unless `tests=` is given: the
## folders and file endings our Roc repos give their tests, specs and gates.
default_tests : Str
default_tests = "/gates/,/tests/,Tests.roc,Expects.roc,_test.roc,Spec.roc,Specs.roc,/specs"

## A comma-separated list's items, each trimmed, the empty ones dropped.
literals : Str -> List(Str)
literals = |text|
	text.split_on(",").map(Str.trim).drop_if(Str.is_empty)

# ── Counting a folder

count_folder! : Str, Markers => Count
count_folder! = |place, markers| {
	if !(Shale.exists!(place)) {
		Shale.fail!("count_roc: no folder `${place}`")
	}
	var $count = {
		place,
		modules: 0,
		lines: 0,
		test_modules: 0,
		test_lines: 0,
		expects: 0,
	}
	for path in Shale.glob!(roc_files_pattern(place)) {
		if !(is_build_output(path) or has_any_marker(path, markers.skips)) {
			match Shale.read!(path) {
				Found(text) => {
					is_test = has_any_marker(path, markers.tests)
					$count = with_file($count, { text, is_test })
				}
				Missing => Shale.fail!("count_roc: ${path} went missing during the count")
			}
		}
	}
	$count
}

## The glob of every `.roc` file below the folder. Shale's glob leaves out
## hidden names, so `.git` and `.zig-cache` are never walked.
roc_files_pattern : Str -> Str
roc_files_pattern = |place|
	if place == "." {
		"**/*.roc"
	} else {
		"${place}/**/*.roc"
	}

## Whether the path is under a build's `zig-out` folder.
is_build_output : Str -> Bool
is_build_output = |path|
	path.contains("/zig-out/")

has_any_marker : Str, List(Str) -> Bool
has_any_marker = |path, markers|
	markers.any(|marker| path.contains(marker))

## The count with one more file added, a module or a test module.
with_file : Count, { text : Str, is_test : Bool } -> Count
with_file = |count, file| {
	lines = line_count(file.text)
	expects = count.expects + expect_count(file.text)
	if file.is_test {
		{
			..count,
			test_modules: count.test_modules + 1,
			test_lines: count.test_lines + lines,
			expects,
		}
	} else {
		{
			..count,
			modules: count.modules + 1,
			lines: count.lines + lines,
			expects,
		}
	}
}

# ── Reading a module's text

## The newlines, and a last line that has none, as Shale's `count_lines`
## counts them.
line_count : Str -> U64
line_count = |text| {
	bytes = text.to_utf8()
	newlines = bytes.count_if(|byte| byte == '\n')
	match bytes.last() {
		Ok('\n') => newlines
		Ok(_) => newlines + 1
		Err(_) => 0
	}
}

## The lines that start an `expect`: the word itself after any indent, not
## a longer name such as `expected`.
expect_count : Str -> U64
expect_count = |text|
	text.split_on("\n").count_if(is_expect_line)

is_expect_line : Str -> Bool
is_expect_line = |line| {
	rest = bytes_after_indent(line.to_utf8())
	if rest.starts_with(Str.to_utf8("expect")) {
		match rest.get(6) {
			Ok(byte) => !(is_word_byte(byte))
			Err(_) => Bool.True
		}
	} else {
		Bool.False
	}
}

## The bytes after a line's indent: spaces, tabs and the other bytes a
## regular expression's `\s` matches.
bytes_after_indent : List(U8) -> List(U8)
bytes_after_indent = |bytes|
	match bytes.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_space_byte(byte))) {
		Ok(start) => bytes.drop_first(start)
		Err(_) => []
	}

is_space_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_space_byte = |byte|
	byte == ' ' or byte == '\t' or byte == '\r' or byte == 0x0b or byte == 0x0c

## A letter, a digit or `_`: what a regular expression's `\w` matches.
is_word_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_word_byte = |byte|
	is_ascii_letter(byte) or (byte >= '0' and byte <= '9') or byte == '_'

is_ascii_letter : U8 -> Bool
is_ascii_letter = |byte|
	(byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or (byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z')

# ── The table

## A column's heading and which side its cells line up on.
Column : { heading : Str, alignment : [Left, Right] }

columns : List(Column)
columns = [
	{ heading: "place", alignment: Left },
	{ heading: "modules", alignment: Right },
	{ heading: "lines", alignment: Right },
	{ heading: "test_modules", alignment: Right },
	{ heading: "test_lines", alignment: Right },
	{ heading: "expects", alignment: Right },
]

count_cells : Count -> List(Str)
count_cells = |count| [
	count.place,
	count.modules.to_str(),
	count.lines.to_str(),
	count.test_modules.to_str(),
	count.test_lines.to_str(),
	count.expects.to_str(),
]

## The counts as Shale's `table` prints rows: a line of headings, then a line
## a folder, each column as wide as its widest cell, columns two spaces
## apart, the numbers right-aligned.
count_table : List(Count) -> Str
count_table = |counts| {
	rows = counts.map(count_cells).prepend(columns.map(|column| column.heading))
	widths = rows.fold(columns.map(|_| 0), with_row)
	layouts = List.map2(
		columns,
		widths,
		|column, width| { alignment: column.alignment, width },
	)
	table_lines = rows.map(|row| Str.join_with(List.map2(layouts, row, padded_cell), "  "))
	Str.join_with(table_lines, "\n")
}

## Each column's width so far, widened to fit the row's cell.
with_row : List(U64), List(Str) -> List(U64)
with_row = |widths, cells|
	List.map2(
		widths,
		cells,
		|width, cell| U64.max(width, cell.count_utf8_bytes()),
	)

padded_cell : { alignment : [Left, Right], width : U64 }, Str -> Str
padded_cell = |layout, cell| {
	gap = " ".repeat(layout.width - cell.count_utf8_bytes())
	match layout.alignment {
		Left => "${cell}${gap}"
		Right => "${gap}${cell}"
	}
}

Shale original

cookbook/roc/count_roc.shale, 55 lines, at f8b34ec1

-- This recipe counts a Roc project: for each folder of `in`, its modules and
-- lines of Roc, the same for its tests, and its `expect`s, the numbers a
-- landing page or a review quotes. A module is a test's when its path holds
-- one of `tests`' literals (by default `/gates/`, `/tests/`, `Tests.roc`,
-- `Expects.roc` and `_test.roc`); `skip` names more literals whose modules
-- are left out (a book's builder inside an app's folder, say). Build output
-- (zig-out, .zig-cache and every hidden folder) is never counted.
--
--   cd ~/showell_repos && shale shale/cookbook/roc/count_roc.shale in=roc-apps/basic,roc-markdown/package
--   cd ~/showell_repos && shale shale/cookbook/roc/count_roc.shale in=roc-apps/canvas_apps/safari skip=/tutorial/
--
-- budget: steps=400000000 reads=50000 arena_bytes=1000000000

const IN = arg("in", ".")
const TESTS = arg("tests", "/gates/,/tests/,Tests.roc,Expects.roc,_test.roc")
const SKIP = arg("skip", "")

function literals(s)
  local out = {}
  for x in split(s, ",") do
    if trim(x) ~= "" then push(out, trim(x)) end
  end
  return out
end

function holds_any(path, lits)
  for l in lits do
    if contains(path, l) then return true end
  end
  return false
end

const TEST_LITS = literals(TESTS)
const SKIP_LITS = literals(SKIP)

local rows = {}
for place in literals(IN) do
  local row = {place = place, modules = 0, lines = 0, test_modules = 0, test_lines = 0, expects = 0}
  for e in walk_all(place, {kind = "file", skip = ".*", like = "*.roc"}) do
    if not contains(e.path, "/zig-out/") and not holds_any(e.path, SKIP_LITS) then
      local text = read(e.path)
      local n = count_lines(e.path)
      row.expects = row.expects + #re_lines(text, "^\\s*expect\\b")
      if holds_any(e.path, TEST_LITS) then
        row.test_modules = row.test_modules + 1
        row.test_lines = row.test_lines + n
      else
        row.modules = row.modules + 1
        row.lines = row.lines + n
      end
    end
  end
  push(rows, row)
end
print(table(rows, {"place", "modules", "lines", "test_modules", "test_lines", "expects"}))

list_long_files

The .zig files over a thousand lines in the repos we work in, longest first: the smallest walk, a sort and a table.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.print!, Shale.read!.
Roc: 96 lines in 1 file. Shale original: 20 lines.

Roc

cookbook/zig/list_long_files/list_long_files.roc, 96 lines

## list_long_files lists the `.zig` files over a thousand lines in the repos
## we work in, longest first, then how many of all their `.zig` files that
## is. Its launcher, cookbook/zig/list_long_files.shale, is how it is run,
## from the folder that holds the repos:
##
##   cd ~/showell_repos && shale cookbook:zig/list_long_files.shale over=500
##
## The work is plain Roc over three of Shale's effects: `Shale.glob!` names a
## repo's `.zig` files, `Shale.read!` gives each one's text, and
## `Shale.print!` writes the table. `Shale.arg!` reads `over`, and
## `Shale.fail!` stops the run on an `over` that is no integer.
## budget: steps=200000000 reads=100000 read_bytes=1000000000 arena_bytes=1000000000
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale

## The repos it walks, each a folder of the root it runs in. A repo that
## isn't there adds nothing.
repos : List(Str)
repos = ["shale", "angry-gopher", "zig-ast"]

## A `.zig` file and its lines.
ZigFile : { lines : U64, path : Str }

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	over = read_limit!({})
	var $files = []
	for repo in repos {
		for path in Shale.glob!("${repo}/**/*.zig") {
			$files = $files.append({ lines: line_count(read_text!(path)), path })
		}
	}
	long_files = $files.keep_if(|file| file.lines.to_i64_wrap() > over)
	longest_first = long_files.sort_by_reversed(|file| file.lines)
	Shale.print!(long_files_table(longest_first))
	counts = "${long_files.len().to_str()} of ${$files.len().to_str()}"
	Shale.print!("${counts} .zig files are over ${over.to_str()} lines")
}

## The `over=` limit: 1000 unless given, and any integer, so `over=-1`
## lists every file.
read_limit! : {} => I64
read_limit! = |{}| {
	given = Shale.arg!("over", "1000")
	match I64.from_str(given) {
		Ok(limit) => limit
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("list_long_files: over=${given} is not an integer")
			0
		}
	}
}

## The file's text. A file the glob named and the read finds gone stops the
## run.
read_text! : Str => Str
read_text! = |path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("list_long_files: ${path} went missing during the walk")
			""
		}
	}

## The newlines, and a last line that has none, as Shale's `count_lines`
## counts them.
line_count : Str -> U64
line_count = |text| {
	bytes = text.to_utf8()
	newlines = bytes.count_if(|byte| byte == '\n')
	match bytes.last() {
		Ok('\n') => newlines
		Ok(_) => newlines + 1
		Err(_) => 0
	}
}

## The files as Shale's `table` prints them: a line of headings, then a line
## a file, the line counts right-aligned under `lines` and the paths after
## two spaces.
long_files_table : List(ZigFile) -> Str
long_files_table = |files| {
	width = files.fold(
		"lines".count_utf8_bytes(),
		|widest, file| U64.max(widest, file.lines.to_str().count_utf8_bytes()),
	)
	heading = "${right_aligned("lines", width)}  path"
	rows = files.map(|file| "${right_aligned(file.lines.to_str(), width)}  ${file.path}")
	Str.join_with(rows.prepend(heading), "\n")
}

right_aligned : Str, U64 -> Str
right_aligned = |cell, width|
	"${" ".repeat(width - cell.count_utf8_bytes())}${cell}"

Shale original

cookbook/zig/list_long_files.shale, 20 lines, at f7898161

-- This script lists the .zig files over a thousand lines in the repos we work
-- in, longest first. `over=N` sets another limit. Run it from the folder that
-- holds the repos:
--   cd ~/showell_repos && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/list_long_files.shale [over=N]

const OVER = arg("over", 1000)

local repos = {"shale", "angry-gopher", "zig-ast"}
local long_files = {}
local file_count = 0
for repo in repos do
  for path in glob(repo .. "/**/*.zig") do
    file_count = file_count + 1
    local line_count = count_lines(path)
    if line_count > OVER then push(long_files, {lines = line_count, path = path}) end
  end
end
sort(long_files, "lines", "desc")
print(table(long_files, {"lines", "path"}))
print(#long_files .. " of " .. file_count .. " .zig files are over " .. OVER .. " lines")

count_comments

How much each Zig file's comments say and how loudly: each trimmed line a tag (blank, code, doc, plain), per-file ratios, and the regular expressions done as byte patterns in plain Roc.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.exists!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.print!, Shale.read!.
Roc: 477 lines in 1 file. Shale original: 96 lines.

Roc

cookbook/zig/count_comments/count_comments.roc, 477 lines

## count_comments counts how much a Zig tree's comments say, and how loudly:
## for each file its code lines, its doc lines (`///`, `//!`), its plain `//`
## lines, comment lines per 100 lines of code, words a comment line, and the
## loud and dated comment lines; the loudest first, then the whole's totals.
## Its launcher, cookbook/zig/count_comments.shale, is how it is run, and its
## header says the arguments and the rules.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:zig/count_comments.shale top=10
##
## The work is plain Roc over Shale's effects: `Shale.arg!` reads `dir`,
## `files` and `top`; `Shale.glob!` and `Shale.exists!` name the files;
## `Shale.read!` gives each one's text; `Shale.print!` writes the table; and
## `Shale.fail!` stops the run when no file matches or `top` is no integer.
## Each line is read as bytes, so a word boundary is a regular expression's
## `\b`: an ASCII letter, digit or `_` against anything else.
## budget: steps=900000000 reads=100000 read_bytes=400000000 arena_bytes=2000000000
app [main!] { pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale

## What a line is, once its indent and its ends are trimmed: nothing, code
## (a comment after code counts as code), or a comment line alone.
LineKind : [Blank, Code, Doc, Plain]

## The counts of a file, or of the whole.
Tally : {
	code : U64,
	doc : U64,
	plain : U64,
	words : U64,
	loud : U64,
	dated : U64,
}

## A file's row: the path as the table shows it, and its counts.
Row : { file : Str, tally : Tally }

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	folder = Shale.arg!("dir", ".")
	patterns = Shale.arg!("files", "src/**/*.zig,tools/*.zig,build.zig")
	top = read_top!({})
	paths = find_files!(folder, patterns)
	if paths.is_empty() {
		Shale.fail!("count_comments: no file matches ${patterns} under ${folder}")
	}
	var $rows = []
	for path in paths {
		tally = tally_lines(read_text!(path).to_utf8())
		$rows = $rows.append({ file: shown_path(folder, path), tally })
	}
	total = $rows.fold(no_lines, |sum, row| sum_of(sum, row.tally))
	loudest_first = $rows.sort_by_reversed(|row| row.tally.loud)
	shown_rows = if top > 0 {
		loudest_first.take_first(top.to_u64_wrap())
	} else {
		loudest_first
	}
	Shale.print!(rows_table(shown_rows))
	file_count = paths.len()
	Shale.print!(summary(file_count, total))
}

## The `top=` row count: 0, every row, unless given.
read_top! : {} => I64
read_top! = |{}| {
	given = Shale.arg!("top", "0")
	match I64.from_str(given) {
		Ok(count) => count
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("count_comments: top=${given} is not an integer")
			0
		}
	}
}

# ── The files

## The files the comma-separated globs name under the folder, each once, in
## the order named. A pattern with no `*` is a file's path, kept when it is
## there.
find_files! : Str, Str => List(Str)
find_files! = |folder, patterns| {
	var $paths = []
	var $seen = Set.empty()
	for pattern in patterns.split_on(",") {
		for path in find_pattern_files!(folder, trim_ends(pattern)) {
			if !($seen.contains(path)) {
				$seen = $seen.insert(path)
				$paths = $paths.append(path)
			}
		}
	}
	$paths
}

find_pattern_files! : Str, Str => List(Str)
find_pattern_files! = |folder, pattern| {
	full = if folder == "." {
		pattern
	} else {
		"${folder}/${pattern}"
	}
	if pattern.contains("*") {
		Shale.glob!(full)
	} else if Shale.exists!(full) {
		[full]
	} else {
		[]
	}
}

## The file's text. A file named a moment ago and gone now stops the run.
read_text! : Str => Str
read_text! = |path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("count_comments: ${path} went missing during the count")
			""
		}
	}

## The path as the table shows it: below the folder, without the folder.
shown_path : Str, Str -> Str
shown_path = |folder, path|
	if folder != "." and path.starts_with("${folder}/") {
		path.drop_prefix("${folder}/")
	} else {
		path
	}

## The text without the spaces, tabs, carriage returns and newlines at its
## ends, as Shale's `trim` takes them.
trim_ends : Str -> Str
trim_ends = |text| {
	kept = trimmed_bytes(text.to_utf8())
	Str.from_utf8(kept) ?? text
}

# ── Counting a file's lines

no_lines : Tally
no_lines = {
	code: 0,
	doc: 0,
	plain: 0,
	words: 0,
	loud: 0,
	dated: 0,
}

## A file's counts, from its bytes: each line, split at its newlines,
## trimmed and counted.
tally_lines : List(U8) -> Tally
tally_lines = |bytes|
	bytes.split_on('\n').fold(no_lines, |tally, line| with_line(tally, trimmed_bytes(line)))

## The tally with one trimmed line more.
with_line : Tally, List(U8) -> Tally
with_line = |tally, line|
	match line_kind(line) {
		Blank => tally
		Code => { ..tally, code: tally.code + 1 }
		Doc => with_comment({ ..tally, doc: tally.doc + 1 }, line)
		Plain => with_comment({ ..tally, plain: tally.plain + 1 }, line)
	}

line_kind : List(U8) -> LineKind
line_kind = |line|
	if line.is_empty() {
		Blank
	} else if line.starts_with(['/', '/', '/']) or line.starts_with(['/', '/', '!']) {
		Doc
	} else if line.starts_with(['/', '/']) {
		Plain
	} else {
		Code
	}

## A comment line's words (after its first three bytes, the `//` and the
## space or mark after it), and whether it is loud or dated.
with_comment : Tally, List(U8) -> Tally
with_comment = |tally, line| {
	..tally,
	words: tally.words + word_count(line.drop_first(3)),
	loud: tally.loud + one_if(is_loud(line)),
	dated: tally.dated + one_if(is_dated(line)),
}

one_if : Bool -> U64
one_if = |holds|
	if holds {
		1
	} else {
		0
	}

sum_of : Tally, Tally -> Tally
sum_of = |sum, more| {
	code: sum.code + more.code,
	doc: sum.doc + more.doc,
	plain: sum.plain + more.plain,
	words: sum.words + more.words,
	loud: sum.loud + more.loud,
	dated: sum.dated + more.dated,
}

# ── Reading a line's bytes

## The bytes between the line's leading and trailing spaces, tabs, carriage
## returns and newlines.
trimmed_bytes : List(U8) -> List(U8)
trimmed_bytes = |bytes|
	match bytes.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_trimmed_byte(byte))) {
		Ok(start) => {
			end = bytes.find_last_index(|byte| !(is_trimmed_byte(byte))) ?? start
			bytes.sublist({ start, len: end + 1 - start })
		}
		Err(_) => []
	}

is_trimmed_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_trimmed_byte = |byte|
	byte == ' ' or byte == '\t' or byte == '\r' or byte == '\n'

## The words, as Shale's `words` splits them: at spaces, tabs, newlines,
## carriage returns, vertical tabs and form feeds.
word_count : List(U8) -> U64
word_count = |bytes| {
	counted = bytes.fold(
		{ words: 0, in_word: Bool.False },
		|so_far, byte|
			if is_word_gap(byte) {
				{ ..so_far, in_word: Bool.False }
			} else if so_far.in_word {
				so_far
			} else {
				{ words: so_far.words + 1, in_word: Bool.True }
			},
	)
	counted.words
}

is_word_gap : U8 -> Bool
is_word_gap = |byte|
	is_trimmed_byte(byte) or byte == 0x0b or byte == 0x0c

## A letter, a digit or `_`: what a regular expression's `\w` matches.
is_word_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_word_byte = |byte|
	is_upper(byte) or (byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or (byte >= '0' and byte <= '9') or byte == '_'

is_upper : U8 -> Bool
is_upper = |byte|
	byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z'

## A part of a pattern: a byte as it is, or any digit.
Part : [Byte(U8), Digit]

literal_parts : Str -> List(Part)
literal_parts = |text|
	text.to_utf8().map(|byte| Byte(byte))

## Whether `holds_at` holds at some place of a line of `length` bytes.
any_place : U64, (U64 -> Bool) -> Bool
any_place = |length, holds_at|
	U64.until(0, length).fold(Bool.False, |found, at| found or holds_at(at))

## Whether the bytes start with the pattern's parts.
starts_with_parts : List(U8), List(Part) -> Bool
starts_with_parts = |bytes, parts| {
	fits_each = |fits, offset| fits and part_fits(bytes.get(offset), parts.get(offset))
	parts.len() <= bytes.len() and U64.until(0, parts.len()).fold(Bool.True, fits_each)
}

part_fits : Try(U8, [OutOfBounds]), Try(Part, [OutOfBounds]) -> Bool
part_fits = |byte, part|
	match (byte, part) {
		(Ok(got), Ok(Byte(wanted))) => got == wanted
		(Ok(got), Ok(Digit)) => got >= '0' and got <= '9'
		_ => Bool.False
	}

## Whether the pattern's parts are anywhere in the bytes.
holds : List(U8), List(Part) -> Bool
holds = |bytes, parts|
	any_place(bytes.len(), |at| starts_with_parts(bytes.drop_first(at), parts))

## Whether the pattern is in the bytes as a word of its own, with no word
## byte just before it or just after it. Every pattern this asks of starts
## and ends with a word byte, so this is a regular expression's `\b...\b`.
holds_word : List(U8), List(Part) -> Bool
holds_word = |bytes, parts| {
	is_word_at_place = |at| {
		fits = starts_with_parts(bytes.drop_first(at), parts)
		fits and is_boundary(bytes, at) and is_boundary(bytes, at + parts.len())
	}
	any_place(bytes.len(), is_word_at_place)
}

## Whether the place before byte `at` is a regular expression's `\b`: a word
## byte on one side of it and none on the other, the line's ends counting as
## none.
is_boundary : List(U8), U64 -> Bool
is_boundary = |bytes, at| {
	word_before = if at == 0 {
		Bool.False
	} else {
		is_word_at(bytes, at - 1)
	}
	word_before != is_word_at(bytes, at)
}

is_word_at : List(U8), U64 -> Bool
is_word_at = |bytes, at|
	match bytes.get(at) {
		Ok(byte) => is_word_byte(byte)
		Err(_) => Bool.False
	}

## A loud line holds `**`, a `──` banner, or a heading of two upper-case
## words or more (`THE HUNT`).
is_loud : List(U8) -> Bool
is_loud = |line|
	holds(line, double_star_parts) or holds(line, banner_parts) or holds_heading(line)

double_star_parts : List(Part)
double_star_parts = literal_parts("**")

banner_parts : List(Part)
banner_parts = literal_parts("──")

## Whether a word starts with two capitals or more, then a space, then two
## capitals or more: the regular expression `\b[A-Z][A-Z]+ [A-Z][A-Z]+`.
holds_heading : List(U8) -> Bool
holds_heading = |line|
	any_place(line.len(), |at| is_heading_at(line, at))

is_heading_at : List(U8), U64 -> Bool
is_heading_at = |line, at| {
	capitals = capitals_from(line, at)
	capitals >= 2
		and is_boundary(line, at)
		and line.get(at + capitals) == Ok(' ')
		and capitals_from(line, at + capitals + 1) >= 2
}

## How many capitals in a row start at `at`.
capitals_from : List(U8), U64 -> U64
capitals_from = |line, at|
	match line.drop_first(at).find_first_index(|byte| !(is_upper(byte))) {
		Ok(count) => count
		Err(_) => line.len() - U64.min(at, line.len())
	}

## A dated line names a QUEUE or FEEDBACK item, a date (`2026-10-20`), or a
## person (`Steve`, `the box`, `CC`), each a word of its own but the items.
is_dated : List(U8) -> Bool
is_dated = |line|
	items.any(|item| holds(line, item)) or dated_words.any(|word| holds_word(line, word))

items : List(List(Part))
items = [literal_parts("QUEUE"), literal_parts("FEEDBACK")]

dated_words : List(List(Part))
dated_words = [
	date_parts,
	literal_parts("Steve"),
	literal_parts("the box"),
	literal_parts("CC"),
]

## `20` and six more digits as a year, a month and a day: `2026-10-20`.
date_parts : List(Part)
date_parts = [
	Byte('2'),
	Byte('0'),
	Digit,
	Digit,
	Byte('-'),
	Digit,
	Digit,
	Byte('-'),
	Digit,
	Digit,
]

# ── The table and the totals

## A share as `n.d`, of `part` per 100 of `whole`, rounded; `-` of nothing.
per100 : U64, U64 -> Str
per100 = |part, whole|
	if whole == 0 {
		"-"
	} else {
		tenths = (part * 1000 + whole // 2) // whole
		"${(tenths // 10).to_str()}.${(tenths % 10).to_str()}"
	}

## A column's heading and which side its cells line up on.
Column : { heading : Str, alignment : [Left, Right] }

columns : List(Column)
columns = [
	{ heading: "file", alignment: Left },
	{ heading: "code", alignment: Right },
	{ heading: "doc", alignment: Right },
	{ heading: "plain", alignment: Right },
	{ heading: "per100", alignment: Left },
	{ heading: "words", alignment: Left },
	{ heading: "loud", alignment: Right },
	{ heading: "dated", alignment: Right },
]

row_cells : Row -> List(Str)
row_cells = |row| {
	tally = row.tally
	comments = tally.doc + tally.plain
	[
		row.file,
		tally.code.to_str(),
		tally.doc.to_str(),
		tally.plain.to_str(),
		per100(comments, tally.code),
		per100(tally.words, comments * 100),
		tally.loud.to_str(),
		tally.dated.to_str(),
	]
}

## The rows as Shale's `table` prints them: a line of headings, then a line
## a file, each column as wide as its widest cell, columns two spaces
## apart, the counts right-aligned and the shares, which are text, left.
rows_table : List(Row) -> Str
rows_table = |rows| {
	cells = rows.map(row_cells).prepend(columns.map(|column| column.heading))
	widths = cells.fold(columns.map(|_| 0), with_row)
	layouts = List.map2(
		columns,
		widths,
		|column, width| { alignment: column.alignment, width },
	)
	table_lines = cells.map(|row| Str.join_with(List.map2(layouts, row, padded_cell), "  "))
	Str.join_with(table_lines, "\n")
}

## Each column's width so far, widened to fit the row's cell.
with_row : List(U64), List(Str) -> List(U64)
with_row = |widths, cells|
	List.map2(
		widths,
		cells,
		|width, cell| U64.max(width, cell.count_utf8_bytes()),
	)

padded_cell : { alignment : [Left, Right], width : U64 }, Str -> Str
padded_cell = |layout, cell| {
	gap = " ".repeat(layout.width - cell.count_utf8_bytes())
	match layout.alignment {
		Left => "${cell}${gap}"
		Right => "${gap}${cell}"
	}
}

## The whole's line under the table.
summary : U64, Tally -> Str
summary = |file_count, total| {
	comments = total.doc + total.plain
	lines = "${total.code.to_str()} code lines, ${comments.to_str()} comment lines"
	kinds = "${total.doc.to_str()} doc, ${total.plain.to_str()} plain"
	per_code = per100(comments, total.code)
	per_comment = per100(total.words, comments * 100)
	shares = "${per_code} per 100, ${per_comment} words a line"
	marks = "${total.loud.to_str()} loud, ${total.dated.to_str()} dated"
	"${file_count.to_str()} files: ${lines} (${kinds}), ${shares}, ${marks}"
}

cookbook/zig/count_comments.shale, 96 lines, at e83affc0

-- This recipe counts how much a Zig tree's comments say, and how loudly. For
-- each file it gives its code lines, its doc lines (`///`, `//!`), its plain
-- `//` lines, comment lines per 100 lines of code, words a comment line, and
-- the loud and dated comment lines. Run before and after a commit that
-- rewrites comments, it shows what the commit changed.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/count_comments.shale
--   shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/count_comments.shale dir=zig:lib/std/zig files=AstGen.zig,Parse.zig,Zir.zig
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/zig/count_comments.shale top=10
--
-- `files` is comma-separated globs under `dir` (default `.`, the root;
-- a mount works): default `src/**/*.zig,tools/*.zig,build.zig`. A glob's
-- `*` on the command line is the shell's unless quoted.
--
-- A line is code when it holds anything but a comment, a comment line
-- when it is only one (a comment after code counts as code). A loud line
-- holds `**`, a heading of two upper-case words or more (`THE HUNT`), or a
-- `──` banner. A dated line names a QUEUE or
-- FEEDBACK item, a date (`2026-10-20`), or a person (`Steve`, `the box`,
-- `CC`). The table is the loudest first, `top` rows of it (default all),
-- then the whole's totals.
--
-- budget: steps=900000000 reads=100000 read_bytes=400000000 arena_bytes=2000000000

const DIR = arg("dir", ".")
const FILES = arg("files", "src/**/*.zig,tools/*.zig,build.zig")
const TOP = arg("top", 0)

function is_loud(c)
  return contains(c, "**") or contains(c, "──") or re_match(c, "\\b[A-Z][A-Z]+ [A-Z][A-Z]+")
end

function is_dated(c)
  return re_match(c, "QUEUE|FEEDBACK|\\b20\\d\\d-\\d\\d-\\d\\d\\b|\\bSteve\\b|\\bthe box\\b|\\bCC\\b")
end

-- The files `FILES` names under `DIR`, each once, in the order named.
local paths = {}
local seen = {}
for pattern in split(FILES, ",") do
  local p = trim(pattern)
  local full = p
  if DIR ~= "." then full = DIR .. "/" .. p end
  local got = {}
  if contains(p, "*") then got = glob(full) elseif exists(full) then got = {full} end
  for g in got do
    if not get(seen, g, false) then
      seen[g] = true
      push(paths, g)
    end
  end
end
if #paths == 0 then fail("count_comments: no file matches " .. FILES .. " under " .. DIR) end

local rows = {}
local all = {code = 0, doc = 0, plain = 0, words = 0, loud = 0, dated = 0}
for p in paths do
  local r = {code = 0, doc = 0, plain = 0, words = 0, loud = 0, dated = 0}
  for l in lines(read(p)) do
    local t = trim(l)
    if t ~= "" then
      if starts_with(t, "//") then
        if starts_with(t, "///") or starts_with(t, "//!") then r.doc = r.doc + 1 else r.plain = r.plain + 1 end
        r.words = r.words + #words(sub(t, 4))
        if is_loud(t) then r.loud = r.loud + 1 end
        if is_dated(t) then r.dated = r.dated + 1 end
      else
        r.code = r.code + 1
      end
    end
  end
  for k in keys(all) do all[k] = all[k] + r[k] end
  local shown = p
  if DIR ~= "." and starts_with(p, DIR .. "/") then shown = sub(p, #DIR + 2) end
  push(rows, {file = shown, code = r.code, doc = r.doc, plain = r.plain, loud = r.loud, dated = r.dated, r = r})
end

-- A share as `n.d`, of `part` per 100 of `whole`.
function per100(part, whole)
  if whole == 0 then return "-" end
  local tenths = (part * 1000 + whole // 2) // whole
  return (tenths // 10) .. "." .. (tenths % 10)
end

for row in rows do
  local comments = row.r.doc + row.r.plain
  row.per100 = per100(comments, row.r.code)
  row.words = per100(row.r.words, comments * 100)
end
local sorted = sort(rows, "loud", "desc")
if TOP > 0 then sorted = take(sorted, TOP) end
print(table(sorted, {"file", "code", "doc", "plain", "per100", "words", "loud", "dated"}))
local comments = all.doc + all.plain
print(#paths .. " files: " .. all.code .. " code lines, " .. comments .. " comment lines (" .. all.doc .. " doc, " .. all.plain ..
  " plain), " .. per100(comments, all.code) .. " per 100, " .. per100(all.words, comments * 100) .. " words a line, " ..
  all.loud .. " loud, " .. all.dated .. " dated")

The shared Roc library

The modules the ports over Roc code share, as a package each app names in its header and imports as lib.X: Roc's parse tree read into records, a file's lines and words, a module's declarations, and a finding's line. Each example that imports it names the modules it uses.

cookbook/roc/lib/Bytes.roc, 128 lines

## A line's bytes read as Shale's builtins read a string: a place counted
## from 1, cut as `sub` cuts, trimmed as `trim` trims, and a width that is
## the bytes with a tab counting four. A recipe that scans Roc a byte at a
## time (Groups, Stacking) reads its lines through these, so its places and
## widths are its Shale original's.
Bytes := [].{

	## A line's width: its bytes, a tab counting four.
	width_of : List(U8) -> U64
	width_of = |bytes| bytes.len() + 3 * bytes.count_if(|byte| byte == '\t')

	## The width of a line given as text.
	line_width : Str -> U64
	line_width = |text| Bytes.width_of(text.to_utf8())

	## Line `number` of the lines, counted from 1, as bytes: empty past the end.
	line_of : List(Str), U64 -> List(U8)
	line_of = |source_lines, number|
		if number == 0 {
			[]
		} else {
			(source_lines.get(number - 1) ?? "").to_utf8()
		}

	## The byte at `place`, counted from 1, or 0 past either end.
	byte_at : List(U8), U64 -> U8
	byte_at = |bytes, place|
		if place == 0 {
			0
		} else {
			bytes.get(place - 1) ?? 0
		}

	## Shale's `sub(s, first, last)` of bytes: the places from `first` to
	## `last`, counted from 1, cut to the bytes there are.
	span : List(U8), U64, U64 -> List(U8)
	span = |bytes, first, last| {
		start = if first == 0 {
			1
		} else {
			first
		}
		end = if last < bytes.len() {
			last
		} else {
			bytes.len()
		}
		if start > end {
			[]
		} else {
			bytes.sublist({ start: start - 1, len: end - start + 1 })
		}
	}

	## Shale's `sub(s, first)`: the bytes from place `first` to the end.
	rest_from : List(U8), U64 -> List(U8)
	rest_from = |bytes, first| Bytes.span(bytes, first, bytes.len())

	## The bytes without the spaces, tabs, carriage returns and newlines at
	## their ends, as Shale's `trim` takes them.
	trimmed : List(U8) -> List(U8)
	trimmed = |bytes|
		match bytes.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_blank(byte))) {
			Ok(start) => {
				end = bytes.find_last_index(|byte| !(is_blank(byte))) ?? start
				bytes.sublist({ start, len: end + 1 - start })
			}
			Err(_) => []
		}

	## The bytes without the blanks at their end, as Shale's `trim_end`.
	trimmed_end : List(U8) -> List(U8)
	trimmed_end = |bytes|
		match bytes.find_last_index(|byte| !(is_blank(byte))) {
			Ok(end) => bytes.take_first(end + 1)
			Err(_) => []
		}

	## Whether `byte` is one of `[A-Za-z0-9_]`.
	is_word_byte : U8 -> Bool
	is_word_byte = |byte| Bytes.is_letter(byte) or Bytes.is_digit(byte) or byte == '_'

	## Whether `byte` is an ASCII letter, small or capital.
	is_letter : U8 -> Bool
	is_letter = |byte| (byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or (byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z')

	## Whether `byte` is a digit.
	is_digit : U8 -> Bool
	is_digit = |byte| byte >= '0' and byte <= '9'

	## Whether `byte` is a small letter or `_`, which starts a lower name.
	starts_lower_name : U8 -> Bool
	starts_lower_name = |byte| (byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or byte == '_'

	## The last byte before `place` that is not a space, or 0.
	byte_before : List(U8), U64 -> U8
	byte_before = |bytes, place| {
		var $at = place - 1
		while $at > 0 and Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $at) == ' ' {
			$at = $at - 1
		}
		Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $at)
	}

	## The first place at `place` or after it that is no space: the end of ` *`.
	spaces_end : List(U8), U64 -> U64
	spaces_end = |bytes, place| {
		var $end = place
		while Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end) == ' ' {
			$end = $end + 1
		}
		$end
	}

	## The first place at `place` or after it that is no `[A-Za-z0-9_]`.
	word_end : List(U8), U64 -> U64
	word_end = |bytes, place| {
		var $end = place
		while Bytes.is_word_byte(Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end)) {
			$end = $end + 1
		}
		$end
	}
}

## A byte Shale's `trim` takes off a text's ends.
is_blank : U8 -> Bool
is_blank = |byte| byte == ' ' or byte == '\t' or byte == '\r' or byte == '\n'

cookbook/roc/lib/Declarations.roc, 341 lines

## What a file declares at its top level or as a module type's member, read
## from its tree in file order: its types, its values and the record fields of its
## types and annotations, never a local's. Each carries `place`, its node's
## place in the tree, so the three kinds can be put back in file order.
import Text
import Tree

Declarations := {
	types : List(Declarations.TypeDeclared),
	values : List(Declarations.ValueDeclared),
	fields : List(Declarations.FieldDeclared),
}.{

	## A type declaration. `underlying` is the type it is built on as written
	## and `shape` the same as a shape (Tree.shape), both `""` when it is
	## built on none, as a module's `Cat := [].{ ... }` is not; `is_nominal`
	## says it is declared with `:=` or `::`, not as an alias with `:`;
	## `is_tag_union` and `is_function_type` say what it is built on.
	TypeDeclared : {
		path : Str,
		place : U64,
		line : U64,
		name : Str,
		owner : Str,
		underlying : Str,
		shape : Str,
		is_nominal : Bool,
		is_tag_union : Bool,
		is_function_type : Bool,
	}

	## A value: an annotation, or a definition with no annotation before it
	## (`annotated` false, its types `""`). `written_type` is its whole type,
	## `result_type` what it gives when it is a function, else the same, and
	## `first_type` its first argument's type, `""` when it takes none.
	## `has_text` says its definition is a string with something in it.
	ValueDeclared : {
		path : Str,
		place : U64,
		line : U64,
		name : Str,
		owner : Str,
		annotated : Bool,
		is_function : Bool,
		has_text : Bool,
		written_type : Str,
		result_type : Str,
		first_type : Str,
	}

	## A record field in a type or an annotation, with its type as written.
	FieldDeclared : {
		path : Str,
		place : U64,
		line : U64,
		name : Str,
		owner : Str,
		written_type : Str,
	}

	## A parsed file: its path, the file's nodes (its syntax tree, a node a
	## place) and its text cut at each newline.
	FileRead : {
		path : Str,
		nodes : List(Tree.Node),
		source_lines : List(Str),
	}

	## Nothing declared, to add files to.
	none_yet : Declarations
	none_yet = { types: [], values: [], fields: [] }

	## What `earlier` holds, then what `later` does.
	concat : Declarations, Declarations -> Declarations
	concat = |earlier, later| {
		types: earlier.types.concat(later.types),
		values: earlier.values.concat(later.values),
		fields: earlier.fields.concat(later.fields),
	}

	## What the file declares at its top level or as a module type's member,
	## each kind in file order. A definition of an annotated value sets the
	## annotation's `has_text`, and the last definition says.
	from_file : Declarations.FileRead -> Declarations
	from_file = |file| {
		nodes = file.nodes
		var $outer_answers = []
		var $declaration_lines = []
		var $annotation_places = Dict.empty()
		var $declared = Declarations.none_yet
		var $at = 0
		for node in nodes {
			$at = $at + 1
			at = $at
			place = { outer_answers: $outer_answers, parent: node.parent }
			is_outer = node.parent == 0 or is_outer_parent(nodes, place)
			$outer_answers = $outer_answers.append(is_outer)
			kind = node.kind
			is_declaration = kind == "s-type-anno" or kind == "s-type-decl"
			$declaration_lines = $declaration_lines.append(
				if is_outer and is_declaration {
					node.line
				} else {
					0
				},
			)
			if is_outer and kind == "s-type-decl" {
				match type_declared(file, at) {
					Ok(declared) => {
						$declared = { ..$declared, types: $declared.types.append(declared) }
					}
					Err(Unnamed) => {}
				}
			}
			field_place = { declaration_lines: $declaration_lines, at }
			if kind == "anno-record-field" and field_declaration_line(nodes, field_place) != 0 {
				field = {
					path: file.path,
					place: at,
					line: node.line,
					name: Tree.attribute(node, "name"),
					owner: owner_of(nodes, at),
					written_type: Tree.written_type(nodes, Tree.first_kid(node)),
				}
				$declared = { ..$declared, fields: $declared.fields.append(field) }
			}
			if is_outer and kind == "s-type-anno" {
				match annotated_value(file, at) {
					Ok(value) => {
						value_key = "${value.owner}.${value.name}"
						value_place = $declared.values.len()
						$annotation_places = $annotation_places.insert(value_key, value_place)
						$declared = { ..$declared, values: $declared.values.append(value) }
					}
					Err(OnlyWhere) => {}
				}
			}
			if is_outer and kind == "s-decl" and Tree.kid_kind(nodes, node, 1) == "p-ident" {
				name = Tree.attribute(Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.first_kid(node)), "raw")
				owner = owner_of(nodes, at)
				values = match $annotation_places.get("${owner}.${name}") {
					Ok(annotation_place) => {
						definition = { place: annotation_place, has_text: is_text(nodes, node) }
						with_text($declared.values, definition)
					}
					Err(_) => {
						value = {
							path: file.path,
							place: at,
							line: node.line,
							name,
							owner,
							annotated: Bool.False,
							is_function: Tree.kid_kind(nodes, node, 2) == "e-lambda",
							has_text: Bool.False,
							written_type: "",
							result_type: "",
							first_type: "",
						}
						$declared.values.append(value)
					}
				}
				$declared = { ..$declared, values }
			}
		}
		$declared
	}
}

## Whether a node's `parent` lets it be outer: the parent is outer itself, as
## `outer_answers` holds it so far (a parent comes before its kids), and of a
## kind a definition may sit in and still be top-level or a module type's
## member, the type's `associated` block among them. Inside any other kind,
## such as a lambda's block, a definition is local.
is_outer_parent : List(Tree.Node), { outer_answers : List(Bool), parent : U64 } -> Bool
is_outer_parent = |nodes, place| {
	parent_is_outer = match place.outer_answers.get(place.parent - 1) {
		Ok(answer) => answer
		Err(_) => {
			parent = place.parent.to_str()
			crash "Declarations: node ${parent} comes after its kid"
		}
	}
	kind = Tree.node_at(nodes, place.parent).kind
	parent_is_outer and ["file", "statements", "s-type-decl", "associated"].contains(kind)
}

## The name of the type declaration around node `at`, or "" at the top level.
owner_of : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Str
owner_of = |nodes, at| {
	var $up = Tree.node_at(nodes, at).parent
	while $up != 0 {
		node = Tree.node_at(nodes, $up)
		if node.kind == "s-type-decl" {
			return Tree.attribute(Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.first_kid(node)), "name")
		}
		$up = node.parent
	}
	""
}

## The line of the declaration the record field at `at` belongs to, as
## `declaration_lines` holds it so far, or 0 when an expression, a pattern or
## a definition lies between them (the field is then a local's), or the
## declaration is not outer.
field_declaration_line : List(Tree.Node), { declaration_lines : List(U64), at : U64 } -> U64
field_declaration_line = |nodes, field_place| {
	var $up = Tree.node_at(nodes, field_place.at).parent
	while $up != 0 {
		node = Tree.node_at(nodes, $up)
		if node.kind.starts_with("e-") or node.kind.starts_with("p-") or node.kind == "s-decl" {
			return 0
		}
		if node.kind == "s-type-anno" or node.kind == "s-type-decl" {
			return match field_place.declaration_lines.get($up - 1) {
				Ok(line) => line
				Err(_) => crash "Declarations: a field's declaration comes after it"
			}
		}
		$up = node.parent
	}
	0
}

## Whether the definition `node` gives a string with something in it: `""`
## spans two columns.
is_text : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> Bool
is_text = |nodes, node|
	match node.kids.get(1) {
		Ok(at) => {
			given = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
			is_wide = given.end_line > given.line or given.end_column > given.column + 2
			given.kind == "e-string" and is_wide
		}
		Err(_) => Bool.False
	}

## A definition of an annotated value: the annotation's place among the
## values, and whether the definition is a string with something in it.
Definition : { place : U64, has_text : Bool }

## The values with the annotation at the definition's place given its
## `has_text`.
with_text : List(Declarations.ValueDeclared), Definition -> List(Declarations.ValueDeclared)
with_text = |values, definition| {
	past_end = "Declarations: an annotation's place is past the values"
	value = match values.get(definition.place) {
		Ok(found) => found
		Err(OutOfBounds) => crash past_end
	}
	match values.set(definition.place, { ..value, has_text: definition.has_text }) {
		Ok(changed) => changed
		Err(OutOfBounds) => crash past_end
	}
}

## The annotation at `at`, unless it is only a `where` clause.
annotated_value : Declarations.FileRead, U64 -> Try(Declarations.ValueDeclared, [OnlyWhere])
annotated_value = |file, at| {
	nodes = file.nodes
	node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
	match node.kids.first() {
		Err(_) => Err(OnlyWhere)
		Ok(type_at) => {
			type_node = Tree.node_at(nodes, type_at)
			if type_node.kind == "where" {
				return Err(OnlyWhere)
			}
			written_type = Tree.written_type(nodes, type_at)
			is_function = type_node.kind == "ty-fn"
			result_type = if is_function {
				Tree.written_type(nodes, Tree.last_kid(type_node))
			} else {
				written_type
			}
			first_type = if is_function and type_node.kids.len() > 1 {
				Tree.written_type(nodes, Tree.first_kid(type_node))
			} else {
				""
			}
			Ok({
				path: file.path,
				place: at,
				line: node.line,
				name: Tree.attribute(node, "name"),
				owner: owner_of(nodes, at),
				annotated: Bool.True,
				is_function,
				has_text: Bool.False,
				written_type,
				result_type,
				first_type,
			})
		}
	}
}

## The type declared at `at`, when it has a name. Whether it is nominal is
## read from the text just after its name, where `:=` or `::` stands.
type_declared : Declarations.FileRead, U64 -> Try(Declarations.TypeDeclared, [Unnamed])
type_declared = |file, at| {
	nodes = file.nodes
	node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
	name_node = Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.first_kid(node))
	name = Tree.attribute(name_node, "name")
	if name == "" {
		return Err(Unnamed)
	}
	declared = {
		path: file.path,
		place: at,
		line: node.line,
		name,
		owner: owner_of(nodes, at),
		underlying: "",
		shape: "",
		is_nominal: Bool.False,
		is_tag_union: Bool.False,
		is_function_type: Bool.False,
	}
	match node.kids.get(1) {
		Ok(built_at) => {
			built_on = Tree.node_at(nodes, built_at)
			if built_on.kind == "associated" {
				Ok(declared)
			} else {
				name_line = Text.line_at(file.source_lines, name_node.end_line)
				after_name = Text.bytes_of(name_line, { start: name_node.end_column - 1, count: 4 })
				Ok({
					..declared,
					underlying: Tree.written_type(nodes, built_at),
					shape: Tree.shape(nodes, built_at),
					is_nominal: after_name.contains(":=") or after_name.contains("::"),
					is_tag_union: built_on.kind == "ty-tag-union",
					is_function_type: built_on.kind == "ty-fn",
				})
			}
		}
		Err(_) => Ok(declared)
	}
}

cookbook/roc/lib/Finding.roc, 42 lines

## A finding of one of a recipe's checks: the file, the line, the check and
## what is wrong there, ordered as the Shale originals sorted their reports
## and printed as their lines.
import Text

Finding := {
	path : Str,
	line : U64,
	check : Str,
	what : Str,
}.{

	## By path, then line, then what is said, each path and saying bytewise.
	order : Finding, Finding -> [Before, Same, After]
	order = |first, second|
		match Text.byte_order(first.path, second.path) {
			Same =>
				if first.line < second.line {
					Before
				} else if first.line > second.line {
					After
				} else {
					Text.byte_order(first.what, second.what)
				}
			other => other
		}

	## The finding as its line: `path:line: check: what`.
	line_of : Finding -> Str
	line_of = |finding| {
		place = "${finding.path}:${finding.line.to_str()}"
		"${place}: ${finding.check}: ${finding.what}"
	}

	## How many of the findings each check made, in the order of `checks`, as
	## a summary counts them: `family 2, twin_name 0`.
	counts_of : List(Finding), List(Str) -> Str
	counts_of = |findings, checks| {
		count_of = |check| findings.count_if(|finding| finding.check == check).to_str()
		Str.join_with(checks.map(|check| "${check} ${count_of(check)}"), ", ")
	}
}

cookbook/roc/lib/Forest.roc, 124 lines

## Every parsed file's tree joined into one list of nodes, as the Shale
## originals of check_errors and check_boundaries join them: each node's
## `parent` and `kids` are places in the joined list, counted from 1, a
## file's root's parent 0, and each node keeps its file's path. Nodes are in source order, each before its kids, so a
## subtree runs from its root to its last descendant, and a node with no line
## of its own takes the next line in the list, across a file's end.
import Tree

Forest := {
	nodes : List(Tree.Node),
	paths : List(Str),
}.{

	## The files' trees joined, in the files' order.
	join : List({ path : Str, nodes : List(Tree.Node) }) -> Forest
	join = |files| {
		var $nodes = []
		var $paths = []
		for file in files {
			offset = $nodes.len()
			for file_node in file.nodes {
				moved_parent = if file_node.parent > 0 {
					file_node.parent + offset
				} else {
					0
				}
				moved = { ..file_node, kids: file_node.kids.map(|kid_at| kid_at + offset), parent: moved_parent }
				$nodes = $nodes.append(moved)
				$paths = $paths.append(file.path)
			}
		}
		{ nodes: $nodes, paths: $paths }
	}

	## How many nodes there are.
	count : Forest -> U64
	count = |forest| forest.nodes.len()

	## The node at a place.
	node : Forest, U64 -> Tree.Node
	node = |forest, at| Tree.node_at(forest.nodes, at)

	## The path of the file the node at a place is in.
	path : Forest, U64 -> Str
	path = |forest, at|
		match forest.paths.get(at - 1) {
			Ok(found) => found
			Err(_) => crash "Forest.path: no node ${at.to_str()}"
		}

	kind : Forest, U64 -> Str
	kind = |forest, at| Forest.node(forest, at).kind

	kids : Forest, U64 -> List(U64)
	kids = |forest, at| Forest.node(forest, at).kids

	parent : Forest, U64 -> U64
	parent = |forest, at| Forest.node(forest, at).parent

	## A node's attribute, `""` where it has none.
	attribute : Forest, U64, Str -> Str
	attribute = |forest, at, attribute_name| Tree.attribute(Forest.node(forest, at), attribute_name)

	name : Forest, U64 -> Str
	name = |forest, at| Forest.attribute(forest, at, "name")

	raw : Forest, U64 -> Str
	raw = |forest, at| Forest.attribute(forest, at, "raw")

	## The place of a node's kid, the kids counted from 1, 0 when it has no
	## such kid.
	kid : Forest, U64, U64 -> U64
	kid = |forest, at, number| Forest.kids(forest, at).get(number - 1) ?? 0

	## The kind of the node at a place, `""` for place 0, no node.
	kind_or_none : Forest, U64 -> Str
	kind_or_none = |forest, at|
		if at == 0 {
			""
		} else {
			Forest.kind(forest, at)
		}

	## The last node of the subtree at a place.
	last_descendant : Forest, U64 -> U64
	last_descendant = |forest, at| {
		var $last = at
		while !(Forest.kids(forest, $last).is_empty()) {
			$last = Forest.kids(forest, $last).last() ?? $last
		}
		$last
	}

	## The line a node is reported at: its own, else the next node's that has
	## one, 0 when no node after it has one (a finding prints that as `?`).
	line_number : Forest, U64 -> U64
	line_number = |forest, at| {
		var $place = at
		while $place <= Forest.count(forest) and Forest.node(forest, $place).line == 0 {
			$place = $place + 1
		}
		if $place <= Forest.count(forest) {
			Forest.node(forest, $place).line
		} else {
			0
		}
	}

	## Each tag of the tag union at a place, as a whole node (`Some(U64)`).
	union_tags : Forest, U64 -> List(U64)
	union_tags = |forest, at|
		Forest.kids(forest, at)
			.keep_if(|tags| Forest.kind(forest, tags) == "tags")
			.join_map(|tags| Forest.kids(forest, tags))

	## The name of a tag node: `Some` for `Some(U64)`.
	tag_name : Forest, U64 -> Str
	tag_name = |forest, at|
		if Forest.kind(forest, at) == "ty-apply" {
			Forest.name(forest, Forest.kid(forest, at, 1))
		} else {
			Forest.name(forest, at)
		}
}

cookbook/roc/lib/Groups.roc, 472 lines

## Roc's bracket groups read from a file's lines, for check_stacking and
## wrap_long_lines (ported from the Shale groups.shale): each pair of
## brackets or a lambda's `|...|`, where it opens and closes, its items counted by the
## commas at its own depth and its tokens. A token is a name (a dotted path
## like `Angle.Bearing` is one), a number, a string or a character;
## punctuation and operators are none. The rule the groups are judged by is
## Stacking's. A place in a line is counted from 1 and in bytes, as Shale's
## `sub` counts, so a line's width is its bytes with a tab counting four.
import Bytes

Groups := [].{

	## A group of the lines read: the line and column it opens at, the line
	## and column it closes at, its items, its tokens, whether a comment or a
	## `\\` string lies inside it (`fixed`), whether its last item ends in a
	## comma (`trailing`), how many groups are open around it, the group
	## around it and whether it is a function type's arguments, `(A, B -> C)`,
	## which can't take a trailing comma.
	Group : {
		line : U64,
		open : U64,
		close_line : U64,
		close : U64,
		items : U64,
		tokens : U64,
		fixed : Bool,
		trailing : Bool,
		depth : U64,
		parent : Groups.Parent,
		fn_type : Bool,
	}

	## The group around a group: the byte that closes it (0 for none), the
	## line it opens on (0 for none) and whether its last item ends in a
	## comma, which is known once it closes.
	Parent : {
		closer : U8,
		line : U64,
		trailing : Bool,
	}

	## The byte that closes a group `byte` opens, or 0 when it opens none.
	closer_of : U8 -> U8
	closer_of = |byte|
		if byte == '(' {
			')'
		} else if byte == '{' {
			'}'
		} else if byte == '[' {
			']'
		} else {
			0
		}

	## Whether `byte` closes a pair of brackets.
	is_closer : U8 -> Bool
	is_closer = |byte| byte == ')' or byte == '}' or byte == ']'

	## The groups of `source_lines`, by where they close. A group that never
	## closes in them is left out.
	groups_in_lines : List(Str) -> List(Groups.Group)
	groups_in_lines = |source_lines| {
		var $scan = {
			open: [],
			closed: [],
			trailing_by_id: [],
			tokens: 0,
			fixed: 0,
			last_code: 0,
		}
		$number : U64
		var $number = 0
		for text in source_lines {
			$number = $number + 1
			$scan = scanned_line($scan, { bytes: text.to_utf8(), number: $number })
		}
		trailing_by_id = $scan.trailing_by_id
		$scan.closed.map(
			|(group, parent_id)|
				if parent_id == 0 {
					group
				} else {
					parent = group.parent
					{
						..group,
						parent: {
							..parent,
							trailing: trailing_by_id.get(parent_id - 1) ?? Bool.False,
						},
					}
				},
		)
	}

	## The groups that open and close on one line.
	groups_on_line : Str -> List(Groups.Group)
	groups_on_line = |text| Groups.groups_in_lines([text])

}

## A group still open: where it opened, the byte that closes it, its commas
## so far and the place of the last one, whether an arrow stands at its own
## depth, whether it is a `where` clause's brackets, and the running counts
## when it opened.
Opened : {
	id : U64,
	line : U64,
	at : U64,
	closer : U8,
	commas : U64,
	last : U64,
	has_arrow : Bool,
	is_where : Bool,
	tokens_before : U64,
	fixed_before : U64,
}

## The scan so far: the groups open (innermost last), those closed with the
## id of the group around each (0 for none), each group's `trailing` by its
## id once it closes, the running counts of tokens and of comments and `\\`
## strings, and the last byte of code seen (0 for none).
Scan : {
	open : List(Opened),
	closed : List((Groups.Group, U64)),
	trailing_by_id : List(Bool),
	tokens : U64,
	fixed : U64,
	last_code : U8,
}

## The scan after one more line.
scanned_line : Scan, { bytes : List(U8), number : U64 } -> Scan
scanned_line = |before, source| {
	l = source.bytes
	line = source.number
	var $scan = before
	var $count = l.len()
	if Bytes.trimmed(l).starts_with(['\\', '\\']) {
		$scan = {
			..$scan,
			fixed: $scan.fixed + 1,
			tokens: $scan.tokens + 1,
			last_code: '\\',
		}
		$count = 0
	}
	$i : U64
	var $i = 1
	while $i <= $count {
		c = Bytes.byte_at(l, $i)
		var $code = c
		if c == ' ' {
			# A space only separates, and spaces are the most common byte.
			$code = ' '
		} else if Bytes.is_word_byte(c) {
			# A name right after a dot continues a path, as in `f(x).name`.
			continues = Bytes.byte_at(
				l,
				$i - 1,
			) == '.' and !($i >= 2 and Bytes.byte_at(l, $i - 2) == '.')
			if !(continues) {
				$scan = { ..$scan, tokens: $scan.tokens + 1 }
			}
			$i = path_end(l, $i) - 1
		} else if c == '"' or c == '\'' {
			$scan = { ..$scan, tokens: $scan.tokens + 1 }
			$i = $i + 1
			while $i <= $count and Bytes.byte_at(l, $i) != c {
				if Bytes.byte_at(l, $i) == '\\' {
					$i = $i + 1
				}
				$i = $i + 1
			}
		} else if c == '#' {
			$scan = { ..$scan, fixed: $scan.fixed + 1 }
			$code = ' '
			$count = 0
		} else if Groups.closer_of(c) != 0 {
			is_where = c == '[' and follows_where(l, $i)
			$scan = opened(
				$scan,
				{
					line,
					at: $i,
					closer: Groups.closer_of(c),
					is_where,
				},
			)
		} else if (c == '-' or c == '=') and Bytes.byte_at(
			l,
			$i + 1,
		) == '>' and Bytes.byte_at(l, $i - 1) == ' ' and !($scan.open.is_empty()) {
			$scan = with_top($scan, |group| { ..group, has_arrow: Bool.True })
			$i = $i + 1
		} else if c == '|' and Bytes.byte_at(
			l,
			$i + 1,
		) != '>' and Bytes.byte_at(l, $i + 1) != '|' and Bytes.byte_at(l, $i - 1) != '|' {
			if top_closer($scan.open) == '|' {
				$scan = closed($scan, { bytes: l, line, close: $i })
			} else {
				# A `|` opens a lambda only where an expression can start.
				b = Bytes.byte_before(l, $i)
				if b == 0 or b == '=' or b == '(' or b == ',' or b == '[' or b == '{' or b == ':' {
					$scan = opened(
						$scan,
						{
							line,
							at: $i,
							closer: '|',
							is_where: Bool.False,
						},
					)
				}
			}
		} else if Groups.is_closer(c) {
			# Pop down to the group this byte closes. A `|` that turned out to
			# be no lambda is dropped on the way.
			var $open = $scan.open
			while !($open.is_empty()) and top_closer($open) != c {
				$open = $open.drop_last(1)
			}
			$scan = { ..$scan, open: $open }
			if !($open.is_empty()) {
				$scan = closed($scan, { bytes: l, line, close: $i })
			}
		} else if c == ',' and !($scan.open.is_empty()) {
			rest = Bytes.rest_from(l, $i + 1)
			in_where = match $scan.open.last() {
				Ok(group) => group.is_where
				Err(_) => Bool.False
			}
			# In a `where` clause's brackets, only a comma before a method
			# constraint, or at its line's end, separates items.
			if !(in_where) or Bytes.trimmed(rest).is_empty() or starts_constraint(rest) {
				comma_at = $i
				$scan = with_top($scan, |group| with_comma(group, comma_at))
			}
		}
		if $code != ' ' and $code != '\t' {
			$scan = { ..$scan, last_code: $code }
		}
		$i = $i + 1
	}
	$scan
}

## The byte that closes the innermost of the open groups, or 0 for none.
top_closer : List(Opened) -> U8
top_closer = |open|
	match open.last() {
		Ok(group) => group.closer
		Err(_) => 0
	}

## An open group with one more comma, the last at `place`.
with_comma : Opened, U64 -> Opened
with_comma = |group, place| {
	..group,
	commas: group.commas + 1,
	last: place,
}

## The scan with a group opened.
opened : Scan,
{
	line : U64,
	at : U64,
	closer : U8,
	is_where : Bool,
} -> Scan
opened = |scan, place| {
	id = scan.trailing_by_id.len() + 1
	group = {
		id,
		line: place.line,
		at: place.at,
		closer: place.closer,
		commas: 0,
		last: place.at,
		has_arrow: Bool.False,
		is_where: place.is_where,
		tokens_before: scan.tokens,
		fixed_before: scan.fixed,
	}
	{
		..scan,
		open: scan.open.append(group),
		trailing_by_id: scan.trailing_by_id.append(Bool.False),
	}
}

## The scan with its innermost open group changed.
with_top : Scan, (Opened -> Opened) -> Scan
with_top = |scan, change|
	match scan.open.last() {
		Ok(group) => {
			..scan,
			open: scan.open.set(
				scan.open.len() - 1,
				change(group),
			) ?? crash "Groups: no open group to change",
		}
		Err(_) => scan
	}

## The scan with its innermost open group closed at column `close` of line
## `line`: its items counted from the commas at its own depth, a last item
## that is a rest pattern (`{ a, b, .. }`, `[x, .. as more]`) not counted.
closed : Scan,
{
	bytes : List(U8),
	line : U64,
	close : U64,
} -> Scan
closed = |scan, at|
	match scan.open.last() {
		Err(_) => scan
		Ok(g) => {
			l = at.bytes
			trailing = scan.last_code == ','
			var $items = if trailing {
				g.commas
			} else {
				g.commas + 1
			}
			if g.line == at.line {
				if Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.span(l, g.at + 1, at.close - 1)).is_empty() {
					$items = 0
				}
				last = Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.span(l, g.last + 1, at.close - 1))
				if !(trailing) and g.commas > 0 and (
					last == [
						'.',
						'.',
					] or last.starts_with(".. as ".to_utf8())
				) {
					$items = $items - 1
				}
			}
			depth = scan.open.len() - 1
			around = if depth > 0 {
				scan.open.get(depth - 1)
			} else {
				Err(OutOfBounds)
			}
			(parent, parent_id) = match around {
				Ok(outer) => (
					{
						closer: outer.closer,
						line: outer.line,
						trailing: Bool.False,
					},
					outer.id,
				)
				Err(_) => (
					{
						closer: 0,
						line: 0,
						trailing: Bool.False,
					},
					0,
				)
			}
			group = {
				line: g.line,
				open: g.at,
				close_line: at.line,
				close: at.close,
				items: $items,
				tokens: scan.tokens - g.tokens_before,
				fixed: scan.fixed > g.fixed_before,
				trailing,
				depth,
				parent,
				fn_type: g.has_arrow and g.closer == ')',
			}
			{
				..scan,
				open: scan.open.drop_last(1),
				closed: scan.closed.append((group, parent_id)),
				trailing_by_id: scan.trailing_by_id.set(
					g.id - 1,
					trailing,
				) ?? crash "Groups: a group with no id",
			}
		}
	}

## Where a name or a dotted path that starts at `place` ends, one past its last byte:
## `[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*`.
path_end : List(U8), U64 -> U64
path_end = |bytes, place| {
	var $end = place
	while Bytes.is_word_byte(Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end)) {
		$end = $end + 1
	}
	while Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end) == '.' and Bytes.is_word_byte(Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end + 1)) {
		$end = $end + 1
		while Bytes.is_word_byte(Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end)) {
			$end = $end + 1
		}
	}
	$end
}

## Whether the code before column `place` ends in the keyword `where`, so
## that a `[` there opens a `where` clause.
follows_where : List(U8), U64 -> Bool
follows_where = |bytes, place| {
	var $j = place - 1
	while $j > 0 and (Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $j) == ' ' or Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $j) == '\t') {
		$j = $j - 1
	}
	if $j < 5 or Bytes.span(bytes, $j - 4, $j) != "where".to_utf8() {
		Bool.False
	} else if $j == 5 {
		Bool.True
	} else {
		b = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $j - 5)
		b == ' ' or (b == '\t' and Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.span(bytes, 1, $j - 5)).is_empty())
	}
}

## Whether the bytes start a method constraint, `k.is_eq :`:
## `^ *[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\.[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!? *:`. In a `where` clause's
## brackets, only a comma followed by one, or ending its line, separates
## items.
starts_constraint : List(U8) -> Bool
starts_constraint = |bytes| {
	var $at = 1
	while Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $at) == ' ' {
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	match name_end(bytes, $at) {
		Err(_) => Bool.False
		Ok(after_type) =>
			if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, after_type) != '.' {
				Bool.False
			} else {
				match name_end(bytes, after_type + 1) {
					Err(_) => Bool.False
					Ok(after_method) => {
						var $end = after_method
						if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end) == '!' {
							$end = $end + 1
						}
						while Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end) == ' ' {
							$end = $end + 1
						}
						Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end) == ':'
					}
				}
			}
	}
}

## Where a lower name `[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` that starts at `place` ends, one
## past its last byte.
name_end : List(U8), U64 -> Try(U64, [NoName])
name_end = |bytes, place| {
	first = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, place)
	if (first >= 'a' and first <= 'z') or first == '_' {
		var $end = place + 1
		while Bytes.is_word_byte(Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end)) {
			$end = $end + 1
		}
		Ok($end)
	} else {
		Err(NoName)
	}
}

cookbook/roc/lib/Headers.roc, 130 lines

## What a Roc file's header says about who chooses its names: a name an app's platform asks for, a
## hook a platform hands its host and a method Roc calls by name were chosen
## somewhere else, so the recipes judge them differently from the names a
## program picks for itself; and which modules a package keeps to itself.
import Bytes
import Text
import Tree

Headers := [].{

	## The methods Roc calls by name, from Roc's docs/langref/static-dispatch.md
	## and operators.md, with the encoders' `encode` and `decode`: a module
	## that declares one has it because Roc asks, not as a name of its own.
	language_fixed_names : Set(Str)
	language_fixed_names = Set.from_list([
		"to_inspect",
		"is_eq",
		"to_hash",
		"plus",
		"minus",
		"times",
		"div_by",
		"div_trunc_by",
		"rem_by",
		"is_lt",
		"is_lte",
		"is_gt",
		"is_gte",
		"range_exclusive_to",
		"range_inclusive_to",
		"range_exclusive_from",
		"range_inclusive_from",
		"range_iter",
		"range_len_if_known",
		"negate",
		"not",
		"from_numeral",
		"from_quote",
		"from_interpolation",
		"iter",
		"next",
		"parser_for",
		"encoder_for",
		"map",
		"map!",
		"subscript",
		"encode",
		"decode",
	])

	## What a folder's `main.roc` exposes, from the file's text (reading the
	## file is the recipe's): `is_package` when its header is `package` or `platform`, and
	## the modules it exposes.
	exposed_by : Str -> { is_package : Bool, modules : List(Str) }
	exposed_by = |text| {
		code = code_of(text)
		word = Headers.header_word(code)
		if word == "package" {
			{ is_package: Bool.True, modules: bracketed_names(code) }
		} else if word == "platform" {
			listed = Text.between(code, "exposes", "]") ?? ""
			{ is_package: Bool.True, modules: bracketed_names("${listed}]") }
		} else {
			{ is_package: Bool.False, modules: [] }
		}
	}

	## The first word of a file's code, its comment lines left out: `app`,
	## `package`, `platform`, `module`, `hosted`, or for a type module the
	## type's name; `""` when it has none.
	header_word : Str -> Str
	header_word = |text| {
		bytes = code_of(text).to_utf8()
		is_word = |byte| Bytes.is_letter(byte) or byte == '_'
		match bytes.find_first_index(is_word) {
			Ok(start) => {
				after = bytes.drop_first(start)
				length = after.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_word(byte))) ?? after.len()
				Str.from_utf8_lossy(after.take_first(length))
			}
			Err(_) => ""
		}
	}

	## The value names a file's tree's header speaks for, in the tree's order:
	## `dictated`, what an app provides,
	## what a platform requires of its app and what it provides to its host;
	## `exposed`, what a `module` or `hosted` header exposes.
	header_names : List(Tree.Node) -> { dictated : List(Str), exposed : List(Str) }
	header_names = |nodes| {
		var $dictated = []
		var $exposed = []
		var $place = 2
		while $place <= nodes.len() and Tree.node_at(nodes, $place).kind != "statements" {
			node = Tree.node_at(nodes, $place)
			if node.kind == "entrypoint" {
				$dictated = $dictated.append(Tree.attribute(node, "value"))
			}
			if node.kind == "symbol-map-entry" {
				$dictated = $dictated.append(Tree.attribute(node, "func"))
			}
			if node.kind == "text" and node.parent > 0 {
				parent = Tree.node_at(nodes, node.parent)
				match Tree.find_attribute(node, "value") {
					Ok(value) if parent.kind == "exposed-lower-ident" =>
						if parent.parent > 0 and Tree.node_at(
							nodes,
							parent.parent,
						).kind == "provides" {
							$dictated = $dictated.append(value)
						} else {
							$exposed = $exposed.append(value)
						}
					_ => {}
				}
			}
			$place = $place + 1
		}
		{ dictated: $dictated, exposed: $exposed }
	}
}

## A file's text with its comment lines left out.
code_of : Str -> Str
code_of = |text| Str.join_with(Text.lines(text).drop_if(|line| Text.trim(line).starts_with("#")), "\n")

## The names in the list between the first `[` and the next `]` of `text`.
bracketed_names : Str -> List(Str)
bracketed_names = |text|
	(Text.between(text, "[", "]") ?? "").split_on(",").map(Text.trim).keep_if(|name| name != "")

cookbook/roc/lib/Imports.roc, 209 lines

## A Roc file's imports, read from Roc's own tree of it, and the ones the file
## never uses: find_unused_imports' rule, `unused_import`, in its one home
## (cookbook/roc/find_unused_imports.shale's header says what counts as a
## use). rewrite_method_calls asks it too, of a file before and after its
## rewrite, to name each import the rewrite left unused.
import Tree

Imports := [].{

	## An import line no name of the file uses: its line and how a finding
	## names it.
	UnusedImport : { line : U64, label : Str }

	## Each import of the file whose names it never uses, from its tree and
	## its source lines, which hold the qualifier of a pattern's tag that the
	## tree drops.
	unused_imports : List(Tree.Node), List(Str) -> List(Imports.UnusedImport)
	unused_imports = |nodes, source_lines| {
		used = heads_used(nodes, source_lines)
		imports_of(nodes)
			.drop_if(|line_import| line_import.names.any(|name| used.contains(name)))
			.map(|line_import| { line: line_import.line, label: line_import.label })
	}
}

## An import line: its line, how a finding names it, and the names a use of
## it may start with.
Import : {
	line : U64,
	label : Str,
	names : List(Str),
}

## The kids of a node, as nodes.
kid_nodes : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> List(Tree.Node)
kid_nodes = |nodes, node|
	node.kids.map(|at| Tree.node_at(nodes, at))

# ── The imports

## Each import of the file, in order: `import pkg.Mod`, its alias and what it
## exposes, and each file import, `import "page.html" as page : Str`.
imports_of : List(Tree.Node) -> List(Import)
imports_of = |nodes|
	nodes.join_map(
		|node|
			if node.kind == "s-import" {
				[module_import(nodes, node)]
			} else if node.kind == "s-file-import" {
				file_imports(nodes, node)
			} else {
				[]
			},
	)

## A module's import. Its name is the alias of `import pkg.Mod as M`, else
## the last part of the module's path; a name it exposes is one too.
module_import : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> Import
module_import = |nodes, node| {
	path = Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
	alias = Tree.attribute(node, "alias")
	name = if alias == "" {
		path.split_on(".").last() ?? path
	} else {
		alias
	}
	label = if alias == "" {
		"`${path}`"
	} else {
		"`${path}` as `${alias}`"
	}
	exposing_lists = kid_nodes(nodes, node).keep_if(|kid| kid.kind == "exposing")
	exposed = exposing_lists.join_map(|list| exposed_names(nodes, list))
	{
		line: node.line,
		label,
		names: exposed.prepend(name),
	}
}

## The names an `exposing [...]` list names: a type's `text`, and each
## value's name, held by the value's own kids.
exposed_names : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> List(Str)
exposed_names = |nodes, list|
	kid_nodes(nodes, list).join_map(
		|entry|
			if entry.kind == "exposed-upper-ident" {
				[Tree.attribute(entry, "text")]
			} else if entry.kind == "exposed-lower-ident" {
				kid_nodes(nodes, entry).map(|name| Tree.attribute(name, "value"))
			} else {
				[]
			},
	)

## A file import's name, used when the file refers to it.
file_imports : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node -> List(Import)
file_imports = |nodes, node|
	kid_nodes(nodes, node)
		.keep_if(|kid| kid.kind == "name")
		.map(
			|kid| {
				name = Tree.attribute(kid, "value")
				{
					line: node.line,
					label: "the file import `${name}`",
					names: [name],
				}
			},
		)

# ── The uses

## The first part of every value, tag and type name the file uses. A bare
## tag (`Other`, in an expression, a pattern or a tag union type) names no
## module, so only a qualified one counts, or one that is a nominal type's
## name (`Point.{ x: 0 }`). A platform header's `hosted { "sym": Host.f! }`
## entry uses its module.
heads_used : List(Tree.Node), List(Str) -> Set(Str)
heads_used = |nodes, source_lines| {
	union_tags = kids_of_kind(nodes, "tags")
	nominal_names = kids_of_kind(nodes, "mapper")
	names = nodes.map_with_index(
		|node, index| {
			at = index + 1
			if node.kind == "e-ident" {
				Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
			} else if node.kind == "e-tag" {
				tag_use(node, nominal_names.contains(at))
			} else if node.kind == "ty" and !(union_tags.contains(at)) {
				Tree.attribute(node, "name")
			} else if node.kind == "symbol-map-entry" {
				Tree.attribute(node, "module")
			} else if node.kind == "p-tag" {
				pattern_tag_use(node, source_lines)
			} else {
				""
			}
		},
	)
	Set.from_list(names.drop_if(Str.is_empty).map(head_of))
}

## An expression's tag, when it names a module: qualified, or a nominal
## type's name.
tag_use : Tree.Node, Bool -> Str
tag_use = |node, names_nominal| {
	raw = Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
	if raw.contains(".") or names_nominal {
		raw
	} else {
		""
	}
}

## A pattern's tag, when it is qualified. roc-ast drops a pattern tag's
## qualifier (`Color.Red =>` comes as `.Red`), so the tag is read from the
## source at the pattern's column.
pattern_tag_use : Tree.Node, List(Str) -> Str
pattern_tag_use = |node, source_lines| {
	raw = Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
	written = if raw.starts_with(".") {
		source_line = match source_lines.get(node.line - 1) {
			Ok(text) => text
			Err(_) => crash "find_unused_imports: a pattern's tag past the file's end"
		}
		written_name(source_line.to_utf8().drop_first(node.column - 1))
	} else {
		raw
	}
	if written.contains(".") {
		written
	} else {
		""
	}
}

## The dotted name the bytes start with: a letter or `_`, then letters,
## digits, `_` and `.`; `""` when they start with none.
written_name : List(U8) -> Str
written_name = |bytes|
	match bytes.first() {
		Ok(first) if is_letter(first) or first == '_' => {
			length = bytes.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_name_byte(byte))) ?? bytes.len()
			match Str.from_utf8(bytes.take_first(length)) {
				Ok(name) => name
				Err(_) => crash "find_unused_imports: a name of ASCII bytes is UTF-8"
			}
		}
		_ => ""
	}

is_letter : U8 -> Bool
is_letter = |byte|
	(byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or (byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z')

is_name_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_name_byte = |byte|
	is_letter(byte) or (byte >= '0' and byte <= '9') or byte == '_' or byte == '.'

## The first part of a dotted name: `Mod` of `Mod.Type.name`.
head_of : Str -> Str
head_of = |name|
	name.split_on(".").first() ?? name

## The places of the nodes that are kids of a node of the kind.
kids_of_kind : List(Tree.Node), Str -> Set(U64)
kids_of_kind = |nodes, kind|
	Set.from_list(nodes.keep_if(|node| node.kind == kind).join_map(|node| node.kids))

cookbook/roc/lib/Packed.roc, 277 lines

## The groups that stay packed whatever the stacking rule says, as the Shale
## groups.shale read them: a row of literals, read at a glance,
## and numeric data, such as a polygon's points. A number is a literal or a
## negative written `(0.0 - 0.5)`; a flat number record is a record of
## numbers, `{ x: 0.5, y: (0.0 - 0.25) }`; and a number list is a list of two
## or more numbers or flat number records. The original's regular
## expressions are matched here by hand, a byte at a time, as a backtracker
## would match them.
import Bytes
import Groups

Packed := [].{

	## Whether a group on its line is a row of literals, read at a glance: a list,
	## or a tuple (a `(` not right after a name, `)` or `!`, so not a call's
	## arguments), whose items are all numbers, strings with nothing interpolated,
	## characters or bare tags, on a line within `width`.
	is_literal_row : { bytes : List(U8), group : Groups.Group }, U64 -> Bool
	is_literal_row = |at, width| {
		bytes = at.bytes
		group = at.group
		if bytes.len() > width or Bytes.width_of(bytes) > width {
			return Bool.False
		}
		opening = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, group.open)
		if opening == '(' {
			b = Bytes.byte_before(bytes, group.open)
			if group.open > 1 and Bytes.byte_at(
				bytes,
				group.open - 1,
			) != ' ' and (Bytes.is_word_byte(b) or b == ')' or b == '!') {
				return Bool.False
			}
		} else if opening != '[' {
			return Bool.False
		}
		inside = Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.span(bytes, group.open + 1, group.close - 1))
		pieces_of(inside, ',').all(
			|piece| {
				item = Bytes.trimmed(piece)
				item.is_empty() or is_literal_item(item)
			},
		)
	}

	## Whether the bytes hold a number list.
	holds_number_list : List(U8) -> Bool
	holds_number_list = |bytes| {
		zeroed = numbers_as_zero(bytes)
		var $at = 1
		while $at <= zeroed.len() {
			if Bytes.byte_at(zeroed, $at) == '[' and number_list_end(zeroed, $at) != Err(NoMatch) {
				return Bool.True
			}
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		Bool.False
	}

	## Whether a group on its line is numeric data: a number list, or a flat
	## number record on a line that holds a number list, as a point among a
	## polygon's points is.
	is_number_data : List(U8), Groups.Group -> Bool
	is_number_data = |bytes, group| {
		text = numbers_as_zero(Bytes.span(bytes, group.open, group.close))
		if number_list_end(text, 1) == Ok(text.len() + 1) {
			Bool.True
		} else {
			text == ['0'] and Packed.holds_number_list(bytes)
		}
	}
}

## The bytes split at each `separator`, as Shale's `split`: an empty text is
## one empty piece.
pieces_of : List(U8), U8 -> List(List(U8))
pieces_of = |bytes, separator| {
	var $pieces = []
	var $piece = []
	for byte in bytes {
		if byte == separator {
			$pieces = $pieces.append($piece)
			$piece = []
		} else {
			$piece = $piece.append(byte)
		}
	}
	$pieces.append($piece)
}

## Whether an item is a literal: `-?[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*`, `"[^"\\$]*"`,
## `'[^']+'` or a bare tag `[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*`.
is_literal_item : List(U8) -> Bool
is_literal_item = |item| {
	count = item.len()
	first = Bytes.byte_at(item, 1)
	last = Bytes.byte_at(item, count)
	middle = Bytes.span(item, 2, count - 1)
	if number_end(item, 1) == Ok(count + 1) {
		Bool.True
	} else if first == '"' {
		is_kept_out = |byte| byte == '"' or byte == '\\' or byte == '$'
		count >= 2 and last == '"' and !(middle.any(is_kept_out))
	} else if first == '\'' {
		count >= 3 and last == '\'' and !(middle.contains('\''))
	} else {
		is_tag_byte = |byte| Bytes.is_letter(byte) or Bytes.is_digit(byte)
		first >= 'A' and first <= 'Z' and item.drop_first(1).all(is_tag_byte)
	}
}

## Whether a byte may follow a number's first digit: `[0-9A-Za-z_.]`.
is_number_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_number_byte = |byte| Bytes.is_word_byte(byte) or byte == '.'

## Where a number `-?[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*` at `place` ends, one past it.
number_end : List(U8), U64 -> Try(U64, [NoMatch])
number_end = |bytes, place| {
	start = if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, place) == '-' {
		place + 1
	} else {
		place
	}
	unsigned_end(bytes, start)
}

## Where a number with no sign, `[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*`, at `place` ends.
unsigned_end : List(U8), U64 -> Try(U64, [NoMatch])
unsigned_end = |bytes, place|
	if Bytes.is_digit(Bytes.byte_at(bytes, place)) {
		var $end = place + 1
		while is_number_byte(Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end)) {
			$end = $end + 1
		}
		Ok($end)
	} else {
		Err(NoMatch)
	}

## Where a negative written `(0.0 - 0.5)` at `place` ends:
## `\(-?[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]* - [0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.]*\)`.
negative_end : List(U8), U64 -> Try(U64, [NoMatch])
negative_end = |bytes, place| {
	if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, place) != '(' {
		return Err(NoMatch)
	}
	first = number_end(bytes, place + 1)?
	if Bytes.span(bytes, first, first + 2) != [' ', '-', ' '] {
		return Err(NoMatch)
	}
	second = unsigned_end(bytes, first + 3)?
	if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, second) == ')' {
		Ok(second + 1)
	} else {
		Err(NoMatch)
	}
}

## Where a field and its number, `[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*: *-?[0-9]...`, at
## `place` end.
number_field_end : List(U8), U64 -> Try(U64, [NoMatch])
number_field_end = |bytes, place| {
	first = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, place)
	if !(Bytes.starts_lower_name(first)) {
		return Err(NoMatch)
	}
	end = Bytes.word_end(bytes, place + 1)
	if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, end) != ':' {
		return Err(NoMatch)
	}
